items.title: Told the Answer Is Not Taught to Reason: What On-Policy Self-Distillation From Privileged Context Transfers to a Language Model, Why Its Gains and Losses Divide Along Whether the Student Can Ever Hold What the Teacher Was Told, and the Controls That Would Separate Three Signals Under One Loss
items.abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. Life of Research On-policy self-distillation trains a language model on its own samples against the token distribution of the same model shown something the student never sees: a reference solution, a final answer, execution feedback or a demonstration. Early 2026 reports credited the recipe with matching reinforcement learning at a fraction of the sampling cost. Later 2026 studies report the opposite on thinking models: accuracy falls by up to 17 percent relative on competition mathematics, by up to 40 percent in another study, and agents trained this way can end below their untrained base. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that the disagreement is not about the method but about three signals that one loss carries at once. A mode signal comes from the teacher's prompt format and reasoning mode; a behaviour signal comes from the confidence, brevity and absence of checking that knowing the answer licenses; an information signal comes from the content of what the teacher was told. On mathematics with students trained in non-thinking mode, ablations that shuffle or delete the privileged content show that the reported gain does not come from that content, and that the gain measured in the student's own non-thinking mode is largely the mode signal. Marker counts and per-token loss attributions show that much of the reported harm is the behaviour signal. The paper argues, using the imitation-gap results from robot and control learning, that the behaviour signal is safe to transfer only when the student can come to hold the information - in its weights, because the information recurs across instances, or in its own context before the step that needs it. Per-problem answers to unseen problems meet neither condition. The paper consolidates 34 published values in a table and a figure, states a reading procedure, sorts 17 published repairs by the signal each removes, and names six measurements that would settle what remains open.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: TileQuant: Tile as the Precision-Allocation Unit for LLM Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization
items.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces large language model (LLM) deployment costs, but preserving quality requires accounting for uneven weight sensitivity. Uniform PTQ uses one weight bit-width, importance-aware PTQ adjusts scales or reconstructs weights within that width, and column-wise mixed precision retains selected columns at higher precision. However, sensitivity varies within columns, so whole-column retention also protects less sensitive weights, while runtime outlier detection adds decoding overhead. We therefore introduce TileQuant, a training-free framework that assigns precision to hardware-aligned 2D weight tiles. Offline calibration provides input-activation-aware scoring from forward statistics for lower calibration cost and gradient-informed scoring from loss sensitivity for stronger quality preservation. Within each projection's retention budget, the highest-scoring tiles remain at 16-bit and the rest use 8-bit. The resulting map guides reconstruction into compact weight buffers, which the kernel reuses for native integer and 16-bit computation with local accumulation to reduce memory traffic. Experiments show that TileQuant reaches 2.66x the original model's generation throughput. Across language modeling, reasoning, long-context retrieval, and question answering, it preserves quality and surpasses quantized and original models on multiple tasks. These results support selecting precision units that capture local sensitivity while enabling efficient hardware execution. The implementation is: https://github.com/HanzhiZhang-Ulrica/TileQuant

items.title: Three tiers of indeterminacy: the exact hull at small places and the container of Step (v) of IUT IV
items.abstract: In Step (v) of the proof of inter-universal Teichmüller theory (IUT) IV, Theorem 1.10, the holomorphic hull of the union of the possible images of the Θ-pilot object is bounded by a container that contains the region pλ·(RI)∼; the indeterminacies (Ind1) and (Ind2) are accounted for by the arbitrary automorphisms φ of IUT IV, Proposition 1.2, and (Ind3) by taking upper bounds. At places that are small in the sense of Proposition 1.2(iii) (p odd and every ramification index at most p − 2), this note compares the container with the hulls reached by four classes of maps: unit scalars and field automorphisms; the maps induced factor by factor by the actual (Ind1) and (Ind2); all factorwise automorphisms of the log-shells; and all automorphisms φ of Proposition 1.2. For the last two classes the hull is exactly p⌈λ⌉−𝔡I·(RI)∼, where 𝔡I is the sum of the orders of the differents, whereas the container of Step (v) has hull p⌊λ⌋−𝔡I·(RI)∼. So when λ is not an integer, which is always the case at bad places, the container is larger than anything these automorphisms reach by exactly a factor p (log p in log-volume). The difference comes from the proof of Proposition 1.2(ii), which uses Proposition 1.1 with the different of every factor; Proposition 1.1 applied to the factor that carries pλ removes it. Unit scalars and field automorphisms do not enlarge the hull; the actual (Ind1), (Ind2) reach the exact value when λ is an integer, provided that automorphisms of the local Galois groups carry a unit to the boundary of the log-shell, which at small places reduces to one condition on the transvections of Hoshi–Nishio and Kondo. The difference is a term of conductor type and does not change the shape of the inequality of IUT IV. An example at a bad place of an explicit initial Θ-datum is computed. The note credits the earlier statements it builds on: IUT IV, Proposition 1.1, is stated with a free choice of the factor that does not pay its different; Dupuy and Hilado choose the factor that makes the inclusion tightest (arXiv:2004.13108); the public repository lana-agents/iut of Project LANA states that for λ = 0 the hull is exactly the container of IUT IV; Mochizuki states that automorphisms of the log-shells give only bounded discrepancies. It is the local, numerical counterpart of the author's note Where Theorem 3.11 sits, whose Theorem 22 uses only an upper bound for the same quantity. No claim is made about the truth of Corollary 3.12 of IUT III or of the abc conjecture. The proofs are on paper and the computations are exact; versions of the statements about the actual indeterminacies were also checked in Lean 4 in a development of the author that is not part of this deposit, and the proofs do not rely on it. The comparison studied here arose in the author's discussions with generative AI tools, and the author decided to make it the subject of this note. The proofs were found with generative AI tools (large language models) under the author's direction, and these tools were also used for the computations, the formalization, the literature search and the writing. The author's own reading of the proofs is still in progress. The author takes full responsibility for the note. The deposit contains the note and an archive of the folder three-tiers/ (LaTeX source, Python scripts and their outputs), made from tag v0.25.0 of github.com/turahigashi/iut-explicit-initial-theta.

items.title: Silane coupling agent for semiconductor manufacturing
items.abstract: Silane coupling agents (SCAs) have evolved from conventional adhesion promoters into multifunctional interfacial materials essential for semiconductor packaging reliability. As device miniaturization, heterogeneous integration, and advanced packaging technologies intensify interfacial challenges, SCAs increasingly contribute to moisture resistance, stress mitigation, electrical performance, and thermal stability. This review examines six decades of SCA development, from composite reinforcement to applications in 2.5D/3D integration, fan‐out packaging, and high‐frequency electronics. Interfacial bonding mechanisms, deposition methods, characterization techniques, and reliability considerations are systematically discussed within front‐end‐of‐line (FEOL) and back‐end‐of‐line (BEOL) processes. Conventional organosilanes, including APTES and GLYMO, are compared with emerging alternatives such as dipodal silanes, cyclic azasilanes, phosphonic acids, imidazole‐based primers, and self‐healing and bio‐derived silanes. Key scientific debates concerning interphase architecture, molecular chain length, hydrolytic stability, and amine orientation are critically evaluated. Advances in vapor‐phase deposition, molecular layer deposition, molecular dynamics simulations, and machine learning are highlighted, particularly emerging relationships between amine protonation states and highly accelerated stress test (HAST) reliability. Remaining challenges include high‐frequency dielectric compatibility and discrepancies between laboratory measurements and actual packaging conditions. Future advances will require precise molecular‐level engineering of interfacial architectures rather than developing generic coupling agents to satisfy increasingly demanding semiconductor reliability requirements.

items.title: SILICON VERSUS CARBON The Great Computational Confrontation Between Artificial Intelligence and the Human Brain A Comprehensive Scientific Treatise on the Architecture, Efficiency, and Future of Intelligence
items.abstract: "SILICON VERSUS CARBON" dissects the computational confrontation between artificial intelligence and the human brain, revealing a fundamental efficiency chasm. While AI systems consume megawatts across sprawling data centers, the brain operates on merely 20 watts. The true miracle lies at the operational level: biological synapses cost approximately one femtojoule (10^-15 J) per operation, while modern GPUs consume roughly one nanojoule (10^-9 J)—a million-fold efficiency gap that no amount of Moore's Law scaling can bridge. The treatise dismantles the "brute force" paradigm through three critical arguments. First, it exposes the Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture as a crude digital approximation of biological sparsity, lacking the analog, asynchronous efficiency of ion-channel activation. Second, it invokes Integrated Information Theory (IIT) and the Phi (Φ) measure to demonstrate that current von Neumann architectures exhibit near-zero integrated information due to their modular, feed-forward design, suggesting true consciousness requires the dense, recurrent connectivity unique to carbon-based brains. Third, it positions neuromorphic computing—merging memory and processing on unified chips—as the only viable path toward twenty-watt efficiency. The verdict is absolute: silicon simulates intelligence through astronomical energy consumption; carbon embodies it through thermodynamic elegance. The future of computing lies not in scaling brute force, but in bio-inspired architectures that honor the physics of biological computation.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Project Proteus: One Nitride, Three Forms, Three Puzzles
items.abstract: Project Proteus follows the Angelica series onto the nitrides. Near lattice match to GaN, one wurtzite ScₓAl₁₋ₓN layer can be a transistor barrier, a ferroelectric switch and a piezoelectric resonator, and each form hides a disagreement in the literature. On the Angelica GaN-on-Si foundation, the paper computes everything that can be computed before a wafer is needed, and ends with five test vehicles for what computation cannot settle. Every result is tagged IMPLEMENTABLE, TESTABLE or CONCEPT. Puzzle 1, the matched composition: laboratories report 0.09, 0.11 and 0.14; 0.18 is the theoretical value. No common match with composition-scale errors of 7–10 % reconciles the three measurements (χ² = 13.8, 2 degrees of freedom).Puzzle 2, the missing mobility: with Angelica's calibrated scattering model, two laboratories' ScAlN HEMTs need an extra scattering channel of about 641–658 cm²/Vs. ScAlN buys current (5.7–8.1 A/mm, 2.5–3.5× AlGaN), not speed.Puzzle 3, two ferroelectrics: sputtered films switch at 4–5.5 MV/cm, epitaxial films near match at 0.65–1.2 MV/cm. In a HEMT gate stack, 2DEG screening and interlayer breakdown let only about 27–45 % (epitaxial) and 2.5 % (sputtered) of the polarization switch, enough for the reported 1–2 V windows.Form 3: a 39 GHz (n260) resonator needs x ≥ 0.175 under an optimistic bandwidth rule and x ≈ 0.30 under a conservative one, so the matched barrier composition is at best marginal for it.On silicon, heat, not current, caps power (4.0 vs 8.8 W/mm on SiC for +175 K); the RF loss of the stack depends on whether a parasitic layer forms at the silicon surface, not on the oxide thickness. Formal paper in English (authoritative), Traditional Chinese and Japanese; primers for middle-school readers in the same three languages; full code and sources. Not peer-reviewed. Defensive publication. Text CC BY 4.0, code Apache 2.0.

items.title: Prognostic Prediction After Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage: Conventional Models, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Large Language Models—A Structured Critical Review
items.abstract: This review aims to critically evaluate prognostic prediction models for mortality and functional outcomes in adults with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), including conventional clinical scores and statistical models, machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and large language models (LLMs). The review addresses three core questions: (1) fairness of model comparisons, including differences in patient populations, predictor availability, prediction timing, and outcome definitions; (2) model stability and reproducibility, including internal, temporal, and external validation, repeated inference, prompt sensitivity, and model version effects; and (3) clinical utility, including calibration, decision thresholds, decision-curve analysis, net benefit, and potential biases related to treatment limitations. Structured literature searches have been conducted in PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science. Title and abstract screening will be conducted by a primary reviewer, with independent verification of all proposed inclusions, uncertain records, and a random 20% sample of exclusions by a second reviewer. Full-text eligibility assessment will be conducted independently by two reviewers, with disagreements resolved through discussion or third-party adjudication. Data extraction will address study characteristics, prediction models, predictor timing, outcome definitions, performance metrics, validation strategies, and clinical applicability. Risk of bias and applicability will be assessed using PROBAST+AI where appropriate, supplemented by LLM-specific reproducibility considerations. At registration, database searching and preliminary deduplication have been conducted, and exploratory assessment of selected representative studies has been undertaken. Formal human eligibility screening, definitive study selection, and final evidence synthesis have not yet been completed. The review will primarily use a structured narrative synthesis rather than prespecifying a quantitative meta-analysis.

items.title: NodaPathlight: An Open-Source Mathematical Control Protocol for Programmable Optical Computing
items.abstract: NodaPathlight: An Open-Source Mathematical Control Protocol for Programmable Optical Computing Recent advances in experimental photonics suggest that the physical foundations may now exist for a different approach to computing, based on the predictable modification of material states by light. NodaPathlight explores how these experimentally established phenomena might be organized into a programmable computing architecture. The central proposition is that optical signals can induce controlled changes in a material's physical state. These changes can persist, providing memory, while the resulting material configuration determines how subsequent optical signals are transformed. By organizing these interactions through a mathematical control protocol, it may be possible to implement sequential computation using the material itself as both a storage and processing medium. Building on published research into optical phase-change memory, material-state logic and photonic signal processing, this white paper proposes a computational framework for implementing such an architecture. The accompanying open-source Python code investigates material-state transitions, optical propagation, signal routing, energy requirements, computational sequences and the conditions necessary for feedback-controlled operations. The work does not claim to demonstrate a functioning optical processor or introduce new physical laws. Although its underlying mechanisms have experimental precedents, their integration into the proposed architecture remains subject to important physical and engineering constraints. The contribution is therefore a mathematical and computational proposal, distinguishing established experimental evidence from conditional constructions and identifying the measurements required to evaluate its feasibility. The purpose of this publication is to make the proposed architecture and its computational implementation openly available for examination, reproduction, criticism and further development. The progress of experimental photonics makes this direction worth investigating. Whether these mechanisms can ultimately support a practical programmable optical computer remains an open question. This work is offered as an alternative approach for scientific exploration, experimental investigation and experimental collaboration.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Multi-agent generative AI ecosystems for cyber-physical systems in Industry 5.0
items.abstract: Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) are increasingly being implemented in critical industrial infrastructure, where complexity and interdependence are rising, posing significant cyber and operational risks. Traditional anomaly detection algorithms can be ineffective in capturing temporal dynamics, relational dependencies, and interpretable response requirements. The present paper proposes a multi-agent generative AI system to detect CPS anomalies and provide decision support by combining temporal feature encoding, relational modeling as graphs, supervised learning, and reasoning with an LLM. The architecture consists of detection, diagnosis, planning, governance, and human-in-the-loop validation agents. The framework is tested on the SWaT benchmark data. Findings indicate that the Autoencoder, LSTM, and 1D-CNN are more effective in terms of raw detection metrics, whereas the Random Forest provides more interpretable and agent-readable evidence to support the post-detection decision. Analysis of features and sensor family suggests the relevance of relational dependencies in characterizing anomalies. The multi-agent layer converts selected anomaly predictions into context-dependent explanations and governance-filtered recommendations to aid operator review, response planning, and process resilience. Overall, the framework supports transparent and human-supervised CPS anomaly management aligned with Industry 5.0 principles.

items.title: Medical AI Technology Gaps and Investment Priorities: Non-Contrast CT "Virtual Contrast" Synthesis, 3D Swin-UNETR ASIC Acceleration, and Clinical ROI Asymmetry (医療AI技術ギャップと投資優先順位:単純CT仮想造影「Virtual Contrast」・Swin-UNETR ASIC・ROI非対称性)
items.abstract: This monograph establishes a rigorous technical, thermodynamic, and capital-allocation framework evaluating the technology gaps and investment priorities in clinical medical AI, centering on three structural axes: (1) Non-Contrast CT to Contrast-Enhanced CT "Virtual Contrast" synthesis, (2) dedicated 3D Swin-UNETR ASIC hardware acceleration, and (3) structural Return on Investment (ROI) asymmetry across hospital reimbursement and liability regimes. While 3D shifted-window transformer architectures (Swin-UNETR) demonstrate high structural fidelity in volumetric feature extraction from routine non-contrast CT (NCCT) scans, executing high-resolution 3D window self-attention on general-purpose GPUs incurs severe memory-bandwidth bottlenecks and latency penalties in acute triage workflows. We formulate a deterministic custom ASIC dataflow architecture tailored for 3D Swin-UNETR volumetric patch partitioning, on-chip SRAM cyclic window shifting, and cryptographic zero-knowledge state verification (QFS-zkVM over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field F_p, p = 2^64 - 2^32 + 1) to eliminate stochastic hallucination risks in synthetic vascular enhancement. Furthermore, we quantify the clinical and economic ROI asymmetry between capital-intensive foundational model training and deterministic edge-ASIC deployment—accounting for contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) mitigation, iodinated contrast supply-chain volatility, radiology throughput gains, and statutory Human-in-Command (HIC) fiduciary liability boundaries. [概要(日本語)] 本論文(モノグラフ)は、医療AIにおける技術的ギャップと資本配分・投資優先順位について、①単純CTからの仮想造影(Virtual Contrast)生成技術、②3D Swin-UNETR専用ASICによるハードウェア・アクセラレーション、③臨床導入におけるROI(投資対効果)の非対称性という3つの構造軸から定量的・数理的に解明するものである。単純CT(NCCT)から造影CT相当の血行動態・病変コントラストを再構成する「Virtual Contrast」において、3次元Swin-UNETRアーキテクチャは高い空間特徴抽出能力を持つ一方、汎用GPU上での3D Shifted-Window Self-Attention演算は深刻なメモリ帯域ボトルネックと推論遅延を引き起こす。本研究では、3次元ボクセルパッチ分割とオンチップSRAM巡回ウィンドウシフトをハードウェアレベルで最適化したSwin-UNETR専用ASICアーキテクチャを設計するとともに、生成画像の確率的ハルシネーション(偽陽性・偽陰性造影効果)を排除するための決定論的暗号検証(64-bit Goldilocks素体 F_p 上のQFS-zkVMおよびHuman-in-Command [HIC] 統治原則)を統合する。さらに、造影剤腎症(CIN)リスクの回避、ヨード造影剤サプライチェーンの逼迫対策、読影スループット向上、および医療過誤責任(Caremark監視義務・製造物責任)の非対称性を踏まえた最適投資優先順位を導出する。 [License & Strict No-Learn Covenant] Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026). items.title: Leveraging artificial intelligence for livestock genetics and breeding
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming modern society including animal genetics and breeding which is essential for meeting global nutritional needs in supplying milk, meat, and eggs among the most complete sources of protein and micronutrients. Although animal breeding has a long history of using data-driven prediction methods, the application of modern AI approaches remains at a relatively early stage and shows substantial potential for wide-ranging applications in animal genetics and breeding. This study aims to review the current use of AI tools in livestock species across three major applications of high interest: AI-assisted phenotyping, AI-enabled dissection of complex-trait biology (focusing on AI-assisted GWAS and AI-for-omics), and AI-assisted genomic prediction. In addition, we discussed emerging methods and tools developed in human genetics that are not yet widely adopted in farm animals but may offer translational potential for future livestock studies. Looking ahead, AI breakthroughs in livestock genetics and breeding are likely to be driven by increases in data scale and resolution, enhanced computational capacities, standardized data infrastructure and benchmarking, and systematic method development and validation. From a livestock genetic improvement perspective, the key value of AI will lie in integrating AI-generated inputs, including improved phenotyping and biological insights, into practical breeding decisions through statistical modeling.
items.venue: Journal of Animal Science and Biotechnology/Journal of animal science and biotechnology

items.title: LAMMPS-CTIP-EChemDID: integrated CTIP and EChemDID packages for LAMMPS
items.abstract: An integrated and updated implementation of two LAMMPS packages: CTIP (Charge-Transfer Ionic Potential) and EChemDID (Electrochemical Dynamics with Implicit Degrees of Freedom). The integration enables simulations that combine electrochemical potential equilibration with dynamic charge transfer in metal oxide materials. The packages are adapted to the LAMMPS 22 Aug 2018 stable release and extended to simulate filament forming in ReRAM devices (TaOx/HfO2) under applied bias. The release contains the modified source files, example LAMMPS inputs for a forming simulation and the scripts used to generate the force-field coefficients. Original code is from CTIP (Kiran Sasikumar) and EChemDID (Onofrio and Strachan).
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: IF:CARGO: LLM-Based Semantic Compilation for Al-Native Rule Programming Games
items.abstract: This case study presents IF: CARGO, an experimental puzzle game that uses a large language model as a semantic compiler rather than an autonomous game-playing agent. Players author IF/THEN rules in natural language, which the model translates into a constrained command schema for deterministic validation and execution by the game engine. This architecture creates a playable loop of expression, execution, observation, and revision, framing AI interaction as semantic debugging. A mixed-methods playtest with 24 participants across eight levels examined player attempts, thinking time, perceived controllability, adjustability, and interpretations of the AI’s role. Results suggest that players generally understood the model as a translation intermediary and could revise their strategies through feedback, while periodic commands, multi-robot coordination, and rule-priority mechanics created greater cognitive and diagnostic demands. The study proposes a practical pattern for AI-native gameplay: constrain natural-language input, preserve player authorship, and ensure deterministic execution.
items.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Digital Entertainment

items.title: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb: AI Agents for Bomb Busters
items.abstract: Bomb Busters is a cooperative board game where players work together to defuse a bomb represented by 48 wires of 12 ranks. Wires are dealt to each player secretly, and are held in ascending order. Using only these constraints, and almost without any explicit communicative actions, players must deduce the ranks of wires held by other players. We present AI agents for the four player base version of the game that use a possible worlds model to represent other players' hands which is narrowed by observations made during game play to play the game near optimally, winning 9915 out of 10000 games. We also discuss the impact of different design decisions on the score of the game.
items.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Digital Entertainment

items.title: Governed Memory for AI Agents: a shared spine with a human merge gate, in production across four deployments
items.abstract: AI collapsed the cost of executing project work and, in doing so, moved the bottleneck to continuity of understanding: the one thing an agent cannot supply for itself, because every session begins amnesiac. Memory stores for agents now appear weekly. Few of them answer the question an organisation has to answer before it lets agents write into its memory: who is allowed to change what we believe, and how is a wrong change undone? We report on Architect, a system in daily production use since April 2026 that answers that question structurally rather than by policy. Its contributions, in order: (1) a lifecycle-gated write contract, in which agents may deposit freely into an append-only spine but may only propose changes of state, one human merges on one surface, and authority is recomputed at the moment of application rather than at the moment of grant; (2) a set of spine invariants that make governance operative instead of descriptive: supersede-not-delete with lineage, structural refusal of malformed or unauthorised writes, human-tethered recording authority for agent personas, and provenance stamped on every unit; (3) the matter-scoped memory substrate those invariants run on, where scope attaches before any prompt, the reachability boundary doubles as the data-sovereignty boundary, a reconciler round-trips records between markdown files and a database, and a third-party AI can connect over a standard protocol and complete the full loop. We present four deployments (a multi-matter central instance, a user-bound matter, a pooled multi-tenant box and a single-tenant box) as measured on 20 August 2026: a corpus of 9,784 units, of which 6,520 are lived rather than imported, and the system's audit of its own lineage, which found 62 supersessions predating a fix, 38 of them in the wrong direction, and reversed 11 by a judge under a confidence floor while holding the other 27 for a human. We close with the frontier (automatic contradiction surfacing, as-of-t query, unit-level promotion) and show, with numbers, why the merge gate itself is the scaling bottleneck and why the answer is graduated autonomy rather than faster human review.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Evaluating human-like chatbot interaction in customer service: integrating anthropomorphism and conversational capability
items.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI)-based technology has driven the development of rule-based chatbots into AI-based chatbots. This development is used by various companies to use AI chatbots as the frontline of customer service. Meeting user expectations for AI chatbots requires an evaluation model to measure chatbot quality. Based on the literature, chatbot evaluation models still focus solely on technical quality, even as AI chatbots are evolving towards human-like services. This research will explore the integration of the technical dimensions of information system success with a new dimension, namely Human-Like Chatbot Interaction (HLCI) as a higher-order construct of anthropomorphism and conversational capability. This quantitative study uses an explanatory research approach. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of users of the Veronika chatbot, owned by Telkomsel, an Indonesian telecommunications company. A total of 213 respondents had data ready for analysis using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method in SmartPLS 4, namely the measurement model and structural model tests. The analysis results show that service quality is not significantly related to user satisfaction but has a direct effect on trust. Meanwhile, information quality, system quality, and human-like chatbot interaction are positively related to trust and user satisfaction. Trust and user satisfaction are positively related to intention to continue using. The results of this study can contribute both theoretically and practically to modern AI chatbot quality evaluation models.

items.title: Enhanced Ferroelectric Performance of P(VDF-TrFE) Composites via MAPbI3-Mediated Crystallization for Flexible Memory Applications
items.abstract: We report a material-engineering strategy in which methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) perovskite is added to poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene) (P(VDF-TrFE)) composites to overcome intrinsic polarization and stability limitations. MAPbI3 incorporation enhances crystalline ordering and ferroelectric response in P(VDF-TrFE) composites, enhancing β-phase formation and strengthening dipole alignment through electrostatic interactions with -CF2- dipoles while simultaneously increasing dielectric permittivity and suppressing depolarization-field-driven polarization loss. With increasing MAPbI3 content, the composite films exhibit progressively improved ferroelectric performance and reach an optimum at 1.0 wt %, exhibiting a substantial increase in remanent polarization (2Pr from 13.7 to 18.4 μC/cm2), a 2.6-fold enhancement in the ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) on/off ratio, and a memory window expansion of 0.3 V. However, extremely high loadings and excessive MAPbI3 incorporation lead to aggregation and leakage-related degradation, resulting in reduced crystallinity and switching stability. Using P(VDF-TrFE) composites with optimized MAPbI3 composition, the composite FeFETs achieve extended retention up to 103 s, while the flexible ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) maintains stable ferroelectric switching after 10,000 mechanical bending cycles, demonstrating excellent mechanical resilience. These results demonstrate a practical material-engineering strategy for high-performance and mechanically reliable ferroelectric memory using a polymer-perovskite composite design.

items.title: Enforcing Narrative Reliability and Epistemic Pacing in LLM-Driven Detective Games via Structured Knowledge Trees
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) enable open-ended dialogue in interactive games, but their non-deterministic outputs make it difficult to preserve authorial control, factual consistency, and the intended sequence of information disclosure. These challenges are particularly significant in detective games, where premature revelation or fabricated details can undermine the logic of player progression. We present a Structured Knowledge Tree architecture coupled with a tri-agent LLM pipeline for controlling dialogue in an open-ended interrogation game. The system separates knowledge retrieval, dialogue generation, and response verification to ensure that the virtual suspect reveals only information permitted by the current narrative state. We evaluate the approach through The Interrogation of Adrian Gale, a playable detective-game testbed, and a formal user study examining hallucination reduction, adherence to authored disclosure sequences, and perceived logical progression. Our results demonstrate that the structured architecture reduces critical hallucinations by 64.78% and entirely prevents premature narrative disclosure. While the strict mechanical constraints introduced usability trade-offs regarding forced conversational reveals, the system successfully enforces rigorous epistemic pacing and provides players with a clear, subjective sense of progression toward solving the case.
items.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Digital Entertainment

items.title: DSLE: A Learning Environment for Dark Souls Boss Encounters
items.abstract: We introduce the Dark Souls Learning Environment (DSLE), a containerized platform that presents all 22 boss encounters of Dark Souls: Remastered as game-playing agent benchmarks through a Gymnasium-style interface. DSLE combines real-time combat, high-dimensional visual input, and sparse terminal rewards, with each environment step being a real action executed against the running game. To support controlled comparison, we define DSLE-5, a representative five-boss subset, spanning a melee fight, a spatially constrained arena, an environmental-hazard fight, a multi-target fight, and a fast final-boss fight, that we recommend as the starting suite for agents built on DSLE. On DSLE-5 we evaluate a random policy, an expert system, an evolutionary baseline, and PPO and DQN agents trained from visual input. The expert system and the evolutionary baseline each defeat the Asylum Demon, the game's tutorial boss (63% and 43% peak win rates), but none of the five methods defeats the other four DSLE-5 bosses; PPO and DQN show no measurable learning (at most 0.33% win rate on the tutorial boss, 0% elsewhere) within a budget that already costs tens of wall-clock hours per run. A broader study running the evolutionary baseline across all 22 encounters under advantaged all level-50 stats yields wins on only a handful of additional early-game bosses and leaves the rest unwon. The failure cases range from sub-10-second deaths in cramped, multi-target encounters to minute-long stalemates that inflict almost no damage, and we report them through survival time and damage dealt rather than win rate alone.

items.title: Cybercrime law and digital forensics: adapting legal frameworks for future technologies
items.abstract: Linked authenticity, integrity, reliability, attribution, jurisdiction, and privacy challenges are created by digital evidence from cloud platforms, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, artificial intelligence (AI), large language models (LLMs), biometrics, drones, blockchain, and virtual environments. This review synthesizes scholarly and authoritative sources on cybercrime law, digital forensics, and emerging technologies through a structured narrative review. The review reveals a technical–legal divide: it emphasizes investigative efficiency, while acquisition, hashing, metadata, chain of custody, tool validation, and automated-analysis reliability require clarification for evidentiary scrutiny. Technology, evidence source, forensic challenge, legal risk, admissibility requirement, and governance response are linked through the Technology–Forensic–Legal Admissibility (TFLA) Framework. Primary artifacts are distinguished from analytical outputs; technical weaknesses are translated into legal consequences and safeguards. Standards and evidentiary rules are complemented; TFLA is conceptual, not empirically validated. Technology-neutral, technically informed, rights-compliant governance is supported through transparent documentation, corroboration, human oversight, and institutional competence. Digital-forensic system design is linked to trustworthy technology governance.

items.title: Code and Data for Data-Driven Extraction of Multi-Exponential Thermal Kernels for Integrated Circuit Thermal Analysis
items.abstract: Code and data behind the paper "Data-Driven Extraction of Multi-Exponential Thermal Kernels for Integrated Circuit Thermal Analysis" by B. Ali, I. Bruce, C. L. Trinh, X. Jin, C. He, and D. Chen, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) Systems. The method extracts a compact three-component exponential kernel from steady-state 3D-ICE temperature maps and predicts the temperature rise by convolving the kernel with the power map. Even reflection across the die edges handles the adiabatic side faces. thermal_kernel_code.zip: MATLAB and Python code of the kernel extraction, the evaluation, and the analyses of the paper, the 3D-ICE input generator and run script, and the HotSpot bare-die adaptation with the comparison scripts. Its README.txt gives the script and settings behind the tables, the figures, and the numbers in the text of the paper. thermal_kernel_data.zip: the 88 steady-state 3D-ICE temperature maps of the paper with their floorplan and stack files (base floorplan, final test sets A and B, Floorplan B, two further cooling conditions, single-cell impulses), the fitted kernel, the HotSpot inputs and fields of the comparisons, the inner problems of the solver cross-check, and the values of the paper's tables as CSV files. Unzip both files into the same folder. The README.txt of each archive describes its contents. The kernel describes the thermal response of the simulated die stack and cooling condition from which it is extracted. A change in the package structure, the layer thicknesses or materials, or the cooling alters that response and requires a new extraction from maps of the new system. All maps in this record are simulated. Copyright (c) 2026 Iowa State University. Code: MIT License. Data: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International. The HotSpot material in the code archive keeps HotSpot's license (see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt).

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Software Testing: A Systematic Survey of Test Generation, Mutation Testing, and Flaky Test Management
items.abstract: Software testing consumes a large share of development effort, and its most labor-intensive tasks — writing test cases, judging whether outputs are correct, and keeping test suites reliable — are precisely the tasks where artificial intelligence has recently made the largest advances. This paper presents a systematic survey of artificial intelligence in software testing. It traces the field from classical and search-based test generation, through symbolic execution and fuzzing, to the present generation of large language model methods; it reviews how AI is used for automated test generation, assertion and oracle construction, mutation testing, flaky-test detection and management, and test prioritization and fault prediction; it examines the evidence for each family of techniques, including where empirical results are strong, where they are mixed, and where they rest on narrow benchmarks; and it analyzes the central challenges of the field — the oracle problem, evaluation validity, non-determinism, cost, and the risk of over-trusting generated tests. The survey concludes that AI has moved testing from a largely manual craft toward a semi-automated discipline, but that generated tests still require human review, measured adequacy criteria, and disciplined suite maintenance, and that the field's most valuable direction is the combination of learned models with classical, coverage-guided, and mutation-based methods rather than the replacement of one by the other.

items.title: An AI-Enabled Software Development Lifecycle with Governed Agent Execution
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) contributes to engineering, delivered behaviour and delegated execution. This paper proposes a software development lifecycle (SDLC) integrating people, AI agents and conventional automation. Three independent applicability questions—Assist, Embed and Operate (A/E/O)—distinguish participation from autonomy and maturity. Seven recurring activities connect tasks, verification and handoffs to accountable decisions. Three operational measures cover accepted-change elapsed time, review effort and delivery cost per accepted change alongside quality and safety guardrails. A purposive synthesis of 58 external source records informs fourteen core requirements, reproduced with verification notes in Appendices A–B. A SupportFlow sandbox demonstration exercises selected application controls using sample records and supplied AI-output fixtures; Appendix C identifies the evidence boundaries. Packaged-software adoption remains illustrative. Internal consistency checks and a prospective comparison with existing DevSecOps address different evaluation questions; comparative effectiveness remains untested. Conceptual research preprint, version 4.0. Not a peer-reviewed journal publication or an empirically validated standard. The paper includes Appendices A–C. Supporting materials provide the current criteria, source records and reproducible internal consistency checks. CC BY 4.0 applies to the paper; supporting-file rights are specified in LICENSES.md.

items.title: AKANE Architecture E2: Finding an LLM's mistakes from how its answers connect
items.abstract: Code, data, and results for small experiments in which a small language model (Gemma-2 2B) answers many true/false statements and writes its own consistency rules, some of them wrong. A network checks the model's answers against those rules while also doubting each rule, using belief propagation, and the signals are compared with the model's confidence and with counting rule violations.

items.title: A transformer-based explainable machine learning framework for heterogeneous ESG risk and return prediction using text intelligence
items.abstract: Corporate ESG disclosure has shifted toward narrative form, yet vendor ESG ratings that most empirical work depends on show substantial disagreement across providers, and encoders dominant in financial text analysis inherit a 512-token ceiling that discards most of a typical 10-K. HET-ESGFormer combines hierarchical long-document encoding, heterogeneity-aware sparse expert routing conditioned on industry sector and firm size, and a dual-channel explanation layer subject to faithfulness verification. The framework is evaluated on 3,182 U.S.-listed firms over 2015 to 2024 using 10-K filings, sustainability reports, earnings call transcripts, and ESG-tagged news. Against nine baselines spanning econometric, dictionary-based, contextual encoder, sparse-attention, and time-series approaches, HET-ESGFormer reduces return RMSE from 0.0417 to 0.0389 and QLIKE from 0.148 to 0.128, with Diebold-Mariano tests rejecting equal predictive accuracy against every baseline after correction for multiple comparisons. The text channel's marginal contribution to downside risk prediction is materially larger than its contribution to return prediction, widening at longer forecast horizons, indicating that ESG narratives carry more information about risk than about expected return. Ablations reveal a decoupling between predictive skill and explanation faithfulness: removing the consistency regularizer barely affects accuracy but sharply degrades explanation quality. The dual-channel explanation improves ERASER comprehensiveness by 50% over SHAP applied to XGBoost, and human raters significantly prefer the framework's rationales over SHAP-based rationales on trustworthiness. Decile-sorted long-short portfolios deliver a post-cost Sharpe ratio of 1.31 against 0.74 and 0.62 for portfolios built on Refinitiv and MSCI ratings, and pass VaR backtests at 95% coverage. The results support text-based ESG modeling as an alternative to vendor-rating-based approaches, particularly where downside risk management and traceable explanation are jointly required.

items.title: A Gold-Standard Study of What Makes a Lightweight Game-Playing Agent Strong
items.abstract: A reinforcement learning agent is only as strong as the opponents it trains against, and it is also hard to grade. It beats a random opponent over 99 percent of the time, and it only ties copies of itself. So we build a strong, fixed, rule-based expert for Gin Rummy and never train against it: no expert games, no demonstrations, no gradients. It does pick the shipped checkpoint, and we say where that matters. The expert beats every agent we trained 66 to 99 percent of the time. Across more than a hundred runs we ask what makes a small agent stronger, and five things help. They are trust-region updates, a well-aimed reward, a curriculum of tougher opponents, warm starting, and keeping the best checkpoint. Stacking them lifts a self-play champion from about 30 to about 34 percent against the expert. Several other ideas did not pay off. Reward shaping at two horizons, learned state embeddings, and DAgger imitation were each unhelpful, and a live large language model opponent was far too slow. Extra capacity does little to break the ceiling, across MLP, convolutional, set-based, attention and recurrent encoders. Handing the learner the opponent's hidden hand does not move it either. We add two standard baselines: neural fictitious self-play and information-set Monte Carlo search. We also reproduce the grading protocol on Leduc Hold'em, whose optimum is computable. The result is a small, fast recipe that never trains on the expert, plus a grading protocol that carries over to any game with a fixed reference. We report bootstrap intervals on the multi-seed comparisons and release the code.

items.title: A Controlled Benchmark of Edge AI Accelerators for Traffic Object Detection: scripts and results

items.title: Beyond Host-Side Control: HBM Controller Partitioning Across Host and HBM Base Dies
items.abstract: Recent generations of high bandwidth memory (HBM), such as HBM4, allow the base die of the memory stack to be manufactured using a logic process that can accommodate more complex controller functions next to the DRAM. We present the first systematic quantitative study of function-level controller placement between the host and the HBM4 base die on a silicon interposer. We divide the controller into its main functions and evaluate four placements, from a complete host controller to a complete base die controller, with intermediate placements that move maintenance or scheduling to the base die. We extend Ramulator 2 with HBM4 timing and maintenance, model a die-to-die (D2D) link with timing checks at the DRAM interface, and compose area, energy, and temperature from synthesized controller blocks, modeled storage, and interface data. A provisioned D2D link preserves per-stack bandwidth and adds about twice its one-way delay to unloaded latency. Maintenance moves to the base die with no bandwidth cost and frees host command slots, and the freed share grows with stack height. Replacing the wide interface with a D2D link saves 61% of host shoreline and 16.85 mm2 of host area per stack. The D2D link dominates the added base die area and power, and the base die runs cooler under streaming with link energy below 0.4 pJ/bit. Shared control delivers up to 1.72x the throughput of static partitioning between two requestors.

items.title: PENSA: A Spatial Accelerator for BitNet b1.58 Inference on an HBM-equipped AMD Alveo FPGA
items.abstract: Ternary large language models (tLLMs) replace general multiplication in dominant linear layers with sign-controlled accumulation, shifting hardware bottlenecks toward packed-weight delivery, reduction, and operator occupancy. PENSA is an end-to-end FPGA accelerator for the BitNet b1.58 2B4T model on an AMD Alveo U50. Two row-partitioned ternary matrix engines consume packed TQ1_0 weights from eight independent high-bandwidth memory (HBM) pseudo-channels, each processing 1,280 ternary weights per cycle through sign selection and integer reduction. The sequencer, attention, and vocabulary-projection units remain resident on the FPGA, while two-stream interleaved scheduling overlaps sequences across the persistent pipeline to form the Penta-Unit. At 104.1~MHz, PENSA achieves 58.09 tok/s at context 128 and 24.60 tok/s at context 2048, corresponding to 2.14-3.14$\times$ the throughput of a same-model Xeon E-2356G baseline. The resulting system demonstrates end-to-end FPGA execution of 2B-scale BitNet topology without modifying its model structure.

items.title: • Technical Specification of the Lotus Core-V3 Ultra: An Optimized 360-Qubit Superconducting QPU Utilizing Zero-Skew Multi-Die Interconnect Topology
items.abstract: This technical specification details the architectural parameters and hardware-level optimizations of the Lotus Core-V3 Ultra, a scalable superconducting quantum processing unit integrating 6 clusters of 12 physical transmon qubits each, yielding a total of 360 physical channels. Moving beyond the NISQ baseline, this multi-die chiplet network achieves permanent geometric zero-skew symmetry (theta = 0.00°), completely neutralizing signal propagation timing errors directly on the hardware plane and eliminating compiler-level software latency overhead. Inter-die capacitive and inductive crosstalk is suppressed to <= -68.5 dB via an atomic layer deposited (ALD) 25 nm Al2O3 insulation matrix paired with a 10 µm grounded shield net. Systematic mitigation of parasitic bus line capacitances drosselt the aggregate thermal dissipation under multi-channel full computational load by 43%, limiting the total cryogenic thermal load to 8.18 nW at a 10 mK stage to preserve maximum quantum coherence.

items.title: Ultra‐Robust All‐Weather Perovskite Memristor Protected by Conformal Parylene Nanoscale Coating
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Halide perovskites are promising memristive materials for neuromorphic computing, yet their practical deployment in hardware is severely hindered by instability against moisture, oxygen, and reactive metallic ions. Here, we develop an ultra‐robust perovskite memristor with all‐weather adaptability protected by a ∼100 nm conformal polymeric nanoscale coating. Deposited by low‐temperature, solvent‐free chemical vapor deposition (CVD) technique, the polymeric Parylene serves as an encapsulation, interfacial passivation, and homogeneous dielectric layer. The memristor exhibits excellent bipolar resistive switching under ambient conditions with high uniformity, an endurance of 1.5 × 10 4 cycles (over 12.5‐fold improvement), and a low set voltage of ∼0.27 V. It maintains stable operation under 100% relative humidity, thermal treatment at 348 K, 6‐month ambient storage, and 300 bending cycles at 90°, and even passes the stringent IPX7 waterproof standard. A hardware‐mapped convolutional neural network leveraging the synaptic properties of these memristors achieves a highly reliable MNIST recognition accuracy of 90%±0.4% across 10 independent test cycles. This work demonstrates that conformal Parylene encapsulation offers a comprehensive solution to the perovskite instability, paving the way for flexible and low‐power neuromorphic systems.

items.title: Thermodynamic-Computational-Agrarian Nexus for Neoglacial Resilience: Cryogenic Non-Volatile MRAM-PIM Intermittent Edge Computing, MCFC Tri-Generation Enthalpy Cascade, and Deterministic QFS-zkVM Sovereign Infrastructure(和訳副題:極小氷期レジリエンスのための熱力学・計算機・農業統合ネクサス:極低温不揮発性MRAM-PIM間欠エッジ計算、MCFCトリジェネレーション・エンタルピーカスケード、および決定論的QFS-zkVM主権インフラストラクチャ)
items.abstract: Full-scale paleoclimatic and econometric reconstructions of the Little Ice Age (LIA, c. 1300–1850) and Japan's Great Tenmei Famine (1782–1788) demonstrate that civilizational systemic failure under severe cooling anomalies stems from the non-linear coupling of shortened growing degree-days, energy cost explosion, and supply-chain fragmentation across over-integrated but ecologically brittle markets. Modern industrial Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) and conventional CMOS/Li-ion smart-farming architectures exhibit an acute thermodynamic vulnerability—the Cryogenic Energy Wall—wherein ambient drops below $-20\,^\circ\text{C}$ trigger severe lithium-ion internal resistance spikes ($>300\%$), lithium plating hazards, and heating enthalpy deficits, while conventional von Neumann edge processors suffer from static leakage and volatile state loss during grid intermittency. This monograph establishes a rigorous physical-layer, thermodynamic, and cryptographic architecture for an autonomous survival node—the Compute-Heat-Food Nexus—designed for deployment in municipal testbeds such as Toyota Woven City. First, we formalize a cryogenic non-volatile edge computing substrate utilizing Spin-Transfer Torque and Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetoresistive Random Access Memory Processing-in-Memory (STT/SOT-MRAM PIM) operating across $-40\,^\circ\text{C}$ to $125\,^\circ\text{C}$ with zero standby leakage ($P_{\text{standby}} \to 0$) and $10\,\text{ns}$ switching latency. Thermal fluctuation suppression at cryogenic temperatures increases the magnetic retention thermal stability factor $\Delta(T) = E_b / (k_B T)$, enabling zero-boot-overhead intermittent computing verified via QFS-zkVM state checkpoints over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field ($\mathbb{F}_p, p = 2^{64} - 2^{32} + 1$). Second, we formulate a closed-loop enthalpy cascade under Relativistic Thermodynamic Overhead (RTO P2.0) coupling biogas-fed Molten Carbonate Fuel Cell (MCFC) Tri-Generation (simultaneously yielding $2.3\,\text{MW}_e$ electricity, $1.2\,\text{t/day}$ $\text{H}_2$, $1,400\,\text{gal/day}$ ultrapure $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, and high-grade exhaust heat at $\eta_{\text{sys}} \ge 0.90$) with Direct-to-Chip liquid-cooled MRAM-PIM Digital Boilers ($60\text{--}70\,^\circ\text{C}$) and geothermal seasonal buffering. Third, we integrate All-Solid-State Battery (ASSB) robotics (retaining $\ge 70\%$ capacity at $-30\,^\circ\text{C}$) with phenotype-driven soil-free hydroponics/aeroponics over a LoRaWAN/Delay-Tolerant Network (DTN) mesh. Finally, we establish a Resilience-as-a-Service (RaaS) economic model backed by zero-knowledge weather-triggered parametric insurance, governed by Human-in-Command (HIC) constitutional interlocks (PHOENIX_BRIDGE / PHOENIX_ROUTER), SEC Rule 15c3-5 pre-execution kill-switches, and Delaware Caremark board-level fiduciary oversight. items.title: Thermally Conductive and Electrically Insulating Thermal Interface Materials for Advanced Packaging: From Filler and Interface Engineering to Thermal Networks
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal interface materials (TIMs) that combine efficient heat transport with electrical insulation are increasingly important for three‐dimensional integration and high‐power electronic packaging. Existing reviews commonly organize the field by filler type or treat surface modification, filler alignment, and network construction as separate strategies, obscuring their coupling across length scales. Here, we present a hierarchical design framework linking physical fundamentals, filler/interface engineering, and thermal‐network engineering. We first examine phonon transport, electrical‐failure mechanisms, area‐normalized thermal resistance, and effective‐medium models to define the constraints governing filler selection. We then compare oxide and nitride ceramics, carbon‐based materials, and emerging high‐thermal‐conductivity candidates, with emphasis on anisotropy, defect chemistry, processability, and electrical compatibility. Filler functionalization, spheroidization, and core–shell design are subsequently analyzed together with orientational alignment, multicomponent hybridization, and three‐dimensional network construction. Particular attention is given to the coupled effects of composite thermal conductivity, interfacial thermal resistance, bond‐line thickness, electrical insulation, processability, and long‐term reliability. Finally, we discuss six research directions spanning unconventional fillers, adaptive interfaces, multiscale computation, advanced manufacturing, chemical interphase design, and sustainable package co‐design. This framework shifts TIM development from isolated property maximization toward package‐relevant thermal–electrical–mechanical co‐optimization.

items.title: The 2026 Global Liquidation of Fraud Hypothesis: Sovereign Seizure of Shadow Bitcoin Reserves, Thermodynamic Collapse of AI Scaling Hype, and Deterministic Settlement via QFS-zkVM
items.abstract: This monograph formalizes the "2026 Global Liquidation of Fraud" (世界規模の不正清算) hypothesis proposed by Yoko Hasebe, demonstrating the structural isomorphism between two seemingly disparate macro-events in early 2026: (1) the kinetic seizure of the Maduro regime's estimated 600,000 BTC "Shadow Reserve" following Operation Absolute Resolve and its prospective absorption into the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve (SBR) under Executive Order 14233, and (2) the institutional authority contraction within frontier AI laboratories (exemplified by Google DeepMind) driven by physical high-bandwidth memory (HBM) bottlenecks, grid power deficits, data exhaustion, and negative return-on-investment (ROI) scaling walls. We construct a unified thermodynamic and algebraic model under RTO P2.0 and QFS-zkVM over the 64-bit Goldilocks prime field ($\mathbb{F}_p, p = 2^{64}-2^{32}+1$) that distinguishes unbacked paper claims and illicit shadow liquidity from verifiable Proof-of-Work and physical infrastructure assets. Furthermore, we integrate Q-SAFA cryptographic sovereign asset forfeiture auditing, PHOENIX_BRIDGE / PHOENIX_ROUTER liquidity isolation gates, Human-in-Command (HIC) fiduciary interlocks, SEC Rule 15c3-5 pre-trade market access controls, and Delaware Caremark board oversight duties to establish a rigorous institutional framework for surviving systemic asset impairment and sovereign supply shocks. items.title: Supplementary reproducibility package for "Independent Gate-Control and Source-Service Partitioning in Multi-Output GAA Logic"
items.abstract: Selected derived evidence supporting the research article "Independent Gate-Control and Source-Service Partitioning in Multi-Output GAA Logic", submitted to IET Circuits, Devices & Systems. The package contains the matched-resource physical acceptance records, extraction configuration, contact-resistivity sensitivity sweep, isolated/crossed source-network impedance matrices, paired compact-model circuit comparisons, fixed-network membership results, arc-characterization grids, workload and contact extensions, receiver-margin constants, deterministic-seed OpenROAD metrics, mesh comparisons, fixed-layout timing-replay records, the two-branch analytical rule, the figure-generation scripts, and an origin-path/SHA-256 manifest binding every copied artifact to its source in the project record. This is a selected evidence package, not a self-contained experiment archive. Raw transient waveforms, routed databases, simulator decks, and full run configurations are not included. GT3 (BSIM-CMG 111.2.1 in ngspice 47), PKP3, and OpenROAD-flow-scripts are public and are cited in the article. Results are predictive comparisons from research compact models and do not claim fabricated silicon, foundry signoff, or statistical yield. Integrity: SHA256SUMS inside the archive lists every file; the manuscript's PACKAGE_VERIFICATION.json records the SHA-256 of this ZIP.

items.title: PROPEL: A Memory-Driven, Adaptive Vector-Flow-Field Router with Process-Aware Waveguide Generation for Large-Scale Photonic Integrated Circuits
items.abstract: Photonic integrated circuits (PICs) are rapidly increasing in scale and routing complexity, driven by photonic computing, optical switching, programmable interferometer meshes, wavelength-routed optical networks-on-chip, and chip-to-chip optical interconnects. Manual waveguide planning becomes increasingly impractical as designs approach hundreds to thousands of photonic components, because routing must satisfy geometric, optical, electrical, and manufacturing constraints. This paper presents Photonic Routing Optimization and Placement Engine (PROPEL) , a memory-driven, native-accelerated adaptive vector-flow-field routing framework with process-aware waveguide generation for large-scale PIC physical design. PROPEL builds a routing kernel based on a bounded vector-flow-field algorithm and design-rule checking (DRC) validation. The same kernel supports passive optical routing, active optical–electrical routing, and topology-driven net assignment. C++ accelerates computationally intensive field and routing calculations, while Python performs detailed DRC replay, legality checking, route commitment, and GDSFactory-based geometry generation. Compared with state-of-the-art routing solutions, PROPEL is faster on 17 of 18 shared passive-routing cases, with a median speedup of 2.6 × and a geometric-mean speedup of 2.5 ×, while maintaining zero final design-rule violations. PROPEL also supports active optical–electrical routing, topology-driven net assignment, length, delay, and optical-path-length matching, process-map-aware waveguide generation, route-memory reuse, selective rip-up/reroute, and Graphic Data System (GDSII)-level legality replay. These capabilities address heterogeneous PIC layouts where optical, electrical, process, topology, matching, and manufacturability constraints must be handled together. In incremental-layout experiments, PROPEL restores more than 95% of previously verified routes after small local component movements and reroutes only the affected subset, reducing modified-design routing from tens or hundreds of seconds to a few seconds while maintaining zero final design-rule violations.

items.title: Lightweight Neural Fault Diagnosis of Analog Electronic Circuits: The Value of a Second Measurement Node and the Limits of Transfer under Severity and Operating-Condition Shift
items.abstract: A classifier can identify large component deviations in a simulated analog circuit and still fail when the deviation becomes smaller or the measurement conditions change. This study evaluates a compact neural diagnostic method with that distinction made explicit, and reports the negative results as carefully as the positive ones. Complex transfer estimates at eight excitation frequencies are normalized by the nominal circuit response and supplied to a multilayer perceptron with 32 and 16 hidden units. Two observation nodes are used, and an output-only variant isolates the value of the additional measurement. The numerical benchmark covers a Sallen–Key low-pass filter and a cascade of two active first-order filters. Circuit realizations are generated independently for training, validation, calibration and six test domains, and the test domains enter none of the model-selection decisions. Across five training seeds, the two-node network reaches 100.00 % matched-domain accuracy on both circuits and 98.25 % and 99.96 % accuracy at a waveform signal-to-noise ratio of 20 dB. Accuracy falls to 79.85 % and 83.56 % for unseen 12–24 % component deviations, and to 56.77 % and 76.41 % under combined stress. A support vector machine performs better under combined stress, by 4.41 and 4.33 percentage points, whereas the neural model improves on the output-only network by 7.84 and 11.49 points. The network has 1,737 trainable parameters. A local sensitivity analysis explains both the benefit and the limit of the second observation node, and an exact parameter-scaling invariance of the Sallen–Key topology is shown to bound what any classifier can recover from these measurements. Confidence analysis shows that nominal-domain temperature scaling does not ensure reliability after a severity shift: expected calibration error increases after calibration in every shifted domain, and a fixed rejection threshold accepts fewer than 10 % of mild-fault cases. The results support a small diagnostic model inside a specified operating envelope, identify the measurements and experiments required before deployment, and should not be read as a claim of robustness outside that envelope.

items.title: LV-RM 3 : Logic Synthesis and Verification of Computing-in-Memory Systems Using 3-Input Resistive Majority Gates
items.abstract: Resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) is a promising non-volatile technology that enables both data storage and in-memory Boolean computation, with 3-input resistive majority (RM \({}_{3}\) ) logic as a native computational primitive. Efficiently synthesizing, mapping, and verifying RM \({}_{3}\) -based logic under device constraints remains a critical challenge for ReRAM-based computing-in-memory (CiM) architectures. This paper presents an end-to-end framework for logic synthesis, mapping, and verification tailored to RM \({}_{3}\) -based ReRAM systems. The proposed approach employs an RM \({}_{3}\) -based logic representation and integrates exact synthesis, algebraic rewriting, and inversion-aware optimization to reduce logic complexity and hardware cost. A dynamic mapping and instruction-generation strategy is further developed to optimize execution efficiency and resource utilization on crossbar arrays. To ensure correctness, a dedicated intermediate representation, ReRAM micro-operation intermediate representation (ReMOIR), is introduced to model stateful execution and enable SAT-based equivalence checking between logic specifications and generated micro-operation sequences. Experimental results on the EPFL benchmark suite demonstrate that the proposed method reduces logic network size and depth by 14% and 17.7%, respectively, compared to majority-inverter graph (MIG)-based approaches. In addition, it outperforms the SIMPLER MAGIC architecture, reducing execution cycles by 10.16% and ReRAM usage by 41.11%. The proposed framework is implemented in the open-source logic synthesis tool ALSO .

items.title: Interfacial Charge Dynamics and Polarization Coupling in Ferroelectric Nematic Liquid Crystal Tailored PVDF Composite Films for High‐Performance Organic Triboelectric Nanogenerator‐Based Electromechanical Energy Harvesting
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing soft and conformable materials with enhanced charge generation and retention capabilities remains a critical barrier for next‐generation flexible triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs). Here, we report a polarization‐coupled tribo‐negative film fabricated by integrating a room‐temperature ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (FNLC) material (FNLC‐1571) into an electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) mat. In contrast to traditional rigid fillers, the optimally engineered ferroelectric nematic phase (N F ) of FNLC‐1571 microdomains assists spontaneous soft polar ordering in the nanofibrous PVDF matrix. This facilitates the integration of dipolar interactions with the fluorinated ends of PVDF, thereby synergistically promoting the crystallization of the electroactive β‐phase, enhancing dielectric behavior, modulating surface potential, improving interfacial charge‐trapping ability, and increasing contact area for superior charge generation while maintaining mechanical flexibility. When paired with a polyethylenimine (PEI)‐coated polyamide‐6 (PA‐6) tribo‐positive counter layer, the optimized 1 wt.% FNLC/PVDF‐based TENG delivers stable electrical output under low‐amplitude mechanical periodic contact‐separation excitation (8N, 10 Hz), with a peak‐to‐peak open‐circuit voltage of ∼395 V, a short‐circuit current of ∼40 µA, and a transferred charge of ∼167 nC. Finally, the optimally engineered all‐organic TENG assemblies were employed for various practical applications by demonstrating efficient capacitor charging, LED illumination, accurate biomechanical‐motion sensing, and real‐time IoT‐enabled monitoring through wireless interfacing.

items.title: IOCaps: de/centralized capabilities for I/O protection
items.abstract: Modern computing systems interact with a minefield of potentially buggy or malicious peripherals such as block storage, network devices, fixed-function video decoders and NPUs, and fully programmable GPUs and FPGAs. These peripherals must be allowed to perform direct memory access (DMA) on host memory, for high-speed bulk memory transfer, but must not be allowed to access memory not meant for them. IOMMUs can thwart DMA attacks via address translation but are limited in spatial security, temporal security, and performance. IOMMUs by definition are limited to page-granularity protection. IOMMUs have to perform slow walks over page tables (stored in slow DRAM) on the critical path, limiting throughput and increasing latency. IOTLBs can cache page table walks but I/O tends to have low locality, constantly accessing new pages and unmapping old ones, making caching ineffective. Invalidating IOTLB entries is so slow that Linux defers invalidation, leading drivers to accidentally access and reuse memory while it may still be exposed, to avoid an otherwise debilitating performance hit. This thesis proposes IOCaps: a capability-based system inspired by CHERI that replaces slow page table walks with fast cryptographic validation, allows peer-to-peer capability delegation and reduction, and improves protection granularity and invalidation latency. Instead of defining access control policies with a cache backed by DRAM page tables, IOCaps are access tokens that are stored by the peripherals, attached to each access, and validated by the host against a set of keys stored in fast SRAM. A Macaroon-inspired Message Authentication Code (MAC)-chaining system allows IOCaps to be reduced and passed between peripherals, facilitating CHERI-like compartmentalization, while remaining secure. IOCaps, like CHERI capabilities, encode the bounds of accessible regions at sub-page precision, avoiding accidental exposure of sensitive data near exposed regions. While IOCaps do not enable translation they can still be layered on top of IOMMU translation if needed, for example, for virtualization. Using separate systems for protection and translation should allow translation to be made less granular, using high-locality hugepages to be more IOMMU-friendly, without sacrificing protection granularity—the best of both worlds. After justifying and describing the basic system, this thesis investigates spatial security, temporal security, and performance to show IOCaps are a viable alternative to IOMMU protection. Spatial Security. IOCaps must be compact to avoid bottlenecking DMA throughput, but must still represent a 64-bit address region with high precision and multiple reductions, which I show is viable through a new approach to compression. Temporal Security. Because protection is no longer backed by a persistent page table, IOCap lifetimes are entirely dependent on that of the keys used to validate them, requiring more keys per peripheral than prior art in the same vein. I investigate different MAC functions, fundamental limits on the number of keys per system, and allocation methods that allow IOCaps to scale to underprovisioned systems without loss of security. Performance. I implement an IOCap protection system in practice using QEMU-based emulation and real FPGA hardware, integrate it with existing CheriBSD VirtIO drivers, and demonstrate that the impact on bulk DMA throughput is minimal.

items.title: Gate Dielectric Engineering and Performance Optimization of Monolayer MoS2 Field-Effect Transistors
items.abstract: 随着硅基电子器件特征尺寸持续缩小，短沟道效应和热耗散瓶颈问题日益严峻。二硫化钼（ molybdenum disulfide,MoS2）作为典型的二维过渡金属硫族化合物（ transition-metal dichalcogenides,TMDCs），因其原子级厚度、直接带隙以及优异电学特性，在下一代低功耗场效应晶体管中展现出巨大潜力。但其原子级沟道使载流子易受界面散射与介电环境影响，仍严重制约器件输运性能。本文通过构建MoS2背栅场效应晶体管模型，系统对比了二氧化硅（ SiO2）、氧化铝（ Al2O3）、二氧化铪（ HfO2）三种栅介质对器件电学性能的影响，并进一步对HfO2栅介质进行厚度优化。结果表明，HfO2高介电常数栅介质通过强介电屏蔽有效抑制库仑杂质散射，在10 nm厚度处实现最优性能：跨导达666 μS，开关比~1013、亚阈值摆幅~70 mV/dec，但受远程界面声子散射影响，其载流子迁移率降至137cm2/(V·s)。本研究阐明了MoS2场效应晶体管栅介质选择与厚度设计对MoS2晶体管电学输运特性的竞争机制，为二维半导体晶体管的栅介质工程研究提供了重要的理论参考。

items.title: Fyto: Autoregressive Language-Model Inference Powered Solely by a Living Houseplant
items.abstract: Published plant- and soil-microbial-fuel-cell (PMFC/SMFC) electronics run duty-cycled sensing and a radio; none runs a neural network. We present Fyto, a sealed box in a potted golden pothos (Epipremnum aureum) that generates text with a llama2.c-class transformer on an Ambiq Apollo4 Plus microcontroller, with two hydraulically separated PMFC chambers as its only energy source and output leaving through a galvanically isolated UART. No Fyto hardware has yet been measured: energy figures are emulated or modelled, and the claim that a plant powers inference is a pre-registered hypothesis. Instruction-level emulation of verified Cortex-M4 kernels gives 3.1–3.5 cycles per int8 multiply–accumulate, about twice the usual assumption; the resulting model gives 18–55 µJ per token for a 1.1 M-parameter model (36–55 µJ at the emulated cycle counts; the low end assumes a hand-scheduled 1.75-cycle kernel). Pots delivering the tens-to-hundreds of microwatts reported in the literature still sustain 2×10⁴–5×10⁵ tokens per day (revised chain, Monte Carlo p10–p90). The binding constraints lie elsewhere: an always-on chain idles at 34–69 µW, the specified harvester's fractional-Voc tracking (70–90 %) captures at most 0.61 of the power of a cell whose maximum power point sits at 0.42 Voc; and retained SRAM costs more than the plant supplies. A revised chain with per-chamber constant-voltage harvesting, a decifarad store, power-gating and per-token MRAM commits idles at 1–2.5 µW and wakes in 99.7 % of draws. Running the real stories260K checkpoint, we measure 0.446 words per token and show that per-token commits resume bit-exactly in all 600 fault-injection runs (1,513 brownouts), against 187 of 600 runs (31 %) for a naive ordering. Because a gram of soil carbon could power this load for decades, we pre-register controls (unplanted, sterilised soil, darkness, plant removal, electrode swap, titanium-only, galvanic), an energy ledger, a coulombic-overdraft test and a ¹³CO₂ electron budget that would measure, for the first time in any plant fuel cell, the fraction of charge, and so of tokens, paid for by freshly fixed CO₂. Preprint v1. Code, data, figures and LaTeX sources are included in fyto-paper-v1-code-data.zip. Project: fytopure.online.
