items.title: Electrochemical Oxidation of Perfluorobutanoic Acid and Ultrashort-Chain Perfluorocarboxylic Acids
items.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical oxidation of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) with ≤3 perfluorinated carbons, including perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA), perfluoropropionic acid (PFPrA), and trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), was investigated using a Ti4O7 reactive electrochemical membrane (REM) anode in an inert NaClO4 electrolyte. This study demonstrated mineralization of all PFAS to fluoride and detailed their anodic reactivity. Oxidation of PFBA, PFPrA, and TFA occurred at potentials ≥3.2 V versus the standard hydrogen electrode (V/SHE), reaching mass transfer limited rates at ≥4.2 V/SHE. Applying 4.7 V/SHE, ≥99% of each PFAS was transformed within a hydraulic residence time of 53 s, and removal was enhanced 1.5-fold due to electromigration of PFAS anions toward the anode. The local pH drop at the anode converted a fraction of the PFAS to their acidic forms, which exhibited lower reactivity due to an increase in their estimated standard redox potentials (E0) by more than 1.0 V, as predicted by density functional theory. Butler–Volmer modeling captured both the activation-controlled and mass transfer limited regimes with transfer coefficients between 0.13 and 0.20, while acid/anion co-occurrence prevented exact determination of E0 and exchange current densities. Finally, sulfate competition during electrochemical oxidation of a synthetic semiconductor fab effluent reduced PFAS mineralization efficiency by >20%, exhibiting the challenge of designing Ti4O7 REM systems to avoid ultrashort-chain PFAS accumulation.

items.title: Comparative Evaluation Methodologies for Algorithm Acceleration on Embedded Platforms: A Structured Review and Reproducible Assessment Framework
items.abstract: Background: Performance results for algorithms accelerated on microcontrollers, field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), multiprocessor systems-on-chip (MPSoCs), embedded GPUs, and application-specific accelerators are often reported under different workloads, accuracy requirements, and measurement conditions. Objective: This review examines how published studies measure execution time, throughput, energy, memory use, and hardware resources, and proposes a consistent approach to interpreting comparisons across platforms. Methods: A targeted review of publisher records, research repositories, and benchmarking standards identified 15 representative implementations published between 2015 and 2026. The analysis draws on 52 references, including primary studies, surveys, and methodological sources. Study outcomes were recorded with their associated tasks, platforms, measurement conditions, and level of source verification. Because the search was not an exhaustive database-level systematic search, the article is presented as a structured review rather than a PRISMA-compliant systematic review. Results: Reported outcomes vary substantially in both units and experimental scope. One FPGA CNN implementation reported 61.62 GFLOPS at 100 MHz; FINN reported 21,906 image classifications per second under a stated system power of less than 25 W; and a 2026 microcontroller study reported 38 ms execution time, 387 µJ per inference, and 174 kB of SRAM in a specified configuration. These results cannot be ranked directly without matching workload and measurement conditions. Discussion: Differences in power boundaries, memory definitions, hardware configurations, and baseline optimization limit cross-study interpretation. The proposed Cross-Platform Accelerator Evaluation Protocol (CAEP) provides a sequence of checks for workload equivalence, measurement boundaries, and reporting completeness before numerical comparisons are made. Conclusion: A defensible comparison begins by establishing whether results measure equivalent tasks under sufficiently similar conditions. The proposed protocol requires prospective validation, and a comprehensive systematic review would require a fully documented database search and independent full-text assessment.

items.title: BEOL-compatible monolithic integration of property-tunable complex oxide single crystals on Si for advancing the more-than-Moore paradigm
items.abstract: Complex oxide single-crystal thin films offer diverse functionalities essential for advancing the More-than-Moore paradigm in semiconductor technology. However, their direct integration with Si-based complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) circuits remains challenging due to thermal budget constraints and the difficulty of applying oxide-engineering techniques—such as strain, interface, and domain engineering— for tailoring properties on silicon. In this work, we demonstrate room-temperature monolithic integration of complex oxides onto silicon by combining epitaxial lift-off and surface-activated metal bonding, effectively overcoming thermal limitations. This method allows the application of oxide-engineering methodologies on silicon substrates, as demonstrated using ferromagnetic SrRuO3, ferroelectric Pb(Mg,Nb)O3-Pb(Zr,Ti)O3, and induced-ferroelectric SrTiO3. Moreover, we highlight its practical potential through the fabrication of flexible ferroelectric heterostructures and electrically-controllable energy storage devices with a one-transistor, one-capacitor structure. This integration strategy facilitates the incorporation of emergent oxide functionalities into CMOS via back-end-of-line (BEOL) processes, bridging complex oxide science with silicon technology for advancing the More-than-Moore paradigm.

items.title: Advanced semiconductor materials for future electronic systems: from conventional to quantum devices
items.abstract: Modern electronics have advanced through the continuous improvement of semiconductor technology. However, the fundamental limitations of conventional silicon, including scaling constraints, short-channel effects, and quantum phenomena, necessitate advanced semiconductor materials and next-generation device architectures. This review discusses the development of semiconductor materials from conventional elemental and compound semiconductors to wide-band-gap, two-dimensional (2D), organic, and quantum semiconductors for future electronic systems. It covers semiconductor physics, band structure engineering, material characterization, device performance metrics, and recent advances in crystal growth, epitaxial growth, film deposition, nanofabrication, and doping techniques. This review also examines emerging semiconductor devices, including FinFETs, gate-all-around (GAA) transistors, neuromorphic and memristive devices, spintronics, and quantum semiconductor devices. Atomically thin 2D semiconductors offer remarkable electrostatic control for future miniaturization, while wide-band-gap semiconductors provide higher breakdown field strength and stability than silicon. Furthermore, the review evaluates defect engineering, interface reliability, quantum–material quality, heterogeneous integration, and fabrication compatibility, particularly the BEOL thermal budget below 400 °C, which is critical for integrating new semiconductor channels with silicon logic. Consequently, low-temperature deposition processes such as atomic layer deposition (ALD), plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD), and selective CVD/MOCVD methods provide beneficial routes for heterogeneous integration.

items.title: The World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA): Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design for Embedded AI in Robotics
items.abstract: Embedded AI is moving from perception to prediction. Robots now use world models$\unicode{x2014}$learned simulators that predict the outcome of candidate actions in a compressed latent space before any is executed. Every predicted step must be computed on board within a tight power and thermal budget, yet the energy these steps fundamentally require, and how far real hardware sits from it, have not been characterized. We derive lower bounds on the arithmetic operations and the CMOS dynamic energy of a latent state transition from information theory and Boolean circuit complexity. Profiling a DreamerV3-style Recurrent State Space Model (RSSM) shows that every rollout operation is memory-bandwidth bound and that a GPU consumes at least $5.9\times10^{10}$ times the CMOS energy floor. Transient 3D thermal simulations show that this inefficiency is also a thermal one, since sustained back-to-back planning heats a millimeter-scale silicon tile to 556 K even behind an ideal copper heat spreader. Guided by this chain from bound to bottleneck, we propose the World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA), a chip architecture for embedded world model planning that combines near-memory computation, real-time entropy estimation, variable-precision rollout units, and copy-on-write latent scratchpads. With a design target of 40x lower power, the same tile stays near ambient at 306 K in simulation, pointing toward practical planning on thermally constrained robots.

items.title: Atik: A Shared-Mesh Transformer Accelerator for RISC-V
items.abstract: Transformer inference repeatedly invokes dense matrix multiplication and attention, including its data-dependent softmax normalization. We present Atik, an open-source RoCC accelerator for RocketChip that executes matrix multiplication and dense attention through one shared fixed-point MAC mesh. Atik accepts and returns BF16 tensors, uses a streaming online-softmax schedule that never materializes the full score matrix, and is invoked through a small descriptor-based ABI. We evaluate three meshes cycle-by-cycle on FireSim and report standalone Sky130 physical-design area. Across 137 logged FireSim test records, all tests pass their benchmark tolerance with zero reported output mismatches. Relative to the same scalar Rocket BF16 reference, the 8x8 configuration reaches 31.5x peak matmul speedup and 225.8x peak attention speedup. Hybrid projections for the single-layer workload-derived C models, using directly measured accelerator-kernel cycles, give aggregate speedups of 44.2x, 77.1x, and 32.3x for ViT, TinyBERT, and GPT-2 prefill, respectively; these are not full-model hardware replays.

items.title: Robust & Scalable Website Fingerprinting via Minimal DRAM Traffic
items.abstract: Website fingerprinting attacks infer websites visited by users and threaten their privacy. These attacks are classified as on-path, which monitor network traffic, and co-located, which exploit shared system resources. Existing co-located attacks, such as sweep-counting and loop-counting, achieve over 90% accuracy but suffer significant performance degradation on many-core systems. Loop-counting accuracy drops from 93% on 8 cores to 50% on 24 cores, while sweep-counting accuracy decreases from 84% to 45% across multiple Core Complex Dies (CCDs). To address these limitations, we propose memory-chasing, a scalable website fingerprinting attack that exploits DRAM traffic interference through pointer-chasing traversals with minimal interference. By counting DRAM accesses over fixed intervals, the attack generates distinctive traces for website classification. Evaluated on the top 50 websites, memory-chasing achieves 96% accuracy on a 24-core system, 86% across multiple CCDs, 80% across multiple sockets, and 97% in an open-world setting. Extensive evaluation across hardware configurations, browsers, operating systems, isolation mechanisms, system noise, and countermeasures demonstrates its robustness and scalability.

items.title: TwinHash: Two-Sided Object Identity Management for Time- and Energy-Efficient Agentic Workflows
items.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) services interleave large language model (LLM) generation with external tool execution, and increasingly rely on search-based workflows that repeatedly revisit shared reasoning states and computations. These patterns create substantial redundancy across tool outputs, LLM responses, and key-value (KV) prefixes, yet existing serving systems primarily optimize shared prompt prefixes, while naive input-keyed caching is unsafe when identical requests produce different outputs. We present TwinHash, a unified object management architecture that assigns each object an input-side hash key to recognize repeated requests and an output-side content fingerprint to validate and locate stored state, complemented by type-specific reuse guards that preserve correctness and response diversity. A software object identity table maintains reusable objects across requests and trajectories, while a hardware object placement table tracks their residency across hierarchical memory tiers so that evicted state can be retrieved rather than recomputed. Across seven agent frameworks and five benchmark suites, reuse follows workflow structure more than benchmark identity. TwinHash serves up to 81% of tool outputs wherever deterministic tool reads recur, and up to 92% of LLM responses in search-based frameworks. Retrieving an evicted KV-prefix from DRAM reduces TTFT by up to 5.6x on Qwen3-32B, with greater gains projected for larger dense models. Under search-based frameworks, TwinHash reduces end-to-end wall-clock time by up to 87% and measured task energy by up to 81% over a prefix-cached baseline, while a per-key serving cap controls the quality-reuse trade-off in adaptive search. These results demonstrate that unified identity, safety, and placement management can convert structural redundancy in emerging agentic workflows into substantial serving-efficiency gains.

items.title: Circuit Theory-Informed AI for Condition Monitoring in Power Electronics
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence for power electronics is evolving toward a deeper comprehension of system intrinsic behaviors and dynamics. As a novel integration of neural computation and electric circuits, spike-based neuromorphic computing offers promising potential in high energy efficiency and adaptability for data-driven applications. Building on the latency-coding principles, this article proposes a framework for data-light condition monitoring that relies solely on three-phase AC current measurements. The AC current signals are encoded as membrane potentials of RC-based spiking neurons, which are inherently compatible with spiking neural networks that can effectively facilitate the estimation of device parameters. Case studies are presented to validate the performances, while constraints and further optimizations are also evaluated and discussed, and future extensions of the methodology are provided.

items.title: ЕКСПЕРИМЕНТАЛЬНЕ ТЕСТУВАННЯ ПЕРЕТВОРЮВАЧА ЧАСТОТИ НА ОСНОВІ GAN ТРАНЗИСТОРІВ ДЛЯ ЕЛЕКТРОПРИВОДІВ ЗМІННОГО СТРУМУ З ПІДВИЩЕНОЮ ЧАСТОТОЮ ШИРОТНО-ІМПУЛЬСНОЇ МОДУЛЯЦІЇ
items.abstract: The experimental results of testing a GaN HEMT based high frequency inverter for controlled electric drives applications are presented. The dead-time insertion impact on the quality of stator reference voltage tracking is also highlighted within this paper. The most used algorithm of dead-time compensation is presended. In that algorithm the polarity of compensation voltage is defined by stator’s currents directions and ithe magnitude of that voltage is defined by dead-time interval duration. It is shown that even without dead-time compensation GaN HEMT based inverter demonstrates better performance that IGBT based inverter in term of stator reference voltage tracking. The ability of GaN HEMT based inverter to operate with PWM carrier frequency up to 60 kHz with dead-time of 50 ns was experimentally proven. Corresponding phase-current waveforms and phase portraits are presented. References 10, Figures 10.

items.title: Wavon Field-Based Generalized In-Memory Computing Chip Architecture
items.abstract: What if a chip could be wired by field instead of lithography? The Wavon architecture answers with a single structural proposition: computation need not be carried by wired electrons at all. It replaces fixed interconnect with a blank topological lattice, in which 20-80 GHz millimetre-band electromagnetic evanescent waves act as the signal carrier, and solid-state magnetic skyrmions hold the state of the machine. Nothing in the substrate is hardwired. PDMM software instructions rewrite the steady-state MTJ magnetoresistance, configuring waveguide routing and model weights online, while the physical eigenstructure of the field does the arithmetic: discrete topological boundaries compress the O(n²) cost of conventional matrix multiply-accumulate into a constant O(1) latency intrinsic to MEPS wavefront evolution. The chip leaves the fab as a uniform blank lattice on a 28 nm ultra-near-field substrate, built by a three-layer ultraviolet nanoimprint co-integration process. Vernier Moiré fringes formed by lattice arrays and passive metallic meshes deliver physical self-alignment between layers, removing the multilayer precision overlay lithography and heavy ion doping that conventional silicon requires, and removing any dependence on high-numerical-aperture front-end lithography across the full operational cycle. Interleaved coplanar MTJ and skyrmion arrangements form a globally vacuum-sealed microcavity tunnelling waveguide system that fixes the local guided-mode refractive index at unity with dn/dT = 0. Rare-earth-free, heavy-metal-free RE-TM heterostructures anchor the skyrmions with zero drift at room temperature. Two modes share one hardware origin: binary wavefront carry arithmetic for absolute-precision digital inference, and continuous field-state evolution for energy-level excitation of topological states. The full fabrication process adapts to mature mass-production semiconductor lines without specialised new equipment. in-memory computing, compute-in-memory, memory wall, power wall, quantum wall, von Neumann bottleneck, memristor, CBRAM, PCM, MRAM, silicon photonics, metasurface, VCMA, MTJ, skyrmion, magnetic skyrmion, evanescent wave, lithography, nanoimprint lithography, CPU, GPU, TPU, photonic computing, topological photonics, 3D integration, 28 nm, post-Moore, AI accelerator, neuromorphic computing, non-volatile memory, synaptic plasticity, write endurance

items.title: Understanding the Surface and Interfacial Structure of N -Heterocyclic Carbenes on Ruthenium Substrates: An X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopic Approach
items.abstract: Abstract N-Heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) are exceptional σ-donors and bind strongly to a wide variety of transition metals. Their unique binding properties have expanded the potential applications of NHCs to area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) for microelectronics fabrication. This new application area requires a deeper understanding of the NHC-to-metal interaction beyond the scale of small molecule NHC–metal complexes. Various surface characterization techniques have been applied to study the NHC-deposited metal surfaces, but to date, most studies have been limited to NHCs deposited on single crystals. Ru is an appealing material in the semiconductor industry because of its moderate resistivity and low electromigration rate. There remains a lack of understanding regarding the surface chemistry of NHCs on Ru metal, with the knowledge gained from NHCs on single crystals not necessarily transferable to NHCs on the polycrystalline substrates encountered in microelectronic devices. To bridge this gap, we report herein an in-depth X-ray photoelectron spectroscopic investigation into the interactions between NHCs and polycrystalline Ru surfaces. Two NHC derivatives with different wingtip and backbone groups were employed. Using different incident energies providing varied penetration depths, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopic measurements were conducted to provide insight into how changes in the NHC structure impact the surface coverage density, molecule-to-metal charge transfer, and the ability to protect Ru surfaces.
items.venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters

items.title: Tunable magnetotransport through kinetically arrested first-order phase transitions in an antiferromagnetic metal
items.abstract: Controllable multilevel resistance states are of interest for memory technologies like neuromorphic computing, but robust materials platforms toward such behavior remain limited. Here, we show that the non-centrosymmetric antiferromagnetic metal CeCoGe$_3$ suggests one such route through a kinetically hindered first-order magnetic transition. Cooling through the kinetically hindered first-order transition in an applied magnetic field produces a magnetic glass state in which high- and low-temperature magnetic phases coexist. The relative fraction of these phases can be controlled by the applied field in which the sample is cooled, and the electrical resistance is directly sensitive to that fraction. As a result, it is demonstrated that CeCoGe$_3$ supports stable multilevel resistive states. These results identify kinetically hindered first-order phase transitions as a promising route towards controllable multilevel magnetoresistive states.

items.title: TinyNCFormer: A Tensor-Decomposed Dual-Stream Transformer with Diffusion-Guided Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for White Blood Cell Classification and Instance Segmentation
items.abstract: Abstract White blood cell (WBC) classification from peripheral blood smear images is central to diagnosing leukemia, infection, and other hematologic disorders, and remains one of the most frequently requested laboratory analyses in clinical practice. Automated classification is difficult because WBC subtypes are morphologically similar, clinical microscopy fields routinely contain multiple overlapping cells, and large, accurate models are impractical to deploy on point-of-care hardware. This trade-off is addressed with a knowledge-distillation framework in which a single teacher, formed by fusing five diverse pretrained backbones over a nuclear-cytoplasmic, stain-separated representation, supervises a compact dual-stream Transformer student, TinyNCFormer, through confidence-calibrated soft-target distillation, diffusion-based feature denoising, and an instance-segmentation head for multi-cell scenes. Evaluated on our newly introduced RV-PBS dataset and three additional blood cell corpora (CRV-PBS, PBC, and C-PBC), the resulting 16.5-million-parameter student exceeds every constituent backbone, reaching classification F1-scores of 96.32--98.32\% and mean average precisions of 0.865--0.883 for instance segmentation across the four datasets, outperforming prior baselines by an average of 8.7\% (range 2.7--15.3\%) in relative mAP. These results show that diverse ensemble supervision with uncertainty- and denoising-aware distillation yields a compact model more accurate than its teacher and substantially more efficient, a practical candidate for point-of-care hematological screening.

items.title: TinyML on the Edge: Optimizing Neural Networks for Low-Power Microcontrollers
items.abstract: To enable autonomous sensing at the extreme edge, machine learning models must escape the cloud. TinyML brings deep learning capabilities directly to resource-constrained hardware such as microcontrollers. Traditional Internet of Things (IoT) frameworks rely on sending massive raw sensor payloads to cloud environments, introducing severe latency, bandwidth congestion, and privacy vulnerabilities. This paper presents a cohesive design flow for optimizing deep neural networks (DNNs) using post-training quantization and structured weight pruning. We demonstrate a highly optimized implementation of a Keyword Spotting (KWS) model deployed on a resource-constrained ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller. The proposed optimization pipeline yields an 86\% reduction in Flash memory footprint and a 6.3$\times$ reduction in inference latency, while dropping overall system active power draw down to 11.2~mW. Our results confirm that complex pattern matching can run locally and autonomously on standard low-cost embedded chips.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Threshold voltage engineering via diode-embedded p-GaN gate HEMTs
items.abstract: Abstract In this work, enhancement-mode (E-mode) p-GaN/AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) with monolithically embedded gate diodes are investigated to explore the use of embedded diode width as a design parameter for threshold-voltage engineering. The embedded diode geometry modulates the electrostatic potential within the gate stack, thereby tuning the threshold voltage. A wide threshold-voltage tuning range of 1.45–3.3 V was achieved, where 1.45 V corresponds to the reference device without an embedded diode and 3.3 V corresponds to the device with a diode-to-HEMT channel ratio of 0.1. In addition, the diode-embedded structure exhibits improved forward gate breakdown voltage while maintaining comparable on-resistance and off-state breakdown voltage. Pulsed bias measurements reveal that smaller diode widths effectively suppress negative threshold-voltage shifts, indicating enhanced dynamic gate stability. These results demonstrate that monolithically embedded gate diodes provide an effective and scalable approach for threshold-voltage engineering and reliability enhancement in E-mode GaN HEMTs for power-switching applications.

items.title: Thermal-Crosstalk-Aware Scheduling and Model Predictive Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling for Spaceborne Multi-Chip AI Clusters in Deep Vacuum: Lumped Multiphysics Modeling, Predictive Control, and Numerical Simulation
items.abstract: High-density heterogeneous artificial intelligence (AI) computing clusters onboard small satellites in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) face severe electrothermal constraints. Gas-mediated convective heat transfer is neglected in the adopted high-vacuum model (h ≈ 0), confining thermal rejection exclusively to internal solid conduction and non-linear Stefan-Boltzmann radiation to deep space (q ∝ T⁴). In multi-chip modules (MCM), heavy neural inference workloads induce severe lateral conductive coupling between adjacent silicon dies (thermal crosstalk). This paper investigates a model-based predictive thermal management strategy, denoted TCAS-DVFS (Thermal-Crosstalk-Aware Scheduling and Model Predictive Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling), formulated from lumped thermodynamic principles for multi-die spaceborne accelerators. The proposed architecture integrates: (i) real-time state estimation via an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) operating over a non-linear 5×5 Compact Thermal Model (CTM); (ii) a discrete linear time-varying Model Predictive Controller (LTV MPC-DVFS) that solves a condensed quadratic program via a warm-started ADMM-style splitting iteration, coordinating operating frequencies; (iii) a dynamic temperature-referenced radiative power-budget surrogate derived from orbital ephemerides; and (iv) a topological task allocator relaxed over the semidefinite cone S₊¹⁷ via Semidefinite Programming (SDP). In a three-orbit numerical co-simulation of a 500-km circular LEO scenario (17,004.0 s, 34,009 time samples, 4 processing dies), TCAS-DVFS produced zero observed junction temperature violations above the 85 °C threshold (0 s versus 200.5 s for binary Thermal Throttling at 85/75 °C and 14.0 s for Space-PID), attenuated peak inter-die thermal gradients by 77.6% (reducing from 9.42 to 2.11 K), and maintained an aggregate throughput proxy of 124.38 FPS with an energy-delay product proxy of 7.48 kJ·s/frame. Rather than asserting unconditional superiority, we characterize TCAS-DVFS as a multi-objective trade-off that enforces strict thermal containment and high throughput, whereas uncoordinated baselines like simple TCA achieve lower peak gradients (1.58 K) at the cost of lower throughput (116.16 FPS). Functional ablation indicates a dominant contribution from the predictive control formulation in damping gradients and bounding temperatures, whereas topological SDP scheduling provides limited observed benefits in compact arrangements (N = 4 dies) due to conductive symmetry. Sensitivity was evaluated under a 30-sample Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) stress-test envelope (±20% parameter variation across physical plant resistances and capacitances), yielding zero observed violations with an exact 95% Clopper-Pearson upper confidence bound of 11.57%, where die-to-radiator thermal resistance (R_r) exhibited the strongest monotonic association with T_max (Spearman ρ = +0.994). Indicative reliability proxy analyses demonstrate that electromigration yields no net life extension (Relative Mean Time to Failure [MTTF] proxy ratios of 0.96 and 0.81 on aggregate dies, with 1.52 and 1.33 on the hottest individual die), whereas cyclic thermal stress severity is substantially reduced (cycles above 2.0 K drop from 612 to 20). The reported evidence is limited to numerical simulation of the stated lumped-parameter model and does not constitute hardware or flight qualification.
authors: Dafnhê Thor Castro de Martins Barros

items.title: Resolving hidden interface-trap capture times through stochastic current transients in multitrap nanoscale transistors
items.abstract: Charge trapping at semiconductor–dielectric interfaces governs threshold-voltage instability, low-frequency noise, and stochastic variability in nanoscale transistors. In the intermediate multitrap regime, the drain-current transient is neither a defect-resolved signal from a single trap nor a fully averaged ensemble response, making the underlying trap kinetics difficult to infer directly. Here, a framework combining pulsed current–voltage measurement and self-consistent stochastic modeling is introduced for extracting statistical capture-time descriptors of interface-trap ensembles from sensing-phase drain-current transients. The approach analyzes repeated subthreshold transients using both the mean current and its cycle-to-cycle fluctuation, while explicitly incorporating trap-to-trap dispersion, sensing-bias-dependent capture kinetics, and electrostatic feedback induced by progressive trap filling. Simultaneous fitting across multiple sensing biases identifies a common model-constrained parameter pair within an assumed log-normal parameterization of the capture-time-constant distribution. Within the assumed model, this analysis distinguishes intrinsic trap-to-trap kinetic disorder from measurement-induced electrostatic renormalization, revealing that the measured transient is not a direct image of the intrinsic time-constant spectrum but a dynamically reshaped response governed by finite-ensemble stochasticity and channel electrostatics. The framework provides a physics-based route for extracting hidden multitrap kinetic descriptors from stochastic electronic transients in nanoscale devices.

items.title: Resistive switching in large-scale MoS2 grown on Ag(111)
items.abstract: Among the many applications in which 2D materials are expected to provide technological advances, recently the discovery of non-volatile resistive switching places them as valuable candidates for future brain-inspired neuromorphic computing or data storage devices. As per other fields, the need for large-scale grown 2D materials, mostly transition metal dichalcogenides, is a key-aspect for the lab-to-fab transition. Here, pulsed laser deposition of MoS2 onto Ag(111) in different environments is implemented as a viable route to obtain the direct growth of the active layer on the metallic electrode. Raman spectroscopy and conductive atomic force microscopy are carried out to check the crystal quality on the cm2 scale and investigate the local electronic properties, respectively. Large-scale growth and resistive switching mechanism are demonstrated, suggesting a critical role of the MoS2/Ag interface depending on the surface preparation and water intercalation in ambient conditions. In a device fabrication-oriented perspective, such aspects should be carefully considered to achieve the best conditions for device operation.

items.title: Resilience of Sub-10 nm MoSi2N4 and WSi2N4 TFETs Against Surface Roughness: Device and Digital Applications
items.abstract: Abstract Monolayers of the \((\mathrm{MA}_2\mathrm{Z}_4)\) family, particularly \((\mathrm{MoSi}_2\mathrm{N}_4)\) and \((\mathrm{WSi}_2\mathrm{N}_4)\), are promising channel materials for steep-slope tunnel field-effect transistors (TFETs) in beyond-CMOS electronics. However, interface imperfections introduce critical device variability. Here, we investigate the impact of substrate surface roughness on sub-10 nm \((\mathrm{MoSi}_2\mathrm{N}_4)\) and \((\mathrm{WSi}_2\mathrm{N}_4)\) TFETs using a tight-binding model within the non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism. The surface corrugation induces localized midgap states, triggering parasitic trap-assisted tunneling that elevates the OFF-current and degrades the sub-threshold swing. Although both 2D channels show strong resilience up to an RMS roughness of \((\delta h \approx 150)\)pm-maintaining intrinsic delays as fast as \((\tau \approx 0.20\text{--}0.25)\) ps at \((L_\mathrm{ch} = 3)\) nm-higher roughness severely suppresses the ON-current and compresses the ON-OFF current ratio by four orders of magnitude. Monolayer \((\mathrm{WSi}_2\mathrm{N}_4)\) consistently demonstrates superior electrostatic robustness compared to \((\mathrm{MoSi}_2\mathrm{N}_4)\). Furthermore, inverter simulations reveal degraded transition slope with surface roughness. These results emphasize the need for atomically smooth substrates or planarization techniques to preserve steep-slope switching in scaled 2D nanoelectronics.

items.title: Reproducibility artifacts for Checking Latency Contracts in ECC Memory Maintenance
items.abstract: Reproducibility materials for an implementation case study of ECC memory maintenance. The package contains Supplement S1 (source pins, verification scope, free tool requirements, commands and expected observations) and Supplement S2 (source-only reproduction reader, raw records, replay evidence, checker controls, progress/interference checks, toolchain lock, licences, artifact change log and file manifests). The associated manuscript is submitted separately and is not included in this deposit. The study examines a pinned PULP ECC SRAM integration. At bank latency two, the original maintenance consumer can use another address's response and replace an unfaulted target with a valid codeword for the wrong payload. A separately attributed experimental correction waits for the intended response and cancels/retries an interrupted maintenance read. There are 15 frozen fixtures at four bank latencies in each of two variants (120 selected executions). The original variant has overlapping scenario counts 7 logical-payload, 16 physical-state, 34 target-report and 45 ownership violations out of 60; the candidate has zero declared violations in those categories. Declared CPU codec-flag transport violations are zero in both. These counts are selected deterministic observations, not population failure rates. A package replay verified 600 byte-identical CSV records and separately reaudited 32 pilot traces. Symbolic results apply only to their fixed sequence, guarded inputs and depth; timed-out repair queries establish no theorem. No arbitrary-traffic, all-parameter, four-state or silicon guarantee is made. Sustained CPU priority may starve maintenance. The recorded reproduction environment is Windows, Python 3.12+, the pinned OSS CAD Suite and a C++20 compiler. The delivered path runs local compilation, simulation and checking. Each source and third-party component retains its individual copyright and licence notices; no blanket relicensing of third-party code is intended.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Quantum Searching and Optimization Algorithms
items.abstract: This book offers a rigorous and forward-looking exploration of one of the most consequential frontiers in modern computation: the use of quantum mechanics to accelerate search, optimization, learning, simulation, and secure information processing. It begins by establishing the conceptual and mathematical foundations of quantum computation, including quantum gates, circuit design, quantum parallelism, and the distinctions between classical and quantum models of information processing. It then develops the algorithmic core of the field, examining how quantum principles can be systematically translated into high-impact procedures for searching structured and unstructured spaces, solving optimization problems, and achieving provable computational advantages under realistic hardware constraints. This book: Provides a comprehensive treatment of the broader quantum ecosystem. Covers quantum cryptography and post-quantum security, error correction and fault tolerance, programming frameworks and software stacks, hardware platforms, and the emerging interface between quantum computing and machine learning. Critically engages with real-world applications in finance, logistics, pharmaceuticals, climate science, cybersecurity, and materials discovery which demonstrate the transformative reach of technology. Engages with future trajectories, commercialization, ethics, governance, and global equity. Equips readers to understand both the power and the limits of quantum computation. Designed for researchers, advanced students, engineers, and technology strategists, this volume presents quantum computing not as an abstract scientific curiosity, but as a structured computational discipline grounded in qubits, unitary gates, circuit architectures, interference engineering, and algorithmic complexity. It is an essential reference for anyone seeking to navigate the technical depth, interdisciplinary scope, and strategic significance of quantum searching and optimization in the coming computational era.

items.title: Quantum Dot‐Based Color Conversion Layers for Displays, Lighting, and Emerging Technologies
items.abstract: Quantum dot-based color conversion layers (QD-CCLs) have emerged as key spectral-engineering platforms for next-generation optoelectronic systems, enabling precise control of light emission through efficient photon conversion. Owing to their high photoluminescence quantum yield, narrow emission linewidth, and size-tunable bandgaps, quantum dots (QDs) offer significant advantages over conventional phosphors for lighting and display applications. Beyond material properties, QD-CCL performance is governed by the interplay between material photophysics, optical design, and structural architecture. This review provides a unified perspective on QD-CCLs by integrating advances across QD materials (Cd-based, perovskite, and heavy-metal-free systems), device architectures, and mechanically deformable platforms. Particular emphasis is placed on optical management strategies that control photon absorption, reabsorption, and light extraction, as well as structural approaches that enhance conversion efficiency and suppress excitation-light leakage. Emerging design considerations in flexible and stretchable systems are also discussed, highlighting the coupling between mechanical deformation and optical performance. Beyond conventional lighting and displays, QD-CCLs are further explored as functional photonic interfaces in applications such as visible light communication and human-machine interfaces. By bridging materials, optics, and device engineering, this review establishes a design framework for QD-CCLs and outlines future directions toward multifunctional photonic systems.

items.title: Predictive Inventory Allocation Models for Regional Pandemic Preparedness Networks
items.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed a structural weakness in healthcare supply chains: inventory is managed facility by facility, which limits regional visibility of local needs, available stock and opportunities to redistribute it. Prior research has examined demand forecasting, inventory optimization, emergency logistics and the ethics of resource allocation, but few studies integrate these streams in a single regional, rolling-horizon decision architecture that includes governance. This conceptual and methodological paper addresses that gap by proposing a predictive inventory allocation framework for regional pandemic preparedness. The framework comprises seven operational capabilities (uncertainty-adjusted demand forecasting, regional inventory visibility, multi-objective allocation, equity safeguarding, inventory pooling, interfacility redistribution and rolling-horizon adaptation), organized in four layers and coordinated by one governance mechanism. It serves six objectives: shortage mitigation, service continuity, distribution efficiency, allocation stability, reserve preservation and protection of vulnerable facilities and populations. Drawing on systems theory, dynamic capabilities theory, resource dependence theory, and distributive and procedural justice theory, we develop four propositions that link regional visibility, coordination, need-based allocation and reserve-protected redistribution to measurable outcomes, together with indicators and moderators. A formal multi-objective model is specified, and a stylized example with four hypothetical hospitals illustrates its mechanics against three baseline allocation rules. The framework has not been empirically validated; a three-phase validation strategy is outlined. The contribution is a theoretically grounded and operationally specified architecture that links forecasting, equity-aware allocation and conditional redistribution.
items.venue: Journal of Engineering Research and Sciences

items.title: Physics-Based Gate Stack Optimisation of p-GaN/AlGaN/GaN HEMTs for Balanced Threshold Voltage and On-Resistance
items.abstract: Abstract In this article, the gate-stack design space of p-GaN/AlGaN/GaN HEMTs (high electron mobility transistors) is explored to achieve a balanced threshold voltage (V T ) and on-resistance (R on ). Physics-based analytical models for V T and R on are validated against experimental data and subsequently employed for a 10,000-point design-space exploration encompassing variations in p-GaN doping concentration, Schottky built-in potential, AlGaN thickness, and Al mole fraction. While a high V T is essential for robust enhancement-mode operation and adequate gate-noise immunity, a low R on is required to minimize conduction losses. The study reveals the inherent trade-off between V T and R on , and identifies an optimum gate-stack design region that balances these competing requirements. Based on the explored design space, practical design guidelines are established to maintain V T within the range of 1.7–2.2 V while achieving the lowest possible R on under process-induced variations of gate-stack parameters.

items.title: Physical AI: IoT, Sensory Input, Data Processing, and Reasoning
items.abstract: Physical artificial intelligence (Physical AI), also referred to as embodied AI or intelligent cyber-physical systems, represents the convergence of AI, robotics, Internet of Things (IoT), edge computing, autonomous systems, and advanced sensing technologies. Unlike purely digital AI systems that operate within virtual information environments, Physical AI systems perceive, reason, and act within dynamic physical environments through continuous interaction with the real world. These systems integrate multimodal sensing, distributed computation, contextual reasoning, and autonomous actuation to support adaptive and intelligent behavior across healthcare, manufacturing, transportation, smart cities, defense, and industrial automation. The emergence of Physical AI has been accelerated by advances in deep learning, edge AI, 5G/6G communication, neuromorphic computing, digital twins, and multimodal foundation models. IoT infrastructures provide the distributed sensing and communication backbone required for real-time environmental awareness, while sophisticated data processing pipelines and reasoning engines enable autonomous decision-making under uncertainty. This chapter provides a detailed examination of the technological foundations underpinning Physical AI with particular emphasis on IoT architectures, sensory input systems, multimodal perception, data processing pipelines, reasoning mechanisms, and embodied cognition. The discussion explores enabling technologies, architectural models, healthcare applications, computational frameworks, and emerging research directions including explainable embodied AI, digital twins, adaptive robotics, and foundation models for cyber-physical systems.

items.title: Phase-geometric classification of memristor hysteresis loops via self-crossings
items.abstract: Memristive devices have revolutionized non-volatile memory and neuromorphic computing, yet the geometry of their hysteresis loops -- in particular, the occurrence and robustness of multiple self-crossings -- remains poorly understood. Here we introduce a topological and algebraic framework that treats the number of transverse self-intersections of a memristor hysteresis loop as a robust integer-valued invariant. Drawing on differential topology, singularity theory, and cusp catastrophe, we employ discriminants and resultants to stratify the six-dimensional parameter space. This approach partitions the parameter space into structurally stable regions separated by explicitly computable catastrophe surfaces. We demonstrate that the crossing number remains strictly invariant under continuous deformations and changes only at self-tangencies or cusp singularities, thereby providing a complete classification of all multi-lobed hysteresis behaviors. These insights bridge device physics with modern singularity theory and suggest a clear roadmap for exploiting higher-order memory effects in next-generation electronics and brain-inspired hardware.

items.title: Optimization of Montgomery Multiplication via MATLAB HDL Coder for FPGA Implementation
items.abstract: Abstract Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) are essential for implementing and verifying complex computational algorithms. This paper is part of a series of research aimed at enabling developers to use FPGAs as an embedded system without prior knowledge of digital design engineering. This paper discusses minimizing combinatorial delay that exists in complex algorithm computation using a software pipeline. How to implement this pipeline using a MATLAB HDL Coder algorithm. A comparison of the implementation of the complex Montgomery Multiplication Algorithm, with and without a pipeline, is performed on the same Virtex-7 platform. The Experiment shows a 56.5\% improvement in the maximum frequency, 128.810 MHz. Although the utilization of slice registers increased by 1\%, the number of slice-LUTs increased by 13\%, the number of fully used LUT-FF pairs increased by 7\%, and memory usage remained constant, demonstrating that high-level optimizations can produce hardware performance that typically requires expert-level manual RTL design.

items.title: Observability Aware Federation Learning in Fog-IoT Systems Round Time and runtime Metrics Analysis through iFogSim-Based implementation
items.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables the training of models on distributed Internet of Things (IoT) and localization of them. Practically, Fog-IoT system More infrastructure differences exist in infrastructure, including differences in communication lag times, differences in access to fog resources, and differences in client activity that introduce much uncertainty in their effects on the length of the federation rounds, and the available literature is more focused on the effect of infrastructure dynamics on the execution of learning behavior than on how to optimally execute the federation process itself. This research aims to design an observability-enabled federated learning framework used to examine how varying conditions in heterogeneous Fog-IoT infrastructure affect the performance of federated learning. The proposed framework incorporates TensorFlow-enabled federated learning with the iFogSim2-based Fog-IoT simulation in order to capture heterogeneous devices, variability in communication, constraints in fog resources, as well as passive telemetry from training, systems, and behavioral layers. Experiments shown that communication latency and constrained fog resources greatly affect the execution of federated learning, since the time needed to complete each round is increased from 4.2-5.3 s in baseline conditions to 6.1-8.8 s in high latency conditions and 5.3-7.9 s in constrained fog resources. In addition, increased utilization of fog resources from 30% to 90% causes the ratio of stragglers to increase from 0.08 to 0.38. This set of findings proves that the heterogeneity of infrastructure is among the major predictors of FL performance and shows the viability of calculating observability to Fog-IoT implementation.
items.venue: International Journal of Innovation and Technology Management

items.title: Next-Generation Interconnect Design
items.abstract: Continuous scaling of the complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) technology has exacerbated the power-delay bottlenecks in global on-chip interconnects, posing critical challenges in achieving energy-efficient and high-speed data transmission. This chapter explores a spectrum of innovative solutions to mitigate these issues, including low-swing signaling schemes, magneto-electric (ME) effect-based receivers, and spin-torque (ST) sensor-driven interconnect frameworks. Specifically, it analyzes techniques like multi- V dd and multi- V th voltage scaling, current-mode signaling, and the advanced modified Junction (MJ) driver to achieve low dynamic and static power consumption. Furthermore, it introduces a capacitively driven interconnect architecture utilizing ME-MTJ devices for efficient signal restoration without analog amplification, and a pipelined repeater framework employing ST buffers with domain wall (DW) motion for delay optimization. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in energy efficiency and signal integrity. These hybrid architectures provide promising pathways for scalable and low-power on-chip systems. Future developments will hinge on advancements in materials, device modeling, and integration strategies for deployment in emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators and neuromorphic processors.

items.title: Neuromorphic Computing and Neuromorphic Hardware for AutoML in Zero-touch Networks: Applications and Challenges
items.abstract: Owing to the fact that future communication systems are increasing in size and complexity, Zero Touch Networks (ZTN) is going toward pervasive networks that self-configure, self-optimize, and even self-heal with minimal human action. AutoML plays a crucial role in ZTN for adaptive model selection, hyperparameter tuning and real-time decision-making under dynamic network conditions. However, the latency and energy consumption of traditional cloud-based AutoML systems at edge devices are usually not acceptable. Recently, neuromorphic computing and hardware which are based on the human brain structure and function has become a promising alternative for large scale VLSI implementation because it possesses event driven processing, extremely large scale parallelism, ultra-low power consumption. We study in this paper the integration of neuromorphic computing paradigms for ZTN in AutoML. We explore how Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) and neuromorphic accelerators can enable real-time learning, adaptive control and anomaly detection in ZTNs. Core use cases such as self-heal network, 240 intelligent traffic optimization, predictive maintenance and edge driven autonomous orchestration are also considered. Moreover, it also reports some critical technical challenges where there are no suitable training platforms for the given specific SNN-based AutoML, and hardware–software co-design restrictions which can compromise meeting a particular network demand as well as syntonic with original network infrastructure & standard benchmark availability. Possible research directions, such as hybrid neuromorphic–conventional schemes and online learning methods, are highlighted. The study shows the potential that neuromorphic accelerator-aided AutoML can provide in helping achieve ZTNs more energy-efficient, scalable and fully autonomously operable and demonstrates the necessity of inter-disciplinary collaboration to circumvent current limitations.

items.title: Memory Window Improvement in Ferroelectric Thin-Film Transistors with HfZrO2/AlN Bilayers Grown by Atomic Layer Deposition
items.abstract: Abstract This study demonstrates proximity-induced ferroelectric switching in a stacked ferroelectric film composed of fluorite-structured HfZrO2 (HZO) and wurtzite-structured AlN, which are grown by thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) and plasma-enhanced ALD (PEALD), respectively. The stacked film shows remanent polarization close to that of HZO but with a much higher coercive field, desirable for enhancing the memory window of ferroelectric thin-film transistors (FeTFTs) for storage applications. The FeTFT with a 5 nm-thick amorphous In–Ga–Zn–O (a-IGZO) channel layer, also grown by ALD, shows a memory window of ∼6.1 V, and data retention over 10 years. It also shows stable endurance cycles of ∼104. These enhancements over the single-layer HZO or stacked HZO/Al2O3 films, which show a minimal memory window of ∼0.3 V and ∼−0.3 V, respectively, are ascribed to the proximity ferroelectric effects between the soft ferroelectric HZO and hard ferroelectric AlN. These results, together with the conformal deposition of the HZO/AlN stack in high-aspect-ratio structures, demonstrate the feasibility of extending the ALD/PEALD-based Prox-FE materials platform toward three-dimensional (3D) process integration.

items.title: Mechanism of Delayed Polarization Saturation Induced by B‐Site Zr Doping for Enhancing Energy Storage Performance in Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 TiO 3 ‐ Sr 0.7 Bi 0.2 TiO 3 Ceramics
items.abstract: ABSTRACT In this work, Zr 4+ ions are introduced into the B‐site of 0.67Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 TiO 3 ‐0.33Sr 0.7 Bi 0.2 TiO 3 relaxor ferroelectric ceramics, leading to a significant improvement in energy storage performance. On one hand, Zr 4+ doping suppresses grain growth, increasing the breakdown electric field from 250 to 470 kV cm −1 . On the other hand, it tailors the phase structure by reducing the fraction of the strong polar rhombohedral phase, refines polar nanoregions (PNRs) into discrete micro‐nano polar clusters with reduced size and weakened cooperative switching, and notably alters their morphology and distribution, thereby reducing the local polarization intensity. These micro‐nano polar clusters exhibit reduced switching cooperativity under an electric field, resulting in a marked delay of polarization saturation—the electric field required to achieve a comparable polarization value is increased. Finally, the recoverable energy storage density ( W rec ) and efficiency ( η ) of the 0.67Bi 0.5 Na 0.5 Ti 0.94 Zr 0.06 O 3 ‐0.33Sr 0.7 Bi 0.2 Ti 0.94 Zr 0.06 O 3 samples are significantly improved, reaching 7.2 J cm −3 and 88.1% under 470 kV cm −1 . It also exhibits stable performance from 30–160°C, with the fluctuation of W rec lower than 5%. Moreover, it possesses a high power density of 140 MW cm −3 and an ultrafast discharge time. The proposed “delayed polarization saturation” strategy offers a new route for designing high‐performance lead‐free dielectric energy storage ceramics.

items.title: Intrinsically Self‐Assembled SrFeO x Topotactic Phase Transition Memristor
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Topotactic phase‐transition (TPT) oxide memristors contain ordered 1D oxygen‐vacancy channels (OVCs) that enable anisotropic oxygen‐ion migration and reversible brownmillerite/perovskite transition, offering a materials platform for neuromorphic computing. However, the lack of spatially predefined oxygen‐ion migration sites in conventional TPT films promotes stochastic perovskite SrFeO 3 conductive filament (CF) growth, compromising the response stability and state distinguishability required for reliable temporal signal processing. Here, a single‐component self‐assembled SrFeO x memristor with alternating vertical and horizontal superlattice‐like OVC regions is reported. Structural characterization, density functional theory calculations, and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations indicate that this intrinsic self‐assembled architecture directs oxygen‐ion migration through vertical channels while horizontal regions restrict stray out‐of‐plane transport, promoting localized CF growth. The device combines forming‐free bipolar switching, an ON/OFF ratio of ∼4.4 × 10 3 , low cycle‐to‐cycle (C2C) variation with CV(V SET )/CV(V RESET ) of 3.2%/0.6%, 16‐state retention over 10 4 s, and endurance up to 10 7 pulse cycles. Reproducible device‐to‐device (D2D) switching is obtained across 32 cells, with D2D CV(V SET )/CV(V RESET ) values of 10.1%/5.9%. Finally, the device's short‐term memory transforms temporal inputs into distinguishable states that a fixed linear readout decodes with 84.59% accuracy on a temporal classification task. This work highlights intrinsic OVC‐orientation engineering as a materials‐level strategy toward reliable single‐component TPT memristors.

items.title: Intrinsic Backflow in Heterogeneous Aquifer During Electrokinetic Remediation: A Challenge in Field‐Scale Application
items.abstract: Abstract Electrokinetics is a remediation technology applying direct‐current voltage across soil to mobilize solutes. It induces electromigration whereby ions migrate toward electrodes of opposite charge, and electroosmosis whereby water flow is engendered because of surface charges in soils. As confirmed by various experiments, electroosmosis has the advantage of mobilizing non‐ionic solutes especially in low permeability clay. We argue herein that due to subsurface heterogeneity, the upscaling of electroosmosis may not be always achievable under normal conditions, mainly because of backflow in regions outside of clay. In this study, analytical solutions derived in periodic heterogeneous system demonstrate how nonuniform electroosmosis induces local hydraulic‐head gradient and backflow. Application in standard lognormal heterogeneity system produces limited backflow due to smoothly varying zeta potential, whereas discrete high absolute zeta potential lenses generate more extensive backflow. These findings highlight the importance of spatial organization (or lacunarity), especially lens size, spacing, for applications of field‐scale electrokinetic remediation.

items.title: Interface Formation in Cadmium-Free CZTSe Solar Cells: Influence of ALD Precursor Sequence and Nominal Subcycle Ratio
items.abstract: This workbook contains eight worksheets with measurements from two champion CZTSe solar cells from the same absorber batch, one with a CdS electron transport layer and the other with a ZTO electron transport layer. For each device, the workbook includes illuminated and dark current density–voltage (J–V) curves, an external quantum efficiency (EQE) spectrum, and a reflectance spectrum. The first two rows of each worksheet identify the measured quantities and their units. J–V measurements were performed at 25 °C, scanning from reverse to forward bias. Illuminated curves were recorded under simulated AM1.5G illumination (100 mW cm⁻²). Current density was normalized to the total cell area of 0.087 cm². Photocurrent is reported as positive at short circuit. In all four J–V worksheets, the measured current density reaches a lower limit of approximately −120.7 mA cm⁻² at high forward bias.

items.title: Integration of AI/ML Techniques in VLSI Design
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are among the emerging technologies that will impact a wide range of electronics design and manufacturing. This chapter deals with the essentials in terms of novel devices, circuits, and architectures (system-on chip (SoC) and network-on-chip (NoC)). Here, we elucidate the AI-ML design techniques for optimizing digital and analog integrated circuits (ICs). This chapter also details the various stages of AI-ML-based design ICs with case studies.

items.title: Hydrogen-Mediated, Voltage-Tunable Modulation of the Metal–Insulator Transition in SmNiO3 at Room Temperature
items.abstract: The broad interest in proton (or hydrogen) doping of strongly correlated oxides, such as perovskite nickelates (RNiO3), stems from their extraordinary modulation of electronic properties that lead to dramatic changes in electrical resistivity. However, the mechanism by which this occurs is not well understood. In this work, in situ X-ray diffraction (XRD), neutron reflectivity (NR), and electrical measurements are utilized to probe the mechanism for a voltage-tunable metal-insulator transition in SmNiO3 (SNO) thin films and memristive devices in hydrogen-rich environments. The SNO films show an immediate expansion of the c-axis lattice parameter at room temperature upon hydrogen exposure, which saturates at a massive value of ∼8%. NR measurements confirm for the first time that this expansion arises from hydrogen incorporation at a ratio of 1:4. In situ current-voltage (IV) measurements reveal that hydrogenation induces a dramatic resistivity change of more than three orders of magnitude, and the protonated Pt/SNO device exhibits a bipolar resistive switching (RS) hysteresis. The RS effects in this system arise from an interfacial Schottky barrier height modulation where proton migration at the Pt/SNO interface and within the SNO film serves as the main driver for the analog IV hysteresis. The dynamics of hydrogen incorporation and desorption are systematically studied in the Pt/SNO device with temperature-dependent electrical characterizations and Avrami model. These results for the first time demonstrate the mechanism by which hydrogen drives electronic transitions in SmNiO3 and, mediated by voltage control, can be used to manipulate the electronic character of neuromorphic devices.

items.title: Hybrid CMOS–MJT Circuits for High-Performance CIM Architecture
items.abstract: The rising ubiquitous demand for artificial intelligence (AI), deep learning, Internet of Things (IoT), big data applications, etc., has been backed at both the software and hardware levels. At the software level, algorithms such as Monte Carlo tree search, convolutional neural networks, ResNet, and EfficientNet are being used; meanwhile, at the hardware level, high-performance, energy-efficient graphics processing units (GPUs) such as GeForce RTX 50 series support the implementation of these applications. The achievement at the hardware level is underpinned by the relentless advancement in fabrication technologies such as progressive downscaling of complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) technology and the introduction of advanced transistor architectures such as Fin field-effect transistors (FinFETs) [ 1 , 2 ] and carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNTFETs) [ 3 , 4 ], which offer improved power efficiency with high performance in modern integrated circuits (ICs). A notable example is Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which, in 2025, successfully fabricated approximately 92 billion FinFETs for NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU using the 5-nm process technology. Despite these achievements, continued downscaling faces formidable challenges as transistor dimensions approach a few atomic layers. At such scales, quantum mechanical effects—especially quantum tunneling—become prominent, leading to increased leakage currents and elevated standby power dissipation [ 5–8 ]. This is particularly critical in volatile memory systems, where continuous power is required to retain stored information. Concurrently, the rise in operating frequencies contributes to higher dynamic power dissipation and escalates heat generation to levels nearing thermal design limits. Furthermore, as CMOS technology scales down, global interconnects become disproportionately longer relative to transistor dimensions. This results in additional dynamic power consumption and signal propagation delays [ 9 ], thereby compounding the overall power challenges in volatile memory systems. Let’s take an example of memory hierarchy as shown in Figure 10.1 . The on-chip cache levels, such as L1 and L2, primarily utilize static random-access memory (SRAM). Although SRAM offers high-speed performance, it suffers from significant standby power consumption due to subthreshold leakage currents. On the other hand, L3 and L4 cache levels, often implemented using dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), are constrained by the volatility of stored charge and require frequent refresh operations, leading to increased power demand.

items.title: High-Reliability Ultrascaled IGZO FETs for Multibit 2T0C DRAM toward Monolithic 3D Integration of an AI Accelerator
items.abstract: Abstract The continued scaling of silicon-based dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) slows down due to increased process complexity and reduced storage capacitance. Oxide semiconductors (OS), represented by InGaZnOx (IGZO), offer an attractive alternative owing to their ultralow leakage and low thermal budget, making them promising candidates for next-generation DRAM as well as monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) architectures. However, realizing IGZO devices with well-balanced overall performance, including high performance and high reliability under ultrascaled dimensions, remains challenging. Here, we report ultrascaled IGZO field-effect transistors (FETs) fabricated using an optimized O2 plasma-enhanced atomic-layer deposition (PE-ALD) process. The IGZO FETs deliver state-of-the-art performance, including an on-state current (Ion) of 785 μA/μm at a drain voltage of 0.5 V and a transconductance (gm) of 620 μS/μm at a drain voltage of 1.0 V alongside a contact resistance (Rc) of 164.5 Ω·μm with positive threshold voltage (Vth). Reliability degradation is effectively suppressed, with bias-temperature instability (BTI) down to 8 mV even at extremely scaled contact length (Lc) of 50 nm. Leveraging these optimized devices, we further demonstrated a scaled two-transistor-zero-capacitor (2T0C) DRAM capable of up to 6-bit per cell, long data retention over 4000 s, and write time down to 10 ns. We proposed an M3D-DRAM architecture with vertically stacked multilayer embedded memory for artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators, achieving 77× faster weight loading and 9.6× lower energy consumption compared with mature high-bandwidth memory (HBM) counterpart, while maintaining graphics processing units (GPU)-equivalent inference accuracy of 92.25%. This work demonstrates an effective approach for the co-optimization of performance and reliability in ultrascaled IGZO FETs, providing critical foundation for next-generation DRAM and M3D applications.

items.title: High-Performance Dual-Source Vertical TFET Design Using Gate Work Function Engineering and Fully Depleted SOI Substrate
items.abstract: In order to overcome short-channel effects and enhance input characteristics, such as obtaining a steeper subthreshold slope, lower threshold voltage, and a higher Ion/Ioff ratio, devices like tunnel field-effect transistors (TFETs) are being considered as alternatives to traditional metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) field effect transistors (MOSFETs). The band-to-band tunneling (BTBT) mechanism, which is in charge of the drain-to-source current, is the foundation of the TFET’s operation. This work proposes and uses technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations to study an optimally designed dual-source vertical tunnel field-effect transistor (VTFET). The VTFET structure increases the device’s scalability by arranging the source, channel, and drain vertically. The switching mechanism of TFETs, which depends on quantum tunneling through a potential barrier instead of thermionic emission over the barrier as seen in conventional MOSFETs, is one of their main advantages. The creation of a two-dimensional model for a single-drain, dual-source n-type VTFET is the main contribution of this work. The device’s performance is greatly enhanced by the addition of an ultra-thin channel between the drain and gate regions; numerical simulations show an average subthreshold slope of 3.36 mV/decade and a minimum threshold voltage (VT) of 0.135 V. The 2D Synopsys TCAD tool has been used to analyze the effects of changes in channel thickness, source height, drain doping, source doping, temperature, and gate work function. High ON current and low OFF current have been recorded as https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> 1.48 × 10 − 4 A / m and https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> 6.74 × 10 − 13 A / m , respectively, with ION/IOFF current ratio in the order of https://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"> 10 8 − 10 9 .

items.title: High landing energy SEM dimensional metrology for High NA EUVL
items.abstract: BackgroundRecently, High Numerical Aperture Extreme Ultraviolet Lithography (High-NA EUVL) started delivering its first wafers, showing its potential by printing 18 and 16 nm pitch line/space. However, as feature sizes drop below 10 nm, questions are raised on the ability of the current metrology procedures and tools to properly characterize such small targets. In particular, it is critical to assess the impact of limited spatial resolution and identify possible ways forward.AimA high-resolution, low damage strategy based on high-landing energy (LE) is proposed.ApproachHigh-LE setting (15 keV) and standard low LE (500 eV) best-known methods are compared using both rigorous simulation and experiments. The comparison is performed for metal oxide resist (MOR) as well as for chemical amplified resist, after development inspection (ADI), and after etch inspection (AEI).ResultsOur results indicated that the 15 keV setting provides 3× better resolution and less ADI damage as compared with the 500 eV setting. AEI damages, throughput, and precision are comparable.ConclusionsUsing high LE provides the needed resolution for High-NA EUVL, with similar or better impact on damages compared with low LE.
items.venue: Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning Materials and Metrology

items.title: HfOx Seed-Layer Functionalization of MoS2 for Top-Gated HZO FeFETs
items.abstract: Two-dimensional MoS2 is a promising channel material for beyond-silicon memory devices, but its chemically inert van der Waals surface makes the direct atomic layer deposition (ALD) of continuous high-k and ferroelectric gate stacks highly challenging in technologically relevant top-gate architectures. Here, we demonstrate an ultrathin sputtered HfOx seed layer as a scalable surface-functionalization strategy enabling conventional H2O-based ALD of ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) on near-monolayer MOCVD-grown MoS2. The HfOx seed layer strongly improves HZO uniformity, while Raman spectroscopy and XPS indicate no significant structural degradation and only limited oxidation of the ultrathin MoS2 channel. Using this seed-assisted integration scheme, we realize top-gate MoS2 FeFETs with low gate leakage currents, efficient channel modulation, and nonvolatile memory operation. These results establish sputtered HfOx seed-layer functionalization as an effective route for scalable integration of ferroelectric HZO with two-dimensional MoS2 channels in top-gate memory devices.

items.title: Hardware Architecture-Driven Efficiency Improvement of Sorption-Based Atmospheric Water Harvesting Using Model-Based Systems Engineering and SysML
items.abstract: Sorption-based atmospheric water harvesting (SAWH) performance depends on the integration of heat and mass transfer, condensation, and cycle operation, yet improvements in individual components do not necessarily translate into higher net water production or lower energy consumption. This study develops a requirements-driven framework using model-based systems engineering (MBSE) and the Systems Modeling Language (SysML) to connect SAWH performance objectives with operating strategies, hardware architecture, and verification planning. With the sorbent bed treated as a black box, the framework establishes traceability across requirements, behavioral and structural models, and a three-dimensional design. The resulting architecture addresses coupled losses associated with airflow distribution, thermal interaction, mode switching, vapor transport, and condensate collection. The design analysis makes explicit the trade-offs between loss reduction, auxiliary energy demand, cycle duration, and operational complexity, providing the rationale for selecting a baseline configuration. A coupled-bed extension is also proposed to reuse adsorption exhaust for condenser cooling and share bed-cooling functions between alternating modules. The principal contribution is a systematic connection between performance requirements, physical design choices, and the measurements needed to evaluate them, providing a basis for prototype development and comparison of alternative SAWH configurations.

items.title: Generating Linguistically Diverse and Semantically Faithful Patient Reports
items.abstract: To protect patient privacy, medical models are frequently trained on synthetic datasets. Focusing on 13 clinical attributes commonly found in breast cancer records, we propose a synthetic data generation framework in which each generated sample is a data-report pair: the structured data capture the 13 attributes of interest, while the accompanying (French) text simulates a corresponding breast cancer pathology report. Data privacy and coverage are obtained by generating the structured data using a tabular data synthesiser. In this work, we focus on enhancing the diversity and quality of the generated texts through a combination of datadriven knowledge distillation, data filtering and data combination. Our findings suggest that the quality of the training data used for the student model outweighs its quantity; that combining data from multiple teachers helps improve performance; and that a compact model (Mistral 7B) can match the zero-shot Information Extraction performance of a significantly larger model (MedGemma 27B) when fine-tuned on high-quality synthetic data 1 .

items.title: GUS - Static Skyrmion Array Electromagnetic Evanescent Wave General Unified Storage Architecture
items.abstract: What if a high-capacity, massively parallel non‑volatile storage substrate built upon static skyrmion lattices could feed enormous weight snapshots and continuous training checkpoints for large‑scale AI systems, without the bandwidth and latency bottlenecks that plague conventional storage hierarchies? The GUS architecture is a standalone pure storage framework engineered to serve as the dedicated persistent memory tier for the Wavon field‑based generalized in‑memory computing stack. It delivers stable topological long‑term archiving and near‑field ultra‑fast register resources tailored for post‑silicon AI hardware, where all interlayer signal coupling relies on 20–80 GHz microwave evanescent eigenstates shaped by static magnetic skyrmion boundary conditions. The system adopts three‑dimensional stacked nanostructures bounded strictly by subwavelength near‑field geometry. The lattice spacing 𝐷, effective action radius 𝑅 of the static skyrmion electromagnetic evanescent mode, and vertical interlayer near‑field gap ℎ satisfy ℎ ≤ 𝑅 < 𝐷/2 and ℎ ≤ 𝐷/3. MEPS, the Microwave Evanescent Pattern of Skyrmion, represents the coupled eigenstate ensemble formed by the magnetic topological lattice and its full induced evanescent field spectrum, distinguishable from isolated magnetic skyrmions, optical skyrmions and exciton skyrmions. A top‑layer nanogrid differential GWD wavefield detector enables contactless, non‑destructive, globally parallel near‑field sampling and electrical readout, capable of streaming immense volumes of model parameters simultaneously. Write, retention and read pathways are fully decoupled at the physical layer. The fabrication pipeline is compatible with the 28 nm ultraviolet nanoimprint co‑integration and vacuum microcavity stacking process shared with Wavon. GUS is purpose‑built to host giant transformer weight banks, iterative training checkpoints and fixed topological axiom parameters. It segregates low‑speed topological rewrite events from high‑speed field computation, removing the classic storage wall and forming a matched two‑component hardware ecosystem designed for sustained, large‑capacity field‑state generalized in‑memory computing. storage wall, memory wall, power wall, RC delay, data movement bottleneck, flash, solid state drive, HBM, DDR, non-volatile memory, storage latency, write endurance, lithography, nanoimprint lithography, 3D stacked memory, magnetic skyrmion, topological storage, post-Moore, AI training
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Field-compatible tissue cryopreservation enables delayed endothelial cell culture
items.abstract: Decades of biomedical research have developed robust tools in molecular and cell biology, including cell culture systems, for model vertebrate species. Logistical constraints associated with remote fieldwork limit the application of these techniques to non-model species. Traditionally, cell culture requires tissue collection from live or very recently deceased animals, followed by immediate sterile processing and cell isolation, but these requirements are often impractical in field settings. To address this limitation, we developed a field-compatible method to cryopreserve arterial tissue from pinnipeds for delayed endothelial cell isolation. Grey seal placentae were opportunistically collected, and arteries were preserved using benchtop blunt dissection and a portable ​​-80 °C freezer with a standard cell freezing medium. Samples were held in a portable ​-80 °C freezer for ~ 2 months before transfer to LN 2 vapor storage for ~ 1 month, followed by endothelial cell isolation. Cells isolated from cryopreserved arteries are phenotypically endothelial, proliferate in culture and are the first endothelial cell cultures derived from grey seals. Grey seal endothelial cells respire after culture expansion, and ATP production rates are ~ 1.5×​​ greater than those in freshly derived endothelial cell cultures from a related species, though the relative contributions of OXPHOS and glycolysis were comparable between cell preparations. This method is practical for field researchers and supports the generation of primary cell cultures weeks-to-months after initial tissue collection with minimal resources, strengthening the ability to investigate the cellular basis of physiological phenomena in the natural world.

items.title: Ferroionic‐Assisted, Charge‐Driven Polymorphic Phase Engineering for Multilevel Memristive Devices
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Memristive device operation can arise from diverse microscopic mechanisms, including charge polarization and trapping, magnetic ordering, ionic migration, and structural phase transitions. Among these, crystalline–crystalline phase transitions in polymorphic materials offer a unique platform for nonvolatile resistance modulation but are often hindered by large energy barriers and limited endurance. Here, we demonstrate a multimodal, charge‐driven phase modulation in an atomically thin polymorphic material, Mo 0.92 W 0.08 Te 2 , enabled by electrostatic coupling to a ferroionic substrate, CuInP 2 S 6 .
