The polymorphic channel exhibits reversible switching between semiconducting and metallic phases via electrostatically accumulated charges, reflecting the intrinsically low energy barrier between its competing polymorphs. Integration with the ferroionic substrate enables spatially localized, nonvolatile charge accumulation in the channel, which provides distinct, programmable phase‐control pathways under a two‐terminal bias configuration. The phase‐induced resistance modulation through field‐driven ionic processes is governed by the evolution of a phase‐dependent Schottky junction at the electrode–channel interface, yielding multiple, stable conductance states under pulsed electrical excitation. Leveraging these experimentally derived synaptic characteristics, we conducted an MNIST inference simulation with a convolutional neural network, achieving 98.45% accuracy. This ferroionic‐assisted phase‐engineering strategy offers new opportunities beyond traditional phase‐change devices for adaptive electronic and neuromorphic material platforms.

items.title: Efficient Spiking Neural Networks with Autapse-Enhanced Temporal Coding?
items.abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have emerged as a promising energy-efficient paradigm for multimedia processing. Within SNNs, temporal coding conveys information through spike firing time, leading to sparser spike activity than in rate coding SNNs. While this sparsity improves computational efficiency, it also limits the representational capacity of temporal coding SNNs. In this work, we propose the Last-Spike-Modulated Spike Response Model (LSM-SRM), a self-connected spiking neuron for temporal coding SNNs that integrates neuron's last spike firing time inspired by autapse in biology. This model adaptively modulates excitability and improves the utilization of historical information, consequently enhancing neuronal dynamics and network's representation. To address the history-dependent optimization challenge posed by autapse, we introduce a counting spike-timing-dependent plasticity rule as an event-driven backward approximation by decomposing post-synaptic current into the spike count term and average temporal decay factor. Extensive experiments on both static and neuromorphic tasks demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our method. For example, on CIFAR100 and DVSGesture datasets, our method increases sparse spike activity by 1.27% and 2.48% while improving performance by 2.06% and 1.04%, respectively. Additionally, we are the first to report the performance of directly trained temporal coding SNNs on larger-scale Tiny ImageNet dataset, highlighting the potential of efficient temporal coding SNNs.
items.venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)

items.title: Effect of annealing on the properties of TiO2 film prepared by atom layer deposition
items.abstract: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) TiO₂ thin films are widely used in optoelectronics, photocatalysis, and biomedical applications. However, their intrinsic absorption and defect-induced absorption limit their application in high-power laser optics. Annealing is an important post-treatment method to modulate the optical properties and reduce absorption. In this work, ALD-TiO₂ thin films were annealed in O₂ atmosphere at different temperatures. The effects of annealing temperature on the optical constants, surface morphology, crystal structure, and impurity states were systematically investigated using spectroscopic ellipsometry, atomic force microscopy (AFM), X-ray diffraction(XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy(FTIR), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). This work provides theoretical and experimental guidance for the preparation of low-absorption, high laser-damage-resistant ALD-TiO₂ optical films through post-annealing treatment.

items.title: EUV reticle defect disposition in fab using comprehensive wafer SEM analysis
items.abstract: Reticle defect disposition in wafer fab remains a critical challenge for extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUVL). Conventional approaches in the mask-shop rely on aerial image measurement system (AIMSTM) or mask SEM-based aerial image simulations (S2A). In this work, we present an alternative wafer-level, SEM image-based approach that enables dispositioning questionable defects directly within wafer fab manufacturing environments. Mask defects are evaluated through direct wafer printing and subsequent automated analysis using the KLA’s Wafer SEM Analysis (WSA) software to detect and confirm criticality of the defect originating from the mask. WSA leverages multiple SEM views of wafer patterns and performs critical dimension (CD) error and edge placement error (EPE) measurements to reliably identify, characterize, and confirm printed defects attributable to reticle imperfections. This analysis establishes a wafer‑level ground truth, reducing operator‑dependent judgment when distinguishing nuisance from real wafer print signatures. This methodology is developed and calibrated using data collected from EUV programmed defect masks (PDM), and then validated from wafer product data, demonstrating that WSA can consistently capture both critical and marginal printable defects across multiple test views while effectively separating non‑printing nuisance defects. WSA results are then exported to KLA’s KlearViewTM data management system where these are correlated with mask inspection and Reticle Analyzer™ data. This integration enables side-by-side comparison of mask-level inspection data and wafer-level print evidence within a single platform, providing robust benchmark for defect source analysis (DSA) in production. The workflow offers a systematic, consistent, and cost-effective solution for EUV mask defect qualification in high-volume manufacturing environments.

items.title: Diamond nitrogen-vacancy center temperature sensing technology
items.abstract: Diamond nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers are powerful quantum sensing units that address the drawbacks of traditional micro and nanoscale thermometry. This paper systematically summarizes three representative NV center-based temperature sensing technologies and their latest research progress. The ODMR method based on zero-field splitting is the most widely adopted scheme, and its detection sensitivity is improved by enhancing fluorescence collection efficiency and prolonging spin coherence time. The all-optical thermometry using the zero-phonon line requires no microwave equipment, which makes it well-suited for long-term and non-invasive measurement in biological environments. The magnetic induction-based indirect method converts temperature fluctuations into magnetic field signals, enabling extremely high detection sensitivity. This work compares their system complexity, measuring performance and applicable scenarios. At present, the large-scale application of NV center thermometry is restricted by multi-physical field interference, technical barriers to on-chip integration and bottlenecks in material parameter optimization. In the future, combining novel functional materials, micro-nano machining and integrated photonics will help develop high-performance composite sensors. Optimized quantum control and advanced packaging technologies will also promote the chip and array design of sensing devices.

items.title: Design of Compact Energy-Efficient Ternary SRAM Cells
items.abstract: This chapter presents the design and evaluation of compact, energy-efficient ternary static random-access memory (SRAM) cells using carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNFETs), focusing on their application in modern Internet of Things (IoT) and embedded systems. Ternary logic offers a promising alternative to traditional binary logic by reducing circuit complexity and power consumption. Four different ternary SRAM architectures (TSRAM0–TSRAM4) are explored, with emphasis on read-disturb-free operation, delay reduction, and improved power-delay product (PDP). The designs are implemented and simulated using the Stanford 32nm CNFET model in the High Performance Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis (HSPICE) environment. Analytical models are presented to evaluate power and current characteristics. Among all the designs, TSRAM4 demonstrates superior performance in terms of reduced delay, low PDP, and better thermal stability. Static and dynamic noise margins, as well as device-level parameters like carbon nanotube (CNT) count and channel length, are analyzed to confirm the robustness of the proposed architectures. The results suggest that CNFET-based ternary SRAMs, particularly TSRAM4, are strong candidates for future low-power, high-performance memory solutions in nanoscale very large-scale integration (VLSI) systems.

items.title: Design Optimization of Advanced FPGA Architectures Using Timing Closure Techniques
items.abstract: Field-programmable gate array (FPGA) designs with control signals have utilized maximum resources, which results in higher power and lower achievable clock frequency. Reset is one of the most common control signals in any digital design, having a direct impact on design parameters like maximum clock frequency, area, and power. The main significance of reset usage in FPGA design is that it makes an impact on area, routing, and timing closure. For achieving better timing optimization, the design should be converted from asynchronous resets to synchronous resets. In this chapter, we propose FPGA implementation of a 16-bit multiplier using the pipeline register concept using different approaches:the first approach is implemented using the asynchronous reset and synchronous reset concept; then next-generation approaches are implemented with synchronous reset with global buffer (GBUF), synchronous reset with the selection of power optimization option in a mixed mode clock manager (MMCM) IP, and synchronous reset with the selection of Jitter optimization option in MMCM IP. These designs are implemented and analyzed using Xilinx Vivado Design Suite software. The proposed designs are analyzed in terms of data required time, data arrival time, slack, total delay, high fanout, total power, and clock uncertainty with anoperating clock frequency of 100MHz and clock period 10ns. It is observed that the design with synchronous reset gives more positive slack compared to the design with asynchronous reset. Positive slack is further optimized using synchronous reset with GBUF design. The total delay of synchronous reset with GBUF design is less than that of synchronous reset without GBUF design. The total power consumption of synchronous reset with MMCM design is lesser than that of synchronous reset without MMCM design.

items.title: Deep learning-augmented ADC: a hybrid approach to automatic defect classification for EUV masks inspected with DUV optics
items.abstract: Extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography is central to advanced semiconductor manufacturing, but the high cost of actinic inspection necessitates the continued use of deep ultraviolet (DUV) optics. However, the resolution gap between DUV imaging and EUV feature sizes introduces significant challenges. DUV optics struggle to resolve sub-resolution fine patterns, making it difficult to distinguish signals caused by factors such as alignment errors or slight focus deviations from actual defect signals. These optical limitations generate an overwhelming number of false defects, resulting in excessive post inspection review effort and creating a critical manual review bottleneck. To address this, we present a novel deep learning–augmented hybrid Automatic Defect Classification (ADC) framework within the Calibre® DefectClassify tool, augmenting a production-proven rule-based solution with deep learning models. The deterministic rule-based engine enforces strict guardrails for high-contrast, high-severity “killer defects”. Meanwhile, the machine learning models resolve high-dimensional, low signal-to-noise ambiguities unique to DUV-based EUV inspections. These ambiguities include dummy pattern noise, focus variation, and contrast-induced artifacts. Validation on high-volume unseen dataset demonstrates this hybrid ADC framework achieves > 90% False-to-False (F2F) accuracy, substantially reducing manual review workload. Crucially, it maintains a zero killer-defect miss rate with 100% Real-to-Real (R2R) accuracy, providing a highly reliable and scalable inspection strategy for high-volume EUV mask manufacturing.

items.title: Dataset supporting thesis titled: "Exploring temporal dynamics of TiOx-based memristors for optimised robustness in neuromorphic computing"
items.abstract: Dataset used for thesis figures in UoS thesis titled: "Exploring temporal dynamics of TiOx-based memristors for optimised robustness in neuromorphic computing"

items.title: Continuous measurement of oxygen consumption rate in hypoxic conditions with adherent cells using an oxygen-sensitive optode
items.abstract: Cellular oxygen consumption rate (OCR) is a widely used readout of mitochondrial respiration and oxidative metabolism. However, many OCR assay workflows are limited by short assay durations, expensive specialized instrumentation, and reduced flexibility under controlled low-oxygen conditions. Here, we describe an in-incubator method for continuous, non-disruptive OCR measurement in adherent cell cultures using the PreSens OxoDish optical oxygen-sensing system. OCR is estimated by applying the steady-state solution of Fick's law to pericellular oxygen measurements acquired at well bottoms. This approach enables OCR monitoring over several hours to 24 hours without removing plates from a standard cell-culture incubator. Using MCF-7 breast cancer cells cultured in DMEM, we calculated basal OCR values of 20.07-32.79 amol cell-1s-1, similar to published values obtained using other methods. We also demonstrate a respiration profiling approach analogous to SeahorseXF Mito Stress Tests by quantifying OCR in parallel wells exposed to oligomycin, FCCP, or antimycin A/rotenone. Importantly, we demonstrate that the method remains functional under hypoxia (1.5% O2) without modification. Benchmarking the PreSens system against the SeahorseXF yielded values within the expected reported range. The approach we describe provides an accessible option for continuous OCR measurements in adherent cell cultures under a range of oxygen levels.

items.title: Comments on a 2026 stochastic subgradient method for VLSI placement: Exact formula checks and questions about the stochastic convergence argument
items.abstract: This independent technical note examines Yue, Dai and Yu, “An efficient stochastic subgradient method for the global placement problem in very large-scale integration circuits,” Journal of Global Optimization 95 (2026), 863–892, DOI: 10.1007/s10898-026-01619-4. It corrects a displayed ReLU identity, identifies an undefined component-wise quotient under a literal reading of the adaptive-penalty rules, and discusses discrepancies between the printed algorithm and analyzed recurrence. It examines filtration and conditional-expectation issues and provides a two-cell example refuting a covariance-sign inference in the convergence proof. This is not a counterexample to the main convergence theorem, and it does not establish that the numerical experiments are invalid. This deposit preserves the original note dated 3 November 2026 and its accompanying LaTeX source and exact-arithmetic Python script, initially prepared for private scholarly correspondence and now made public. References to private circulation in the PDF describe its original context. No private correspondence is included. This is an independent technical note, not a journal-issued corrigendum or an endorsement by the original authors. AI assistance and responsibility: An OpenAI language model was used for English improvement and numerical checks, and assisted with drafting and mathematical analysis, including development of counterexamples and draft arguments. The author bears full responsibility for the construction and verification of counterexamples, lemmas and propositions, all proofs and conclusions, and the final wording and mathematical correctness of the manuscript.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Code and data for "Multiscale warming scaling rates of worst-case precipitation: A typhoon storyline approach"
items.abstract: This record contains the principal analysis code, selected processed WRF outputs, actual applied pseudo-global-warming (PGW) perturbations, and representative WRF/WPS settings supporting the accompanying study of Typhoon Hagibis. The analyses cover basin precipitation maxima and warming scaling across 1–48-hour durations, storm diagnostics, and decompositions of intensity, effective duration, contributing area, temporal coherence and maximizing-member selection. Figure and code correspondence and north-to-south target-region numbering are documented in the archive. The code-and-data ZIP contains major scripts and compact model-derived figure inputs. The separate PGW ZIP contains the actual temperature, SST and humidity perturbation CSVs. Extract both into the same parent directory. Purchased JMA radar–raingauge precipitation, RA-derived annual-maxima/fit tables, third-party basin boundaries, original CMIP6/FNL inputs, and complete raw WRF output are not redistributed. RA preprocessing and return-period estimation/map code are outside the scope of this archive. Some geographic plots and full recalculation require external inputs. Saved PGW-generation notebooks document the main workflow; the archived applied deltas define the simulation perturbations. Author-owned software, including notebook code cells, is licensed under the MIT License. Author-created data, explanatory documentation and experiment settings are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). Existing third-party rights, licenses and attribution notices remain in force; these licenses do not relicense external inputs or dependencies.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Certified anisotropic meshing of thin, high-aspect-ratio regions in device modeling
items.abstract: Abstract Thin layers embedded in much larger bodies are routine in semiconductor devices and a chronic difficulty for device simulation. A mesher that keeps elements near-isotropic must resolve the layer thickness in the plane as well, so the number of unknowns grows as the square of the layer aspect ratio. We resolve the layer instead with anisotropic structured cells, whose count does not depend on the aspect ratio, and we certify the result. For steady conduction, a conforming P1 potential and an equilibrated Raviart--Thomas flux, computed on the same mesh, enclose the exact resistance between guaranteed bounds without any reference solution. The enclosure width depends on how planar the field is, not on element shape. For layer-parallel flow it is at round-off level, below $10^{-11}$, for cell aspect ratios from 10:1 to 1000:1. For a 10~mm wide, 30~$\upmu$m thick film, 567 nodes then give the exact sheet conductance, where an isotropic mesh would need about $1.6\times10^{7}$ nodes. For a point source on a 30~nm film over a substrate, the anisotropic solution matches the closed-form image series to within 0.14\% once the grounded outer boundary is accounted for. For a contact on a film--substrate structure, the certified enclosures are nested and shrink from 23\% to 6.9\% under refinement. Applied to a three-layer stack, the method shows that a 30~nm sheet, 0.5\% of the total thickness, carries 0.13\% or 13.4\% of the potential drop depending on its doping, and the certified enclosures of the access resistance for the two dopings are disjoint.

items.title: Atomic layer controlled electron beam induced etching of molybdenum using sequential O2 and HCl exposures with positive sample voltage
items.abstract: Atomic layer controlled molybdenum (Mo) etching was performed at <100 °C using alternating exposures of O2 and HCl combined with simultaneous electron exposures and positive sample voltage. Electron exposures at ∼100 eV were derived from a hollow cathode plasma electron source. The Mo surface was oxidized to MoOx using concurrent O2 and electron beam exposures. The Mo oxidation rate increased dramatically when a positive voltage of +20 V was applied to the sample stage. Subsequently, the MoOx layer was linearly etched during synchronous HCl and electron exposures when a positive voltage of +20 V was also applied to the sample stage. No enhancement of the oxidation or etching was observed with a negative voltage of −20 V on the sample stage. The oxidation and etching enhancement in the presence of the positive sample voltage suggested that low energy electrons or anions dominated the reaction. The primary electrons at ∼100 eV can produce low energy electrons by ionization of Ar in the reactor and also by secondary electron yield from the Mo substrate. Low energy electrons can form O− or Cl− anions via dissociative electron attachment. Low energy electrons and anions can then be pulled to the sample stage at +20 V. Alternating oxidation and chlorination steps were applied in a digital fashion to define the Mo etching process. An etch per cycle of 1.3 Å/cycle was measured using in situ spectroscopic ellipsometry. The ellipsometric measurements could separately measure the MoOx growth, MoOx removal, and Mo film thickness loss during each etching cycle.
items.venue: Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology A Vacuum Surfaces and Films

items.title: Asymmetric Triple-Channel Schottky Barrier FinFET Biosensor for Cardiac Biomarker Detection
items.abstract: Abstract We have designed and simulated a new form of Schottky barrier FinFET, known as an SB-FinFET, that is designed to detect cardiac biomarker proteins without labels. The SB-FinFET uses an asymmetric, triple-channel stacked architecture, with the three channels positioned vertically on top of each other. The SB-FinFET consists of three channels made of silicon carbide (SiC), with nickel silicide (NiSi) Schottky contacts and hafnium oxide (HfO 2 ) insulating material as the gate dielectric to reduce the amount of intrinsic leakage current and improve the efficiency with which electrostatic coupling occurs. The architecture allows for the decoupling of current driving ability from sensing ability because of the difference in doping levels of the channels: the two outer channels have a doping density of 1 x 10 17 cm − 3 and are 4 nm deep, while the central channel has a doping density of 1 x 10 10 cm − 3 and is 1 nm thick. The two outer channels provide a suitable amount of current drive and gain, while the central channel serves as a high-sensitivity transducer that converts the biomarker/protein interaction into an electrical signal. The 3D TCAD simulation results exhibit an I ON /I OFF ratio of approximately 1 x 10 8 with low subthreshold swing for target biomolecules that have dielectric constants within the range of k = 1.5–3.5 (e.g., uricase, streptavidin, and troponin). The performance was further characterized through an analysis of linearity with transconductance (g m ) and through third-order nonlinearity metrics (VIP 3 and IIP 3 ). The SB-FinFET has been compared against other types of devices, including Negative Capacitance FET (NC-FET) and Tunnel FETs (TFETs), for sensitivity and complexities associated with fabrication. The results from these comparisons show that SB-FinFET's performance is similar to the two other device structures previously mentioned, while having a lower complexity and cost to fabricate them. The SB-FinFET is therefore an excellent experimental platform for developing new cardiac diagnostics devices that would allow for rapid diagnosis at or near the site of patient care.

items.title: Advancements in Embedded Surveillance Robotics for Defense and Security Applications
items.abstract: In military applications, surveillance plays a critical role in ensuring security, particularly in isolated and border areas. This chapter presents a recent approach to surveillance using a robot for military applications. The planned methodology is to substitute soldiers in border areas with robots, to enhance the security and both autonomous and manual control via internet connectivity. Equipped with multiple sensors and various electronic devices, the robot is designed to detect enemy presence, capture camera footage, and live-stream data to authorized personnel. This robot enables armed forces to proficiently monitor isolated areas and respond immediately to potential threats. Human risk is reduced by using this type of robot surveillance system. Deploying robots in high-risk isolated areas minimizes personnel exposure to potential threats while maintaining effective surveillance. The use of autonomous technology increases operational efficiency by enabling continuous surveillance without requiring constant human intervention. By combining cutting-edge embedded technology, real-time monitoring, and remote operability, this robot vehicle delivers a consistent and effective solution for border or boundary security. Integrating advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), embedded systems, and very large-scale integration (VLSI), will significantly enhance the capabilities and efficiency of the robot in armed forces. This robot provides not only a human-free system but also an efficient smart system to address military challenges.

items.title: ATLAS: Adaptive Task-Aware Federated Learning with Heterogeneous LoRA and Split Learning for Edge LLMs
items.abstract: Federated learning (FL) can adapt large language models (LLMs) without centralizing private data, but deployment on heterogeneous edge clients is constrained by task diversity, device variability, and communication cost. Standard task-agnostic aggregation and uniform-rank low-rank adaptation (LoRA) often cause negative transfer and poor resource matching. This paper presents ATLAS, a task-aware framework for parameter-efficient federated fine-tuning of transformer LLMs on heterogeneous clients. ATLAS combines representation-based task discovery, budget-aware heterogeneous LoRA allocation, state-consistent split federated learning, and LoRA-only graph regularization, together with INT8 LoRA communication and FP32 server-side computation. On a heterogeneous GLUE federation with three tasks, nine clients, and three backbones, ATLAS improves the macroaverage task score over standard FedAvg by 16.18 points on DistilBERT, 24.83 points on GPT-2, and 6.86 points on Qwen-2.5-0.5B, while reducing LoRA synchronization traffic and eliminating low-resource-client failures.
items.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series

items.title: AI Surge Accelerates the Transition to Liquid Cooling: Rethinking Energy and Water Use in Data Center Cooling
items.abstract: Abstract The power density of AI workloads is rapidly driving shifts to liquid cooling. This study rethinks and assesses the global impact on energy and water demand of this cooling transformation. Results suggest that liquid cooling can reduce cooling energy use by 25-56% relative to air cooling, offering substantial energy savings for GW-scale AI data centers. Best-practice PUE values could be as low as 1.07-1.08 for today’s systems and 1.03-1.04 for emerging designs and WUE values from 0.38 to 2.63 L kWh⁻¹, depending on temperature conditions. We identify global free-cooling rack inlet temperature thresholds of 33 °C for evaporative systems and 49 °C for dry systems, demonstrating the practicality of 100% free cooling in many locations. The model finds that minimum PUEs do not necessarily coincide with minimum total energy use. Results quantify the large sustainability potential of liquid cooling and provide actionable targets for data center design and policies.

items.title: A full-hardware edge detection system based on a highly robust dual random number generator
items.abstract: Conventional edge computing hardware at autonomous driving terminals is limited by chip area and power efficiency for complex image data. Recently, researchers have used memristors to construct dedicated hardware systems, achieving advancements in multiple image processing fields such as pattern recognition and edge detection. However, a full-hardware image processing system with anti-interference, low power, and high real-time performance remains challenging. Here, we fabricated a volatile Ag/AlO x /n-Si memristor with exceptional stability and low power. High-resolution electron microscopy visualized Ag conductive filament formation. Integrating two memristors with a logic circuit, we designed a low-power edge detection unit using dual random number hardware computation. Its energy consumption is 92.3% lower than traditional logic circuits, with strong anti-interference. To validate practical use, we constructed a 32-channel parallel full-hardware system with 64 devices, achieving 31.25 frames per second and excellent edge detection. The system exhibits excellent scalability, stability, and anti-interference, offering great potential for edge vision hardware in autonomous driving, safety monitoring, and surgical assistance.

items.title: A Review on Changing Trends in Mobile Security Utilizing FPGA-Based Lightweight Cryptography, AI-Based Threat Analytics, and Decentralized Identity Protocols
items.abstract: The rapid growth of mobile and Internet of Things (IoT) systems has created crucial security challenges as many devices have limited computing power, are expanded across different networks, and are facing continuously changing cyber threats. Traditional methods like fixed intrusion detection, Advanced Encryption Standard (AES)-based encryption, and centralized login systems are becoming less effective in protecting today’s mobile infrastructure as they are not adaptable to these changes. In order to protect mobile devices from these security threats, three modern technologies were invented. The first is blockchain-based decentralized identity (DID), which will manage user authentication and access without relying on a central authority, and make the system more secure. The second is AI-based intrusion detection systems (IDSs), which apply machine learning to detect unusual behavior or threats in real time. The third is lightweight cryptography (LWC), which will secure data protection while using less power and processing, and this feature is making it ideal for small devices. This review will inspect these three approaches along with its working mechanism with their advantages and challenges, with a primary focus on field-programmable gate array (FPGA)-based implementations of LWC to deal with the needs of VLSI integration. It will also provide a comparison framework, and it will investigate how the application of these technologies can be combined in the future to build more secure mobile systems. Lastly, it will also focus on major issues like compatibility, system delay, and scalability, and it will suggest future research directions, which include federated learning (FL), quantum-resistant encryption, and lightweight blockchain protocols that are designed for mobile environments.

items.title: A Novel Technique for Low Power in Adiabatic Logic Based on FinFET
items.abstract: An efficient answer to the growing need for portable, low-power gadgets is adiabatic logic gates. This chapter presents several adiabatic logic designs, including differential cascode pre-resolved adiabatic logic (DCPAL), positive feedback adiabatic logic (PFAL), and 2N-2N2P logic circuits. The purpose of the study is to lower the power for fundamental gates such BUFFER, NAND, NOR, and XOR based on several adiabatic logic types and the suggested logic circuit in order to compare their efficiency in terms of average power consumption and latency at different frequencies. By providing the correct stacking, the NMOS transistor prevents the charge from being discharged toward GND. The effectiveness of the suggested logic circuit is evaluated by comparing its average power consumption and latency at various frequencies with the traditional PFAL logic circuit. Additionally, the suggested circuit and other adiabatic logic types are compared based on their power consumption at various frequencies. Complete simulations are performed at various frequencies using the HSPICE tool at 16 nm and 32 nm technology. Finally, graphs are used to illustrate the average power dissipation characteristics and compare the proposed PFAL-based logic family with the adiabatic logic family.

items.title: A Metacognitive Framework for Test-Time Adaptation: Taxonomy and Research Challenges
items.abstract: In Test-Time Adaptation, when out-of-distribution samples interleave unpredictably with corrupted in-distribution samples, adaptation without corrective measures is prone to significant performance decrease. Existing protocols rely on unreliable cues (e.g., predictive entropy) which are unable to distinguish corrupted in-distribution data from semantically novel open-set samples. To address this issue, we formalize Test-Time Adaptation through a two-level metacognitive framework that decouples task execution from control, facilitating a unified taxonomy that categorizes existing Test-Time Adaptation protocols across three core axes, i.e., which knowledge is monitored, which part of the models are targeted for adaptation, and how adaptation occurs. We provide evidence that robust corrective measures in Test-Time Adaptation require monitoring grounded in structured internal representations to reliably estimate model competence. Lastly, we frame monitoring as a resource-allocation problem, examine neuromorphic substrates for bounded self-regulation, and outline key open challenges.
items.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series

items.title: A Comprehensive Review on Contemporary Challenges and Emerging Solutions in Deep Learning and Machine Learning: Limitations, Trends, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Deep Learning and Machine Learning have emerged as transformative technologies driving innovation across healthcare, finance, autonomous systems, and generative intelligence. Despite their remarkable success, the rapid scaling and deployment of these models have exposed a series of critical challenges that limit their reliability, efficiency, and real-world applicability. This comprehensive review paper presents a systematic analysis of contemporary problems and prospective solutions in the field, based on literature published between 2022 and 2026. Major challenges identified include data-related issues such as bias, scarcity, poor quality, and privacy concerns; model-centric limitations including the black-box nature leading to lack of interpretability and explainability, poor generalization to out-of-distribution data, and vulnerability to adversarial attacks and hallucinations in generative models. Furthermore, we highlight the escalating computational costs, high energy consumption, and environmental impact associated with training large-scale models, alongside growing ethical and regulatory concerns. In response, this review examines emerging solutions shaping the next generation of AI. These include efficient architectures such as Vision Transformers, Mamba models, model quantization, pruning, and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (LoRA), data-centric approaches like synthetic data generation and federated learning, and trust-centric methods including Explainable AI (XAI) using SHAP and LIME, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for hallucination mitigation, and robust and trustworthy AI frameworks. The paper concludes by outlining key research gaps and future directions towards developing more trustworthy, efficient, scalable, and sustainable AI systems.
items.venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

items.title: A Comprehensive Architectural, Cryptographic, and Cyber-Physical Analysis of Blockchain-Secured Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Digital Twin Synchronization in Industry 4.0 Smart Manufacturing: From PUF Zero-Trust Authentication to Predictive Maintenance and Cloud Manufacturing-as-a-Service
items.abstract: The convergence of Operational Technology (OT) and Information Technology (IT) under the Industry 4.0 paradigm has transformed traditional isolated factories into hyper-connected Cyber-Physical Production Systems (CPPS). In modern smart manufacturing, Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machining centers, 6-DOF industrial robotic arms, Additive Manufacturing (3D printing) cells, and Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) stream continuous high-frequency telemetry via the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) to synchronize real-time virtual replicas known as Industrial Digital Twins (IDTs). Concurrently, Cloud Manufacturing-as-a-Service (CMaaS) platforms enable original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) to outsource on-demand part production across globally distributed micro-factories. However, legacy centralized Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) and cloud-hosted Digital Twin repositories suffer from single-point-of-failure downtime risks, Stuxnet-style PLC command spoofing, counterfeit sensor firmware injection, intellectual property (IP) theft of proprietary 3D CAD/G-code files, and opaque Service-Level Agreement (SLA) disputes during unplanned machine breakdowns. Blockchain technology—combining tamper-evident distributed ledgers, low-latency industrial consensus, and deterministic smart contracts—provides a decentralized Zero-Trust security fabric for smart factories. This paper presents a comprehensive architectural, mathematical, and cyber-physical investigation of blockchain technology in Industry 4.0 IIoT and Digital Twin ecosystems. We formalize a five-layer industrial reference architecture integrating SRAM Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) shop-floor devices, IEEE 802.1Qbv Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) and OPC UA edge gateways, hybrid Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) and Credit-Raft consortium ledgers, InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) CAD storage, and automated smart contracts. We formulate rigorous mathematical models for PUF-anchored challengeresponse device authentication, cryptographic Digital Twin state-synchronization divergence bounds, Wiener stochastic bearing degradation and Remaining Useful Life (RUL) smart contract maintenance triggers, and gametheoretic CMaaS capacity matching. Finally, we benchmark authentication overhead on ARM Cortex-M4 controllers, Digital Twin sync latency across 2,000 sensors, and industrial operational KPI improvements.
authors: Priyanshu Raj, Dheeraj Yadav, Dr. Vishal Shrivastava, Dr.Ashok Kajla, Mr.Rahul Sharma,  Er.Ram Babu Buri
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: A Comprehensive Analysis FinFET, FeFET, CNTFET, Nanowire FET and Nanosheet FET for Low Power Applications
items.abstract: Abstract This research undertakes a comparative examination of semiconductor devices operating at the nanoscale, exploring their viability as substitutes for conventional Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors (MOSFETs) within Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) architectures. Such nanoscale devices exhibit superior operational speed, reduced physical dimensions, and diminished energy consumption, thereby mitigating the inherent challenges encountered with traditional MOSFETs as their feature sizes are progressively reduced. In order to perpetuate the advancement of semiconductor technology as predicted by Moore's Law and to satisfy escalating performance benchmarks, it is imperative that nanoscale devices overcome short-channel effects while maintaining interoperability with Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) fabrication processes. The objective of this investigation is to furnish device engineers with a framework for selecting appropriate MOSFET alternatives that conform to contemporary standards of efficacy, scalability, and manufacturing feasibility, thereby contributing to the progress of low-power, high-performance semiconductor innovations.

items.title: Enabling Retraining-Free Accurate Inference in Analog Compute in Memory Accelerators
items.abstract: Analog compute-in-memory (CIM) accelerators compute matrix-vector products directly inside memory arrays, eliminating weight movement and promising order-of-magnitude gains in inference efficiency. However, converter and device errors make pretrained models unusable on these arrays, and hardware-aware retraining is costly. We enable retraining-free, accurate inference of pretrained models on simple analog arrays with low-cost, shared calibration. Our key observation is that analog error depends on how each layer is represented on the array, and that this representation can be changed offline without changing the computation. We center the inputs and apply Hadamard rotations designed for analog arrays, which keep shared reference errors spread and confine input mixing to each array. Across CNNs, vision transformers and LLMs up to 14B parameters on PCM and ReRAM, the method brings vision models and larger LLMs within a few points of floating-point accuracy and matches or approaches published hardware-aware training without training any weights. On ReRAM with 6-bit ADCs, it restores ViT-B/16 from 37.4% to 82.9% and Phi-4 from 27.0% to 72.2%, both within 2.2 points of floating-point accuracy.

items.title: MCUFlowNet: Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search for Optical Flow on Microcontrollers
items.abstract: Dense optical flow allows small drones to avoid obstacles. However, few dense optical flow networks are designed for microcontrollers (MCUs) with neural accelerators, whose on-chip SRAM limits the input resolution. We present PACE-NAS, a macro-to-micro neural architecture search framework that decouples memory from latency: a macro design fixes the backbone and its peak SRAM, and a micro design searches operators and depths to trade accuracy against compiler-estimated latency. We apply it to EdgeFlowNet on a Grove Vision AI V2 board (Ethos-U55), where profiling locates the peak SRAM at the full-resolution output head. Replacing transposed convolutions with bilinear upsampling and convolutions lowers the peak SRAM by 18%, and two lightweight context modules lower the endpoint error (EPE) without raising the peak. All searched subnets share this peak, so the search needs no memory constraint. We name the Pareto-optimal models MCUFlowNet; the fastest variant, MCUFlowNet-S, runs 1.76x faster than a retrained EdgeFlowNet at a 1.6% higher EPE and, in simulated forest flights at 2 m/s, reaches the goal without collision in 51.5% of trials, against 41.8%. PACE-NAS also applies to semantic segmentation, where a searched PIDNet-S variant runs 1.17x faster at similar accuracy. Code is available at https://gitlab.kuleuven.be/emedia-research-lab/esat-stadius/mcuflownet/mcuflownet.

items.title: CAMP: Context-Aware Mapping and Placement for LLMs on 3D-IMC Arrays
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) incur severe memory-access overheads due to the cost of loading large weight matrices and key-value (KV) caches. Analog In-Memory Computing (AIMC) is an emerging solution that enables computation directly on static weights stored in memory, substantially reducing energy and latency. 3D-IMC further stacks memory arrays into vertical tiers, increasing capacity but revealing a new challenge: how weights are placed in memory determines which matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) can execute concurrently, affecting latency and throughput. The concurrency aspect of 3D-IMC weight-mapping remains underexplored in the literature, leading to sub-optimal utilization of compute resources on 3D-IMC chips. In this context we propose CAMP (Context-Aware Mapping and Placement), an inference-context-aware weight mapping algorithm for 3D-IMC-based LLM accelerators. CAMP captures the potential resource contention resulting from the architecture, targeted network, and runtime context in a conflict matrix, enabling throughput-optimized weight mapping. This mapping is refined through a profiling-driven feedback loop that efficiently prunes the search space and returns optimized mappings within practical runtimes. CAMP is an offline, software-based solution requiring no hardware changes and improving 3D-IMC compute utilization from 42.4% to 60.3%, delivering up to 2.0x higher 3D-IMC throughput and 1.74x higher end-to-end throughput over state-of-the-art mapping algorithms.

items.title: Experimentally Grounded Machine Learning of PrecursorSurface-Reactant Chemistry in Atomic Layer Deposition
items.abstract: Whether a precursor-substrate-reactant combination yields an atomic layer deposition (ALD) process is still settled by trial-and-error experiments. Here we introduce AJIN (ALD Joint Interpretable Network), a machine-learning framework that learns this decision from experimental outcomes. We compiled 560 experimentally observed ALD and area-selective ALD outcomes spanning 76 precursors, 27 substrates, 20 reactants and 25-620 degrees Celsius. Following the ALD cycle, AJIN predicts adsorption from graph-neural-network embeddings of the precursor and substrate with temperature, and deposition by adding the reactant. The best model (CHGNet-MLP) reaches balanced accuracies of 79.2% for adsorption and 84.8% for deposition and transfers partially to unseen precursors. SHAP and ablation analyses show that substrate chemistry governs adsorption, whereas precursor, substrate and reactant all contribute to deposition. Tested against our laboratory's ALD experiments, AJIN correctly predicted 83% of new-substrate cases and 71% of new precursor-substrate adsorption cases, providing an experimentally grounded tool for prioritizing ALD and area-selective ALD chemistries.

items.title: Two-dimensional transistors for capacitorless dynamic random access memory
items.abstract: The continued advancement of data-intensive technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and high-definition multimedia is placing unprecedented demands on storage systems, requiring innovations in device architecture and materials. Conventional dynamic random access memory (DRAM), based on the one-transistor-one-capacitor (1T1C) cell, is increasingly constrained by scaling challenges, including reduced storage capacitance, increased leakage currents, and complex fabrication requirements. To address these limitations, this thesis explores the development of capacitorless two-transistor-zero-capacitor (2T0C) DRAM architectures integrated with two-dimensional (2D) materials, aiming to achieve high-density, energy-efficient, and scalable memory solutions. The first part introduces a novel van der Waals (vdW) integration method for incorporating high-quality Al2O3 dielectrics onto 2D MoS₂ to fabricate damage-free MoS₂ transistors, overcoming the challenges posed by the lack of surface dangling bonds in 2D materials. By employing monolayer h-BN as a buffer, aluminum is deposited and oxidized to form aluminum oxide (Al₂O₃), which is then transferred onto the MoS₂ channel, preserving pristine interfaces and intrinsic device properties. The resulting MoS₂ transistors exhibit high ON/OFF ratios, low leakage currents, sharp subthreshold swings, and minimal interface trap densities. The fabricated 2T0C DRAM cells demonstrate fast write speeds and long retention times, highlighting the promise of this approach for next-generation memory applications. The second part of this thesis presents the design, fabrication, and characterization of a vertically stacked 2T0C DRAM cell employing CaNb₂O₆ (CNO) as the gate dielectric and MoS₂ as the channel material. Utilizing a substrate-assisted molten salt growth strategy, high-quality CNO nanoflakes with excellent dielectric properties were synthesized and integrated with exfoliated MoS₂ to form back-gate field-effect transistors. The vertical stacking of two such transistors, separated by a low-κ h-BN interlayer, enabled the realization of a monolithic three-dimensional (3D) 2T0C DRAM architecture exhibiting robust data retention exceeding 2000 seconds, multilevel storage capability, and excellent endurance. Comparative analysis demonstrates the promising scalability and operational stability of this 2D-material-based approach relative to state-of-the-art DRAM technologies. Overall, the research presented in this thesis establishes new paradigms for DRAM technology by leveraging the unique properties of 2D materials and innovative device architectures. The strategies demonstrated offer significant potential for the realization of high-density, energy-efficient, and scalable memory systems. These advancements hold significant promise for the evolution of memory technology, opening new possibilities for future technological progress in data storage and processing.
items.venue: PolyU Institutional Research Archive (Hong Kong Polytechnic University)

items.title: Three-Dimensional Multiphysics Modeling of Bipolar Electrochemical Graphite Exfoliation and Graphene Deposition
items.abstract: Abstract Bipolar electrochemistry drives graphite exfoliation, transport of graphene-related species, and electrodeposition simultaneously in one reactor through a wirelessly polarized graphite electrode. Because these processes are coupled within the same electrolyte, the local ion concentrations, graphene-related species concentration, and current density that control the deposition are difficult to measure experimentally. A three-dimensional multiphysics model coupling charge, species, momentum, and energy conservation was developed, in which DFT calculations on simplified static reference systems provided the effective intercalation numbers of the OH- and H3O+ assisted exfoliation pathways (x = 4 and y = 3) for the COMSOL-based continuum simulations. The model simulated graphite consumption and feeding electrode deposition under different operating temperatures, graphite rod arrangements, and reactor geometries. Raising the temperature from 25 to 80 °C increased the simulated 24 h current density by approximately 82%. Adding a second pair of graphite rods increased the current density by approximately 16%, almost independently of the pair spacing, whereas the deposition was maximized when the spacing equaled the feeding electrode width (s/l = 1). Increasing the rectangular reactor width from 3 to 8 cm reduced the deposition thickness by approximately 60% while the current density decreased by only 9%.

items.title: Tailored waveform biasing for precise ion-energy control during plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition of nitrides
items.abstract: Ion-energy control during plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) allows for tailoring the properties of thin films. The energy of ions impacting the growth surface during plasma exposure can be controlled by applying a substrate bias, generally at a radiofrequency (RF) of 13.56 MHz for PEALD. This approach, however, typically results in broad ion flux-energy distribution functions (IFEDFs) and can influence the plasma through changes in plasma density. Tailored waveform (TW) biasing provides an alternative, enabling narrow IFEDFs without affecting the plasma otherwise. In this Letter, TW biasing at 200 kHz was implemented during the PEALD of various metal nitrides, where a range of benefits was observed. TW biasing reduced the oxygen incorporation in AlN films. For the conductive nitrides TaCxN1-x, WCxNy, TiN and NbN, TW biasing led to significant improvements in electrical resistivity, with TaCxN1-x additionally showing enhanced crystallinity. More broadly, TW biasing during PEALD offers the potential for more controlled tuning of material properties compared to conventional RF biasing.

items.title: TCAD-Assisted Deep-Learning Surrogate Modeling of a Dielectric-Modulated FinFET Biosensor for HER2-Equivalent Dielectric-State Sensing
items.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a TCAD-assisted deep-learning surrogate framework for a dielectric-modulated FinFET biosensor under a HER2-equivalent effective dielectric-state sensing condition. The first part establishes the device modeling of a three-dimensional silicon FinFET with an analyte-accessible nanocavity, where the nanocavity permittivity modulates the gate-to-channel electrostatic coupling and produces measurable changes in the drain-current transfer characteristics. The second part develops a multilayer-perceptron (MLP) surrogate model using logarithmic current and dielectric representations to reconstruct TCAD dielectric anchor states and predict the held-out HER2-equivalent k = 8 dielectric state. The framework is further extended to cavity-length and cavity-thickness screening , transconductance prediction, I ON /I OFF extraction, sensing-metric analysis, and computational-cost evaluation. For the surrogate-predicted k = 8 case, the extracted sensing parameters indicate an I ON /I OFF ratio of 1.72 × 10 9 , a threshold-voltage sensitivity of 0.26912, and a sensitivity of approximately 6300. Unlike direct clinical detection studies, the present work is restricted to device-level dielectric-to-electrical response prediction. It does not model HER2-antibody binding, concentration-dependent biomolecule loading, biological sample variability, or fabricated-device validation. Overall, the results show that the proposed surrogate can reproduce TCAD transfer characteristics, perform bounded interpolation at the HER2-equivalent dielectric state, and rapidly screen FinFET dielectric-geometry trends for biosensor design exploration.

items.title: TACT-KV: Tri-Axis Cosine Transform for Compressing Volumetric KV Caches in Medical VLMs
items.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) applied to 3D medical scans face a structural memory wall. A single CT or MRI volume produces tens of thousands of vision tokens, and the resulting key-value (KV) cache scales linearly with both batch and context. Existing KV compression methods operate on the cache's feature or token statistics, or apply 1D and 2D transforms, leaving the three-axis spatial structure in the cache unexploited. We propose TACT-KV (Tri-Axis Cosine Transform), a calibration-free KV compression method that exploits strong spatial correlations in visual KV states along all three anatomical axes of 3D scans. This correlation concentrates the KV cache energy under a frequency-domain transform. TACT-KV applies a separable 3D discrete cosine transform to the KV cache, allocates a per-layer bit budget across frequency bins via reverse water-filling (more bits to high-energy components), and quantizes each bin with a fixed scalar codebook. We derive a close-form relation: the distortion reduction from adaptive bit allocation is dominated by the spectral concentration of the transformed cache. Across six medical VLMs and two 3D CT benchmarks, TACT-KV achieves the lowest 1-bit prediction-flip rate on eleven of twelve model and dataset pairs in our main comparison. The same advantage reproduces on four general-purpose VLMs evaluated on video tasks, indicating that the benefit of exploiting three-axis structure generalizes beyond medical imaging. At equal high-bandwidth memory (HBM), TACT-KV scales the decoding batch size on a single GPU by up to $8\times$.

items.title: Synaptic Multi-Weight Wafer-Scale Domain Wall Magnetic Tunnel Junctions Driven by Spin Orbit Torque
items.abstract: Spintronic synaptic devices based on magnetic random access memory (MRAM) are a rapidly evolving class within the analog neuromorphic architecture. However, obtaining the multi-weight or analog behavior desired for improved neural network inference accuracy in scaled MRAM remains a challenge. In this study, we demonstrate and tune up to eight distinct resistance levels in 300 mm wafer-scale magnetic tunnel junction artificial synapses driven by spin orbit torque. By varying the applied in-plane field, multi-weight resistance states emerge through domain wall nucleation and pinning. These multi-weight states appear stochastically and can be addressed with an iterative programming algorithm to program a specific resistance. Electromagnetic simulations indicate the multiple states are due to domain wall nucleation mediated by in-plane field and applied voltage. Implementation of the measured multi-weight devices in a neural network yields a 96.1% inference accuracy using the MNIST dataset if all devices provide the same number of multi-weight states. When experimental device-to-device variation is included, the accuracy is 48.6%. Overall, this work demonstrates a route towards multi-weight artificial synapse MRAM, establishing a path towards scalable neuromorphic systems based on spintronics.

items.title: Substrate-Dependent Cryogenic and UV Performance of AlGaN/AlN/GaN HEMTs and Photodetectors
items.abstract: Abstract AlGaN/AlN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) and metal–semiconductor–metal photodetectors (MSM-PDs) were integrated on Al2O3 and 4H-SiC substrates to quantify the impact of substrate selection on cryogenic electrical stability and ultraviolet (UV) optoelectronic performance. The HEMT/SiC structure exhibited a higher peak transconductance (gm) of 1.56 mS/2.34 mS at 300 K/130 K compared to the HEMT/Al2O3 structure (1.27 mS/1.83 mS). At 300 K, the gate-source voltage corresponding to peak gm was −0.3 V for the HEMT/SiC compared to −2.1 V for the HEMT/Al2O3, indicating different strain-induced polarization effects. For integrated sensing, the peak relative spectral response wavelengths were observed at 300 nm (on Al2O3) and 370 nm (on SiC). High-resolution characterization confirms that improved crystal quality and carrier transport in SiC-based heterostructures result from reduced lattice mismatch at the GaN/SiC interface. These findings establish the AlGaN/AlN/GaN-on-SiC platform as a compelling architecture for high-efficiency, switching GaN electronics and integrated cryogenic optoelectronic applications.

items.title: Substrate Yield Enhancement Enabled by Advanced Packaging Metrology System
items.abstract: Detecting dimensional errors in substrate fabrication induced by the manufacturing process is a challenge for high-density substrates. Such detection is especially important in advanced substrates that incorporate high-speed impedance-controlled circuits where a small change in linewidth and spacing can impact circuit performance. A 100% metrology inspection system has been developed that can detect these dimensional errors and provide the data needed to correct these errors. The Beltronics system can perform up to 10-billion line width, line space and pad diameter measurements on a 510mm x 515mm substrate in 5 minutes, to an accuracy of 0.15 microns. This new system provides real-time feedback to enable continuous inline process control to monitor the sizes of all features on the substrate during the fabrication process. The system compares the dimensions of features on the substrate to dimensions from the original CAD data to detect and classify defects. This paper presents an overview of this new technology and explains how it can be used to detect machine dependent distortions, such as non-linearities in the lithography lens or direct write exposure system, and design dependent distortions resulting from etch rates varying as a function of feature size, shape, and metal density in the neighborhood of each feature.

items.title: Spaceborne radiation-tolerant atomic-layer memory with on-orbit real-time testing
items.abstract: Abstract The human endeavor in space exploration has never ceased, where space electronics with high radiation tolerance are of paramount importance. Due to the atomic-level thin-layer characteristic, atomic-layer material electronic devices exhibit extremely high radiation tolerance compared with traditional bulk material devices. However, on-orbit testing on atomic-layer electronics is still lacking, restricting the understanding of their online performance in the space environment. Here we report a spaceborne radiation-tolerant and low-noise atomic-layer MoS2 memory array. Deployed on the Fudan No.1 Satellite in a low Earth orbit, this work enables the first demonstration of on-orbit real-time testing on atomic-layer memory. To date, after 23 months of on-orbit testing, the accuracy of the returned memory data has remained at 100%, indicating impressive radiation tolerance. This work presents a substantial step forward for the practical application of atomic-layer space electronics.

items.title: Solution‐Processed HZO–IGZO Thin Film Transistors for Multiclass Classification Tasks
items.abstract: In recent years, thin film transistors (TFTs) based on HfZrO (HZO) have made significant progress in the fields of memory and neuromorphic computing. However, the fabrication of conventional HZO TFTs usually relies on sophisticated techniques such as atomic layer deposition and rapid thermal annealing. Although these techniques improve device performance, they may increase cost and process complexity. To address this issue, this work proposes a low‐cost and simple solution‐based strategy for fabricating HZO TFTs. The fabricated devices exhibit typical counterclockwise hysteresis, successfully emulating various synaptic plasticity behaviors, as well as achieving stable multilevel conductance states under consecutive pulse stimulation. A three‐layer fully connected neural network constructed using the experimentally measured discrete conductance states of the devices achieves a recognition accuracy of 95% on the MNIST handwritten digit recognition task after 50 training epochs. Furthermore, the weight‐replacement model is extended to a ResNet‐18 deep convolutional neural network, attaining an accuracy of 87% on a 102‐class flower image classification task. The proposed solution‐based process, which requires no complex vacuum equipment, is simple and low‐cost, providing a feasible technological pathway for the development of low‐cost neuromorphic computing and image enhancement applications based on HZO TFTs.

items.title: Scenario-aware Adaptive Neuromorphic Intelligence for multimodal sensor fusion
items.abstract: Multisensory Physical AI systems operating in isolated conditions must make timely and reliable decisions within strict energy and hardware budgets. In this context, the present analytical study investigates the feasibility of reliable multimodal sensor fusion using a neuromorphic approach based on memristor-based Integrate-and-Fire neuron circuits driven by aggressively compressed representations of sensory information. Rather than relying on fixed processing and learning parameters, the proposed framework introduces scenario-dependent adaptability into individual stages of the neuromorphic decision-making pipeline, including sensor-data compression, nonlinear spike encoding, reliability assessment, and memristive learning-forgetting dynamics. By coupling multiple sensor inputs through adaptive memristive synapses, the framework investigates how reliable and correlated observations can strengthen learned associations, while weak or obsolete relationships gradually decay through nonlinear forgetting. The resulting neuronal responses are evaluated across ten representative driving scenarios derived from the NuScenes dataset by comparing their encoded output patterns with predefined synthetic ground-truth codes representing the expected actuator responses. The simulations demonstrate that scenario-adaptive activity-vector sizing achieves a 61.5% reduction in retained sensory information, while improving mean bit-wise agreement from approximately 55% to 61.2% compared with a fixed maximum-resolution configuration. These findings highlight the potential of introducing scenario-aware adaptability directly into the building blocks of a neuromorphic system, providing a foundation for future hardware implementations that could significantly transform the capabilities of Physical AI systems operating under stringent resource and environmental constraints.

items.title: Scaling Up Analog CIM: A Simulation Framework for Topology-Aware Mapping
items.abstract: Analog compute-in-memory (CIM) enables energy-efficient AI inference by performing in-situ matrix multiplication. The growing demand for deploying larger models motivates chiplet integration to expand CIM capacity. However, simulation abstractions based on local operator costs and aggregate communication metrics obscure the impact of weight-mapping topology when CIM system scales up. We develop a phase analysis that quantifies how strongly mapping topology affects system performance across hardware configurations and how mapping optimization translates into latency gains. To evaluate and exploit this design space, we present Isobar, a simulation platform integrating CIM decompositions, heterogeneous execution, and resource modeling. Validated against silicon measurements and cycle-accurate simulation, Isobar provides reliable cost estimates that enable effective mapping search across model and hardware configurations. For Gemma-7B prefill, Isobar-guided mapping reduces communication time by 23.3% and end-to-end latency by 18.6% relative to the strongest baseline. Isobar's system-level modeling show that analog CIM retains energy-efficiency potential relative to GPU when scaled to thousands of dies, and identify topology-aware mapping as a key design dimension for efficient execution.

items.title: SPARE: Fast Linear Attention Decoding with Compact Recurrent States
items.abstract: Linear attention reduces the quadratic sequence-length complexity of softmax attention by maintaining fixed-size recurrent states. However, these states scale quadratically with the representation dimension and require repeated data transfers during decoding, creating a substantial GPU memory bottleneck. Recent studies have revealed significant low-rank redundancy in recurrent states, suggesting opportunities for more efficient representations. We introduce SPARE (State Projection for Accelerated Recurrent Execution), a training-free method that exploits this redundancy through fixed low-dimensional subspaces, heterogeneous rank allocation, and lightweight write compensation. By performing recurrent reads and updates directly on compact states, SPARE reduces memory traffic without online decomposition or dense-state reconstruction. SPARE achieves 2.55x full-model decoding speedup, 7.49x lower recurrent-kernel DRAM traffic, and 3.31x lower peak GPU memory, while preserving better associative-retrieval accuracy than structured pruning at matched memory budgets.

items.title: Retaining Hole Conduction Using a Germanium Seed Layer for High- k HfO2 ALD on Salt-Assisted APCVD Tungsten Diselenide
items.abstract: Abstract Tungsten diselenide (WSe2) is the leading p-type channel candidate for two-dimensional complementary field effect transistors (CFETs). However, depositing high-k gate dielectric on its inert basal plane has still been a challenge. Modified atomic layer deposition (ALD) chemistries to avoid unintentional doping, plasma surface treatments, and interfacial seed layers are among a few promising methods for high-k integration. Extensive studies have been done on molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) to identify possible routes to high-performance NFET. This study presents a possible route to integrating high-k HfO2 on salt-assisted atmospheric pressure chemical vapor deposition (SA-CVD)-grown WSe2 on Si/SiO2 wafers. We compare evaporated Hf, Ti, and Ge seed layers, oxidized in ambient, prior to high-k ALD on SA-CVD WSe2. Because salt-assisted growths bind defect density to local precursor flux, plasma-based surface treatments can damage or modify the underlying channel material, making seed layers a favorable option over plasma processes. ALD without any seed layer suppresses the hole branch of both exfoliated and CVD WSe2 transistors, where peak drive currents were lowered by roughly six orders of magnitude. Seedless HfO2 ALD, Hf and Ti seeds eliminate hole conduction below 0.5 nA/μm. Germanium is the only one of the three seeds that we study that preserves the hole branch, at least at the level of an unseeded reference device at equal gate overdrive, and shows a +40 V threshold voltage shift, making the device hole dominant. Therefore, Ge is a promising seed for retaining hole conduction in WSe2 PFETs, and the seed-ALD high-k HfO2 is a possible dielectric stack for top-gated PFETs.

items.title: Proving That a GPU, NPU, DPU or Other Device Consumed the Intended Command, Used Current Memory Translations and Produced Only the Declared Effect
items.abstract: AI workloads reach hardware through runtimes, drivers, command queues, firmware and IOMMU/SMMU translations before a GPU, NPU, DPU or other device produces an effect. Permission to compute, driver acceptance, a descriptor that was inspected a moment ago and the host’s current page tables do not prove what the device actually did. A descriptor can change after it was checked; a stale IOTLB entry can direct DMA to the wrong page; a reset or firmware update can reuse a queue slot for another tenant; a replayed command can be consumed twice; and a SmartNIC or peer-to-peer path can produce a network or storage effect that no one authorized. This disclosure describes a vendor-neutral, non-actuating method for reconstructing silicon-level consistency from evidence. Each hardware command is bound to an original operation, principal and permitted class. The descriptor the device actually consumes is compared by digest with the approved one. Queue, mapping, firmware and device-incarnation generations must be current; DMA bounds and permissions must hold; translation invalidation must be acknowledged; admission must cover every effect path and be replay-safe; and device completion and the observed effect must correspond to the original operation. Results are combined in three-valued logic: a proven contradiction yields CONTRADICTED even when other evidence is missing, full support yields SUPPORTED, and gaps yield UNRESOLVED — in particular, missing effect telemetry is never treated as proof that no effect occurred. The document provides a 60-stage, six-phase silicon workflow and a separate 60-stage integratedembodiment, each with flowcharts, 72 technical invariants, twelve hardware variations (GPU, DPU/SmartNIC, CPU trusted domains, chiplets, firmware, peripherals), 48 formal relations, 60 engineering checkpoints, a comparison with existing mechanisms (IOMMU/SMMU and ATS invalidation, PCIe IDE and TDISP, confidential-computing device assignment, SR-IOV and function-level reset, doorbell and queue protections, device attestation with SPDM, GPU command validation and DPU offload) and anon-actuating reference evaluator in Python, JavaScript and Go with 90 shared synthetic vectors, all passing. It is not hardware-validated or certified; the laboratory is synthetic, self-authored and not peer reviewed. The author is open to acquihire or strategic collaboration. Keywords: AI safety; hardware security; GPU; NPU; DPU; SmartNIC; command descriptors; DMA; IOMMU; SMMU; IOTLB invalidation; ATS; TOCTOU; device reset; function-level reset; device incarnation; firmware update; replay prevention; PCIe IDE; TDISP; SPDM attestation; confidential computing; three-valued logic
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Prediction of Deep Neural Network for TCAD Analysis of Degradation Induced by Near-Interface Displacement Defects in 4H-SiC MOSFETs
items.abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) devices used in space and nuclear environments are exposed to radiation that creates displacement defects (DDs), but the effect of DDs near the gate oxide/SiC interface has not been analyzed systematically. Using technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulation, this study analyzes how near-interface DDs in a 4H-SiC metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) affect the threshold voltage (Vth), transconductance (gm), and on-current (Ion), and builds deep neural network (DNN) models that predict these effects. The DDs were modeled as acceptor-like traps with varied energy levels, concentration, depth, lateral position, and distribution width. The degradation was largest at the channel entrance and the edge of the junction field-effect transistor (JFET) region. The center depth mattered little while the trap region reached the interface, whereas a small gap between the trap region and the interface strongly reduced the degradation. Shallow-level traps reduced Ion without shifting Vth, whereas only deep-level traps caused an actual Vth shift. The DNNs accurately predicted the degradation for new TCAD conditions in which the trap parameters simultaneously took values not used in training and outperformed grid interpolation and other regression models. The trained DNNs thus rapidly predict the degradation at the simulated lateral positions for radiation reliability assessment.

items.title: Polarized twin walls in a halide perovskite
items.abstract: Halide perovskites have emerged as promising materials for next-generation photovoltaics, laser sources, and X-ray detectors. There is intense debate as to whether some photoactive halide perovskites exhibit ferroelectric behavior and whether it might be possible to utilize the bulk photovoltaic effect to enhance the performance of halide perovskite solar cells. Here, using low-dose scanning transmission electron microscopy, we identify ferroelastic twin walls in vapor-deposited CsPbI 3 thin films, parallel to {110} and {112}. Remarkably, despite CsPbI 3 being centrosymmetric and nonpolar, we observe directly that Pb atoms shift at {110} twin walls driving a local ferroelectric-like polarization. These polar twin walls form an intrinsic array of nanoscale interfaces, spaced ~30 to 50 nm apart, embedded within the nonpolar perovskite lattice. In contrast, {112} twin walls do not show a polar displacement of Pb but strongly suppress octahedral tilt and off-center Cs atom displacements, revealing a different untapped structural degree of freedom. These findings reveal previously hidden nanoscale polarization in halide perovskite semiconductors, opening opportunities for enhanced conductivity and photovoltaic behavior through domain wall engineering.
items.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

items.title: Physics-aware Jacobian calibration for bridging the simulation-to-real gap in LDMOS modeling
items.abstract: Abstract The simulation-to-real gap between idealized TCAD simulations and experimental data from fabricated devices limits the accuracy of data-driven modeling for semiconductor devices. This work proposes a Physics Aware Jacobian Calibration (PAJC) framework to improve neural network (NN) surrogate modeling of LDMOS devices under sparse experimental supervision. A Physics Prior Model (PPM) trained on large scale TCAD simulations provides first order response sensitivities through its Jacobian matrix, enabling corrections from a small set of experimental anchor samples to propagate across the design space. Using the corrected simulation data together with experimental samples, a Calibrated Proxy Model (CPM) is constructed for device performance prediction. Experimental results on LDMOS devices show that the CPM achieves an average Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 2.28% on an unseen experimental test set while preserving physically consistent trends between design parameters and device performance. The proposed framework provides a scalable approach for physics informed AI assisted semiconductor modeling under realistic process variations.
items.venue: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics

items.title: Novel Interconnect Materials for Advanced Packaging Assembly Processes
items.abstract: As advanced packaging continues to drive towards heterogeneous integration, new materials need to be developed to address the many challenges faced in the assembly process. Development of novel materials for the various assembly processes is crucial to ensuring high yield for the assembly process for reliable SiP applications, and high density, fine pitch interconnects. As ultra-fine pitch flip-chips become prevalent in advanced packaging, with reduced standoff of flip-chips and other IC packages, cleaning becomes ever more challenging, especially as the chip and package sizes increase. The shift towards using semiconductor grade ultra-low residue no-clean flip-chip fluxes, which eliminates the cleaning process, is therefore one of the solutions for overcoming these challenges. The flux residue left behind after the soldering process is minimal and is compatible with the underfill or molding materials used in the subsequent processes. Further, adhesive agents, which leave near zero residue, have also been developed to enable fluxless soldering for wafer/die bonding. Another challenge is the warpage induced open joints defects as the chips are becoming thinner and larger, and thermo-compression bonding (TCB), and laser-assisted bonding (LAB) are being explored as alternatives for the typical mass reflow process, to improve process yield with robust flux materials. With more semiconductor chips and smaller components packed into a smaller footprint, the deposition of solder paste for high density SiP applications has become very challenging. For fine feature solder paste applications, the quality of fine solder alloy powder, flux formulations, and solder paste rheology, are crucial to achieve consistent solder paste deposition and good soldering performance. Particularly, for solder paste applications down to 100um or less, fine solder alloy powder, robust flux formulations, and solder paste rheology have been developed to achieve consistent solder paste deposition and good soldering performance. Due to some packaging design where printing of solder paste may not be possible, dispensing or jetting can also be used as an alternative. This presentation will cover innovative materials for advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration, including novel ultra-low residue flux formulations for flip chip attach that is compatible with underfill and molding compound, adhesive agent for fluxless soldering, and solder paste for ultra-fine pitch printing. These novel materials are critical enablers for high density packaging applications. Use cases for high density SiP modules, TCB and LAB, for advanced packaging and 2.5D modules, will be discussed as well.

items.title: Neural Architecture Search of Time-to-First-Spike-Coded Spiking Neural Networks for Efficient Eye-based Emotion Recognition
items.abstract: Eye-based emotion recognition enables eyewear devices to perceive users' emotional states and support emotion-aware interaction. However, deploying such functionality on their resource-limited embedded hardware remains challenging. Time-to-first-spike (TTFS)-coded spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer a promising solution due to their extremely sparse and energy-efficient computation, where each neuron emits at most one binary spike. While prior works have primarily focused on improving TTFS SNN training algorithms, the role of network architecture has been largely overlooked. This is particularly critical, as spike timing in TTFS SNNs is tightly coupled with architectural design, and eye-based emotion recognition requires compact yet highly efficient networks.
