In doublesided-cooled (DSC) modules, these two issues are strongly layout dependent because the main current path, common-source path, gate routing, and heat-spreading path are all defined by the threedimensionalpackage structure. This paper presented an electrothermal co-design method for a DSC multi-chip SiC MOSFET module by combining chip screening, source-feedback-oriented parasiticmodeling, and thermal-uniformity-oriented chip placement. The electrical design used the commonsource inductance matrix and equivalent feedback inductance as branch-level indicators, so that thelayout was not evaluated only by total commutation-loop inductance. The thermal design used a chiplevel temperature-uniformity index and a thermal-resistance matrix to select the chip spacing, and themodel was checked by comparing the measured staircase/Cauer thermal-resistance network with the simulated layer-level thermal resistance. A fabricated 1200 V, 450 A prototype was used to verify thepackage-level electrical and thermal models through double-pulse, short-circuit, and dual-interface thermal-resistance tests. The results establish a bounded validation route for using package extractionand thermal simulation to guide source-feedback and thermal-uniformity co-design in DSC multi-chip SiC MOSFET modules.

items.title: Mitigating the effect of traps in p-GaN HEMTs through field plate and doping optimization
items.abstract: Abstract This work presents a complete analysis of normally-off p-GaN High Electron Mobility Transistors (HEMTs) with field plate using TCAD simulations in conjunction with physics-based analytical model. The study focuses on maximizing the breakdown voltage ( $$V_{BR}$$ ) through the integrated optimization of field plate (FP) length and Magnesium (Mg) doping concentration in the p-GaN cap layer under the influence of thermally assisted traps. The analyses were performed taking the reported experimental values of Mg and TAT (Trap Assisted Tunneling) concentrations. Implementation of the field plates successfully suppresses the crowding of electric field and enhance the channel breakdown voltage. The numerical length of the field plate is optimized for the highest breakdown voltage which was achieved at 978V when the field plate length (LFP) was 1.5 $$\mu $$ m in combination with high Mg doping.TCAD results also reveal that, Mg concentration significantly modulates the device’s threshold voltage ( $$V_{TH}$$ ), power density and leakage current. Explicitly, increasing the parametric value of Mg active concentration to $$1\times 10^{18}$$ $$cm^{-3}$$ increases the DC peak output current from 12 mA/mm to a saturation value of 67 mA/mm for V $$_{GS}$$ = 10V, while shifting the threshold voltage $$V_{TH}$$ from 4.91V to 1.6V. Furthermore, the TCAD results are compared with a physics-based analytical models specially developed for p-GaN HEMTs. These comparisons demonstrate strong agreement between the TCAD and the theoretical results in terms of DC characteristics for the proposed device. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, the combined optimization of field-plate length and Mg doping under trap-assisted tunneling conditions has not been previously investigated in detail. With the analytical cross-validation against experimentally-calibrated TCAD simulation, this approach also offers various performance parameter configurations, helping designers select the ideal combination for reliable high-power applications.

items.title: Effects of Deposition Temperature on the Microstructure and Electrical Properties of 50 nm High-k BaTiO3 MIM Capacitors Fabricated by Atomic Layer Deposition
items.abstract: Abstract Thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) of BaTiO3 (BTO) is of interest for next-generation microelectronic devices, including RAM and NAND memory. Herein, we investigate the influence of deposition temperature on the microstructure and electronic properties of 50 nm BTO thin films fabricated by ALD at 200, 220, 240, and 280 °C using bis-(1,2,4 triisopropylcyclopentadienyl)-Ba [Ba(iPr3Cp2)], titanium isopropoxide, and water as precursors, and highlight the significance of void formation in films based on this chemistry. Self-limiting ALD behavior is observed, such that the deposition rate and Ba:Ti ratio are independent of prolonged Ba dose times. XRD shows that films deposited at 220 and 240 °C are significantly more crystalline than films deposited at 280 °C after annealing. Scanning electron microscopy reveals a difference in film microstructure depending on deposition temperature, indicative of different “structural zones”. Cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy reveals that annealed, crystallized BTO films are susceptible to void formation, especially when lower ALD deposition temperatures are used. This void formation appears to result from a combination of the microstructure of the as-deposited film and the easily hydrated barium constituent and is identified as an important structural defect that will need to be avoided to achieve desired dielectric performance. Electrical properties, such as capacitance–voltage (CV), dielectric loss, and DC current–voltage (IV), are closely correlated with microstructure. Fifty-nanometer BTO thin films deposited at 220, 240, and 280 °C have relative permittivity values (εr) of 73, 60, and 33, respectively, at 10 kHz after annealing. Dielectric loss (tanδ) is as low as 0.001. A modest dispersion in capacitance is observed across varying sampling frequencies. Future research to further understand and mitigate void formation while retaining proper stoichiometry for this ALD chemistry is recommended to further improve dielectric performance.

items.title: Baseline Uncertainty Limits Mechanistic Interpretation of Power-Law Degradation Exponents in GAA Transistors
items.abstract: Power-law exponents are widely used to describe time-dependent transistor degradation and to extrapolate accelerated measurements toward operating conditions. Their physical interpretation, however, depends on the baseline from which degradation is measured. This study examines baseline sensitivity using published gate-all-around (GAA) transistor degradation data and a zero-curvature baseline reconstruction rule. In a primary dataset of 24 degradation curves, each curve yields one admissible zero-curvature root, shifting the median nominal exponent n = 0.550 to a reconstructed value 1/m = 0.346. Within an established phenomenological framework, this shift changes the inferred correlation parameter from χ = −0.820 to χ = −1.899. The apparent decrease in the local exponent with accumulated degradation appears in 19 of the 24 nominal curves but remains in only 5 curves after baseline reconstruction and is not robust under cross-fitted analysis. Across 26 eligible external nanowire curves (≥5 time points, out of 32 total curves), 19 curves yield a single admissible zero-curvature root. These roots remain numerically stable under single-point deletion (median relative change in m of 2.97% across 15 eligible curves) without systematically improving the secondary log–log fit. Numerical root stability therefore does not establish physical baseline validity. Consequently, the empirical exponent remains a useful kinetic descriptor, but it does not by itself distinguish between HCI- and BTI-like behavior or establish a transition between them.

items.title: A statistical framework for laser-induced subsurface modification and cracking in 4H-SiC
items.abstract: Abstract Laser slicing of 4H-SiC enables low-kerf wafer separation, but reproducible subsurface crack formation remains challengingbecause the modified layer is buried, defect-sensitive, and statistically variable. Here, nanosecond laser-induced subsurfacemodification and cracking in commercial n-type 4H-SiC are described probabilistically rather than through deterministicthresholds. Incident fluence, pulse-to-pulse pitch, and focal depth below the surface were varied systematically, and image-derived outcomes were classified as modification onset, crack onset, or stable crack formation. Weibull analysis was used todescribe the probability of each outcome, while binomial confidence intervals and bootstrap resampling were used to quantifyuncertainty. Modification formed within a comparatively narrow fluence band across all tested depths and pitches. Pulse pitchemerged as the primary parameter governing the transition from modification to cracking. At smaller pitch, stable crackingbecame probable within the same fluence interval as modification, whereas at larger pitch a statistically separable fluencerange produced modification without subsequent cracking. Cross-sectional SEM supported the corresponding morphologicalprogression from void-like or elliptical modifications to wedge-like, crack-forming inclusions. This combined statistical andmorphological analysis captures both systematic parameter trends and excursions among nominally identical conditions,providing a basis for selecting more reproducible crack-forming process windows for 4H-SiC wafer slicing.

items.title: TADA: Technology Aware DNN Accelerator Performance and Energy Estimator
items.abstract: Deep neural network (DNN) accelerators for edge inference must meet tight energy, latency, and area (EDP) constraints, and their optimal hardware architecture and dataflow configuration is typically identified through design space exploration (DSE). However, on-chip memory technology including cell type, bank organization, and process node, is rarely treated as a first-class citizen in DSE. For example, increasing memory capacity can reduce memory accesses through greater data reuse, but at the cost of higher area and access energy, thereby limiting the compute units budget. Consequently, memory technology can fundamentally shift the optimal accelerator architecture for a given area and EDP budget. Existing machine learning (ML)-based DSE methods require repeating simulation, data generation, and model training for each new memory technology. We present TADA, a memory technology-aware DNN accelerator performance and energy estimator that predicts system latency and energy for a given workload, hardware configuration, and memory technology. TADA is trained on a synthetic dataset that generalizes across memory technologies. The dataset spans current and future technology trends while enforcing physics-based guardrails to preserve realistic area-energy trade-offs. Each memory technology is represented by a technology signature, a vector of read energy, write energy, and storage capacity across a range of areas, provided as input alongside the workload and hardware configuration. Across 21 unseen technology curves spanning SRAM, STTRAM, ReRAM, PCM, FeFET, eDRAM, and CTT, TADA predicts system energy and latency with 1.5-4.4% and 0.7-1.2% mean absolute percentage error, respectively. In three pairwise case studies, it matches the simulator-selected memory technology at 98.7-100% of area budgets, with a mean EDP loss of at most 0.21%, while achieving over 10^4x higher evaluation throughput.

items.title: HippocamPEX: A Hippocampus-Inspired In-Silico Architecture for Context-Aware Sequence Prediction
items.abstract: The brain's hippocampus enables episodic memory - the ability to encode events within their context, organize them into sequences, and generate predictive representations to guide adaptive behavior. Modern computing architectures, however, are optimized for large-scale arithmetic and struggle with such context-dependent sequential prediction or "cognitive" tasks. To translate these capabilities into a mixed-signal architecture, we first derived a working model from the neuroscience literature distilling key hippocampal computations into engineering-friendly abstractions. We then leveraged converging advances in in-memory computing, neuromorphic computing, asynchronous circuits, and analog computing to design a mixed-signal hardware architecture implementing these computations, called HippocamPEX. Finally, we demonstrated that HippocamPEX reproduces characteristic representational dynamics of hippocampal subregions and performs robust context-specific sequence prediction through detailed activity and circuit simulations. By tightly coupling hardware design with neuroscience knowledge, this work establishes a pathway for artificial systems capable of rapid, adaptive, and context-aware decision-making, addressing a central gap between biological and conventional computing.

items.title: Surface chemistry as data for level-set simulation of etching and deposition
items.abstract: Level-set simulators of etching and deposition move the surface with a velocity that depends on adsorbate coverages. These coverages are usually computed from balances solved and coded by hand for each chemistry, whereas voxel-based Monte Carlo profile simulators read the reaction mechanism as data. For the open-source level-set simulator ViennaPS, this work presents a surface model whose rate laws, Jacobian and velocity are derived from a reaction file and evaluated with ray-traced fluxes. Steady-state coverages are obtained with Newton's method and transient coverages with a conservative integrator. One compiled model is applied to eight chemistries for chemical vapour deposition, selective epitaxy, plasma etching, sputtering and atomic layer deposition. It reproduces a hand-written silicon etch model to seven significant digits at a single point and within the Monte Carlo noise in a masked trench. In a high-aspect-ratio cavity, alumina conformality is determined by a trimethylaluminium reaction probability within the measured range.

items.title: Selection of the most appropriate semiconductor on the DC-DC buck converters by multi-criteria decision making methods
items.abstract: Abstract The selection of suitable semiconductor is one of the most important factors affecting the performance of the power electronics circuits. The general characteristics of the circuit such as voltage, current, and switching frequency limit the switch selection. When choosing semiconductors that meet these constraints, the criteria such as switching speed, losses, cost etc. are be taken into consideration. The importance weights of the criteria may vary depending on the expert’s experience and the application conditions. Therefore, to make the best decision, it is necessary to make a choice based on all criteria. In this paper, the most suitable semiconductor selection for a 36–12 V DC-DC buck converter has been made using the multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods, MOORA and integrated AHP-TOPSIS firstly in the literature. GaN-transistor, IGBT and power MOSFET has been evaluated according to the four criteria. The consistency of the results obtained with both MOORA and the integrated AHP-TOPSIS methods demonstrates that these methods are successful in determining the most suitable semiconductor in power electronics applications where there is more than one option.

items.title: Layered Precursor‐Guided Growth of Nondegenerate Amorphous In 2 O 3 Approaching the Thickness Limit
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Oxide semiconductors are promising channel materials for ultrathin electronics. However, conventional growth methods often produce excess carriers, poor stability, and interfacial issues, limiting their electronic applications. Here, we present a layered precursor‐guided synthesis of atom‐thin amorphous indium oxide (In 2 O 3 ) by oxidizing a layered InSe precursor within a back‐end‐of‐line (BEOL)‐compatible thermal budget. The oxide thickness is precisely controlled by the number of precursor layers, enabling In 2 O 3 as thin as 0.63 nm at the physical thickness limit. By avoiding localized nucleation and island coalescence issues, the resulting In 2 O 3 exhibits atomically smooth surfaces and excellent electrostatic uniformity with potential variations below 22 meV. Capacitance‐voltage analyses confirm a carrier density of 2.8 × 10 18 cm −3 in the nondegenerate regime and a low interface trap density of 10 10 ∼10 11 cm −2 ·eV −1 . We further demonstrate reproducible enhancement‐mode transistors with sub‐3 nm channels, featuring near‐zero threshold voltage, a low subthreshold swing (SS) of ∼74 mV/dec, a negligible hysteresis of < 10 mV, and robust gate‐stress stability. This work establishes a reliable route for integrating ultrathin, high‐performance amorphous oxide semiconductors, pushing the limits of next‐generation nanoelectronics.

items.title: Effects of DBC Copper Layer Thickness on the Electrical, Thermal, and Thermo-Mechanical Performance of Parallel SiC Chip Power Modules
items.abstract: Direct Bonded Copper (DBC) substrates simultaneously provide current conduction, heat spreading, and structural support in multi-chip power modules, making Cu thickness a key trade-off variable. This study investigates the effects of DBC Cu thickness on the electrical, thermal, and thermo-mechanical responses of a 300 A parallel SiC chip power module. Thermal-coupling analysis was performed to distinguish the temperature effects of chip spacing from those of top Cu thickness. Electro-thermal simulation showed that conduction loss and maximum chip temperature increased as the top Cu thickness decreased, with a pronounced change between 0.175 and 0.160 mm under the 300 A condition. Thermo-mechanical analysis showed that reducing the symmetric top/bottom Cu thickness from 0.30/0.30 to 0.15/0.15 mm decreases reflow warpage of the baseplate from 183.930 to 30.091 μm. Thermal-cycling analysis showed that the cycle increment in volume-averaged inelastic strain energy density in the evaluated solder region decreased by 17.2%. The results showed distinct thickness-dependent responses: reducing the top Cu thickness increased conduction loss and maximum chip temperature, whereas symmetrically reducing both the top and bottom Cu thicknesses decreased reflow warpage and solder inelastic strain energy density in simulation.

items.title: Dual-Gate IGZO Transistor-based Time-Varying Reservoir Computing for Highly Efficient Human Action Processing
items.abstract: Abstract Physical reservoir computing (PRC), which leverages the intrinsic dynamics of materials, offers significant advantages for time-series processing with its low training complexity. However, most reported PRC systems suffer from fixed characteristic timescales, which limits their applicability to scenarios involving widely varying temporal dynamics. To address this issue, we demonstrate an on-chip PRC system based on a dual-gate IGZO transistor. In this device, a modulation gate is introduced to electrically control the relaxation timescale by tuning the ionic relaxation of the electric double layer (EDL). As a result, the device enables ~3.3-fold tunable timescales and is feasible for monolithic integration. A 5 kb IGZO transistor array is fabricated and integrated with a custom FPGA board, providing an array‑level and FPGA‑based demonstration of a time-varying reservoir computing (TV-RC) system. This TV‑RC system enables multiple time-series processing tasks, including electrocardiogram (ECG) and speech signal classification. Furthermore, human action recognition, which has not been accomplished by previous on-chip PRC systems, is validated in this system using the UTD-MHAD dataset. The system achieves an average recognition accuracy of 91.85% across 27 actions. It consumes 5.15 mJ/action for inference, with only 3.99 J/action for reservoir state generation. Our design would be of profound significance for extending the boundaries of physical reservoir computing, especially for vision-based intelligent tasks.

items.title: Design of a Long Life Bi-directional Off-board Battery Electric Vehicle Charger
items.abstract: Abstract Gallium Nitride (GaN) High Electron Mobility Transistors (HEMTs) have reshaped the power semiconductor landscape by outperforming silicon (Si) MOSFETs, silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs, and superjunction devices across a variety of applications and disrupting the order of merit of semiconductor technology choice. Their unique combination of low conduction losses, high switching speeds, and reverse voltage blocking capability enables more compact converter designs and innovative circuit topologies. In this paper, the design of a bidirectional off-board EV charger featuring a GaN-based totem-pole power factor correction (PFC) stage is presented. The goal was to achieve an operational lifetime of 120,000 h, significantly exceeding the industry norm of 8,000 h, allowing the charger to outlast multiple EV life cycles. This work details the constraints imposed by lifetime, thermal, and performance requirements, outlines the design trade-offs and solutions implemented, and presents an algorithm for extending the lifetime of the device. The results highlight the unique capabilities of the GaN HEMTs in delivering efficient, high power density EV chargers.

items.title: Characterisation of vertical gate-all-around tunnel FET using modulation-doped InGaAs nanowire/Si junction on SOI wafer
items.abstract: Tunnel field-effect transistors (TFETs) utilising quantum tunnel transport are expected as promising candidates for low-power switching applications, primarily due to their potential to overcome the thermionic limit of 60 mV/dec in subthreshold slope (SS) of conventional FETs. Despite this potential for low-voltage switching operation, TFETs face serious challenges for practical circuit integration, most notably low on-state currents and a narrow gate voltage window for maintaining steep SS characteristics. In this report, we characterised selective-area growth of modulation-doped core-multishell (CMS) nanowires (NWs) consisting of an InGaAs/InP/AlInAs/δ-doped AlInAs/AlInAs/InGaAs heterostructure on InGaAs NW sidewalls on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) substrates and vertical gate-all-around (VGAA) TFETs using the CMS NW-channels on SOI. The TFET devices exhibited robust gate modulation of the tunnelling current at the n-InGaAs/p-SOI junction, achieving a minimum SS of 35 mV/dec at a low drain-source voltage. While the TFETs are promising, the enhancement of the on-state current was constrained by an unintentionally thick InP barrier layer and over-etching to reveal the contact layer, both of which induce a non-ideal distribution of the internal electrical field. These findings underscored that precise dimensional control of the CMS architecture and moderate junction engineering at the InGaAs/Si heterointerface were critical for achieving high-performance VGAA-TFETs in practical applications.

items.title: Atomic-Scale Electron Microscopy of Two-Dimensional Matter: Defects, Interlayer Coupling, and Confined Reactions
items.abstract: Atomic-resolution electron microscopy reveals how defects, local coordination, and interlayer interactions shape the behavior of two-dimensional materials. This Review discusses selected advances in transmission and scanning transmission electron microscopy and electron energy-loss spectroscopy, with emphasis on graphene, hexagonal boron nitride, transition-metal dichalcogenides, and species confined within bilayer graphene. The discussion begins with specimen preparation and low-voltage operation, emphasizing the influence of contamination and electron irradiation on structural interpretation. Representative studies then illustrate how imaging and spectroscopy connect atomic configurations with bonding, electronic states, and functional responses. Particular attention is also given to spectroscopic signatures of interlayer coupling and show how bilayer graphene provides a confined environment for unusual atomic arrangements and beam-driven chemical reactions. These examples highlight the need to distinguish observed structures from inferred properties and irradiation-induced products. Finally, future opportunities in dose-efficient acquisition, depth-sensitive imaging, spectroscopy, and correlative measurements are outlined for understanding and controlling low-dimensional matter.

items.title: Adaptive ZVS Control and ZCD Delay Compensation for a Single‐Phase CRM Totem‐Pole PFC Converter
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents an adaptive zero‐voltage‐switching (ZVS) control and zero‐current‐detection (ZCD) delay compensation strategy for a single‐phase critical‐conduction‐mode (CRM) totem‐pole power‐factor‐correction (PFC) converter. Conventional CRM and quasi‐square‐wave (QSW) control schemes suffer from three inherent limitations: ZVS failure in the high‐input‐voltage region, excessive switching‐frequency rise under light‐load conditions, and input‐current distortion caused by the fixed ZCD propagation delay. To address these issues, a state‐plane‐based model is first established to derive the ZVS condition and its failure boundary. Based on this model, an online timing scheme is developed that incorporates the minimum ZVS time‐margin requirement and the maximum switching‐frequency limit, and adaptive dynamic dead times are introduced to accommodate resonant transitions under varying operating conditions. In addition, a ZCD delay compensation method combining zero‐crossing blocking and full‐line‐cycle feedforward correction is proposed to suppress reverse current and improve input‐current waveform quality. Simulation and experimental results on a 1.6‐kW GaN‐based prototype demonstrate that the proposed method achieves reliable ZVS over the investigated operating range, effectively limits the switching frequency under light‐load conditions, and mitigates the input‐current distortion caused by the ZCD delay.
items.venue: International Journal of Circuit Theory and Applications

items.title: Complete Au-free Metallization Platform for UWBG Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N channel MOS-HEMTs using Ti/Al/Ti Ohmic Contacts and Refractory TiN/Pt Gates
items.abstract: Au-free ohmic contacts and refractory gate stacks are critical for integrating ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) Al-rich AlGaN transistors with Si-CMOS technology. In this work, we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first complete Au-free metallization platform for Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N-channel MOS-HEMTs, combining electron-beam-evaporated and sputtered Ti/Al/Ti ohmic contacts with sputtered TiN and Pt gate metals. The Ti/Al/Ti contacts achieved a contact resistance of approximately 7.5--7.7 $Ω\cdot$mm while being fully Au-free. This contact resistance is achieved using a 600 $^\circ$C anneal, substantially below the 850--950 $^\circ$C typically required for Au-capped Ti/Al/X/Au contacts on Al-rich AlGaN, indicating a reduced thermal budget and improved compatibility with silicon-CMOS foundries. TiN gates deliver drain-current density up to 450 mA/mm at $V_{\mathrm{th}} = -13$ V, whereas Pt gates shift $V_{\mathrm{th}}$ to -2.5 V with a reduced current drive of 220 mA/mm, reflecting the effects of gate work function. TiN-gated devices exhibit lower current degradation under pulsed operation and a higher critical breakdown field ($E_{\mathrm{c}} \approx 3.5$ MV/cm) than Pt-gated devices ($E_{\mathrm{c}} \approx 2.98$ MV/cm), measured without field plating at $L_{\mathrm{GD}} = 2.3$ $μ$m. Collectively, these results establish a low-thermal-budget, fully Au-free, CMOS-compatible metallization platform for high-performance Al-rich AlGaN UWBG power electronics.

items.title: Caerus: Prefetching by Thinking Globally and Acting Locally
items.abstract: Modern processors rely heavily on data prefetching to bridge the growing performance gap between computation and memory accesses. In offset prefetching, prefetches are issued at an address delta relative to the most recently observed access, selecting deltas that have exhibited high coverage in the recent access-stream history. The Best-Offset Prefetcher (BOP) exemplifies this approach by selecting a single uniformly-issued global offset that delivers timely prefetches. However, its lack of context-sensitive accuracy tracking results in significantly increased DRAM traffic and sometimes disappointing performance. Conversely, Berti, the state-of-the-art offset prefetcher, achieves impressive prefetching performance and accuracy. However, its Program-Counter (PC)-local approach to extracting offsets limits its ability to capture global memory patterns, meaning there are many scenarios where simpler global offset prefetchers, such as BOP, outperform it. Observing the limitations of contemporary offset prefetchers, we present Caerus: an offset prefetcher that employs PC-local filtering on multiple non-overlapping globally derived offsets. Caerus extracts multiple offsets from the global memory trace and maximizes their combined coverage by training each offset only on accesses not already covered by previously learned offsets. The accuracy of each extracted offset is tracked per-PC based on whether it can cover future accesses for any PC. This allows Caerus to address complex delta patterns while maintaining high accuracy. In SPECspeed 2017, Caerus gains a geomean speedup of 8.3%, outperforming Berti by 2.0% while achieving low hardware and DRAM-traffic overhead.

items.title: Hardware-Aware Model Inversion in Memristive Spiking Neural Networks
items.abstract: Hardware-accelerated spiking neural networks (SNNs) implemented on memristive crossbar arrays offer significant gains in energy efficiency, while device variability and analog noise are sometimes assumed to hinder information extraction. However, whether these hardware effects improve, preserve, or degrade privacy after deployment remains largely unexplored. Therefore, we ask whether model-inversion leakage characterized on an SNN remains representative after the same model is mapped to a non-ideal memristive substrate, and how hardware non-idealities and reliability faults affecting synapses, neuron thresholds, and spike processing reshape that leakage. To study this problem, we introduce Spiking Domain Model Inversion (SDMI), an inversion method that combines Expectation over Transformation (EOT) with surrogate gradients to optimize inputs through stochastic analog behavior and non-differentiable spiking dynamics. We use SDMI consistently across the SNN model, its memristive SNN, and the same memristive SNN under additional hardware perturbations. Across four datasets, reconstruction leakage does not vary monotonically with model accuracy or hardware variability. At comparable accuracy levels, neuron-threshold perturbations increase reconstruction fidelity, measured by SSIM, by up to 51.8%, whereas spike-level perturbations primarily degrade utility without consistently improving reconstruction. Weight noise, in contrast, reduces leakage under the same inversion procedure. These results show that hardware variability is not inherently privacy-preserving: model inversion leakage in memristive SNNs depends on the hardware state and cannot be inferred from model accuracy alone.

items.title: Non-Volatile Memory Devices for Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: This chapter explores the critical role of emerging non-volatile memory (eNVM) devices in advancing neuromorphic computing. Inspired by the human brain's remarkable ability to perform complex tasks like pattern recognition and adaptation, neuromorphic computing offers immense potential for implementing complex neural networks (NNs) in real hardware. Despite ongoing research into the brain's complexities, its fundamental operation relies on neurons (processing units communicating via electrochemical signals) and synapses (junctions between neurons). The modifiable strength of the synapse is key to learning and memory functionality, allowing the brain to adapt and rewire itself. For dense and low-power circuits in neuromorphic computing, these eNVM devices are ideal due to their synaptic-like behavior and non-volatile information storage. Properties such as conductance modulation of these devices emulate synaptic plasticity, which is crucial for learning, and their scalability makes them promising for large-scale neuromorphic architectures. This chapter will delve into the various types of eNVM devices such as resistive RAM (ReRAM), phase-change memory (PCM), spintronics-based memory devices, and their applications in neuromorphic computing, discussing their challenges and opportunities, and highlighting recent advances in their integration within neuromorphic systems.

items.title: APPlace: Co-Optimizing Device Locations and Access Points for Routing-Aware Analog Placement
items.abstract: Analog layout automation remains challenging in Analog/Mixed-Signal circuit design, because parasitics and mismatches introduced during layout strongly affect circuit performance. Placement is especially critical among the layout stages, as it constrains the routing solution space and the achievable post-layout performance. Existing analytical placement methods optimize device coordinates under center-based wirelength proxies and leave access point (AP) selection to routing. In analog circuits, however, a routing pin is an extended piece of terminal metal rather than a fixed point, and the best AP on it depends on where the other connected devices are placed, so a coordinate-only placement optimizes for connection points that the router will not use. We present APPlace, a routing-aware analog placement framework that co-optimizes device locations and AP selections during global placement, followed by a legalization stage that preserves the structure established by global placement. Experimental results on four real-world analog benchmarks show that APPlace achieves better overall post-layout performance than representative baselines at comparable layout area. Ablation studies further show that removing AP co-optimization causes up to a 13 dB CMRR loss among the OTA benchmarks and a 23% increase in comparator delay.

items.title: Energy-Efficient Memristor Accelerator for Depression Detection with a CNN-LSTM Hybrid Model
items.abstract: Early screening of depression requires efficient analysis of audio and speech data, while conventional CPU and GPU platforms incur high latency and energy consumption for CNN-LSTM inference. To address this challenge, we propose a unified resistive RAM (ReRAM) processing-in-memory accelerator for a CNN-LSTM attention workload. The architecture integrates convolutional, recurrent, attention, and multi-layer perceptron (MLP) stages within a crossbar-based framework, reducing intermediate data movement between spatial and temporal branches. CNN operations are mapped through im2col-based vectorization, while LSTM gate computations are reformulated using concatenated input-state vectors and mapped onto ReRAM crossbars. We further provide module-level workload breakdown, parameter sensitivity analysis, and matched-workload context against representative ReRAM/PIM accelerators. Experimental results show 32.1 times and 9.3 times latency reduction over CPU and GPU baselines, respectively, with about 160 times and 140 times energy reduction. Simplified weight-perturbation tests characterize ASLF sensitivity in an untrained pipeline with synthetic spectrogram-shaped inputs. Task-level prediction accuracy and robustness remain to be evaluated.

items.title: Characterizing Performance Tradeoffs in Heterogeneous GPU-Wafer-Scale Accelerator Systems
items.abstract: As AI accelerator architectures become increasingly diverse, integrating different architectures into a unified system is emerging as a new heterogeneous computing paradigm. GPUs and WSEs differ substantially in compute, memory, and communication organization, creating both architectural complementarity and additional overheads, yet how to translate this heterogeneity into practical performance gains remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose a hierarchical benchmarking methodology to characterize GPU--WSE heterogeneous execution and the conditions for exploiting complementarity, together with an analytical performance model that identifies when heterogeneity becomes a bottleneck and when it yields system-level performance gains.

items.title: TiN Stepwise Etch for CFET Replacement Metal Gate Module
items.abstract: A TiN digital stepwise etch process is reported that could significantly simplify the monolithic Complementary Field Effect Transistor (mCFET) flow within the Replacement Metal Gate (RMG) Module. The process consists of repeated cycles of controlled TiN oxidation followed by selective oxide dissolution step. Various chemistries were screened for enabling controlled and selective TiN recess. Furthermore, we demonstrate that TiN cyclic etch does not damage the seam in between the nanoSheet (NS) in the CFET patterned structures.
items.venue: Diffusion and defect data, solid state data. Part B, Solid state phenomena/Solid state phenomena

items.title: Test Vehicle and Metrology for Defectivity Study in Wet Processes
items.abstract: Controlling defectivity is critical for achieving high yield and performance in advanced CMOS fabrication. Wet processing presents key challenges such as pattern collapse, non-uniform etching, and incomplete cleaning in high-aspect-ratio (HAR) structures. To effectively optimize single-wafer wet process conditions with good across-wafer uniformity, well-designed test vehicles and advanced metrology are indispensable. This paper provides an overview of 300 mm patterned wafer test vehicles, as well as recent developments in advanced metrologies. Together, they offer a robust framework for quantitatively assessing process performance, thereby enabling more efficient and reliable single-wafer processing.
items.venue: Diffusion and defect data, solid state data. Part B, Solid state phenomena/Solid state phenomena

items.title: Si Thinning in Alkaline Solutions for 3DDRAM Applications
items.abstract: This work investigates silicon (Si) thinning by wet alkaline etching to enable vertical bit lines (VBL) and monocrystalline silicon Gate-All-Around (GAA) architectures for 3D DRAM integration. Two etchants—tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAH) and ammonium hydroxide (NH₄OH)—were systematically studied. Process screening was initially performed on blanket Si to identify conditions offering controlled etch rates and low surface roughness. Optimal conditions were then applied to wagon wheels and 3D patterned test structures, revealing strong anisotropic behaviour influenced by Si crystallography. To mitigate this directional dependence, wafers with a 45° notch rotation were explored to align vertical sidewalls along the orientation, promoting isotropic etching in the desired directions. In TMAH, rotated wafers initially exhibited suppressed lateral etch rates, but prolonged etching exposed fast-etching planes, leading to undesired lateral etching. NH₄OH demonstrated a similar evolution, though boron-doped Si showed partial etch-stop behaviour and increased surface roughness. Blanket etch tests on epitaxially grown boron-doped Si further corroborated these observations. These insights provide critical guidance for integrating scalable GAA devices in next-generation 3D-DRAM architectures.
items.venue: Diffusion and defect data, solid state data. Part B, Solid state phenomena/Solid state phenomena

items.title: NORmal: Architecting 3D Ferroelectric NOR Flash as Main Memory -- From Co-Fabricated BEOL Arrays to 200B-Class Multi-Agent LLMs in a Smartphone
items.abstract: Smartphone agents increasingly work as teams, in which a large planner directs parallel workers across long sessions. Running such a team on the device requires 200B-class models and contexts that exceed phone DRAM many times over, yet existing tiers treat flash as storage: UFS starves per-token weight streaming, and mobile High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) needs a redesigned SoC and cannot absorb continuous KV writes. We show that a non-volatile memory can join an unmodified LPDDR6 bus as a plain rank only if its access latency fits the DRAM timing window, a condition no NAND tier meets. We present NORmal, to our knowledge the first main-memory architecture for 3D ferroelectric NOR flash. We have fabricated and experimentally characterized back-end-of-line (BEOL) 3D FeNOR arrays that co-integrate dense 3-bit MLC and fast, high-endurance in-place-writable SLC with sub-7.5 ns sensing. NORmal turns these co-fabricated arrays into a byte-addressable, deterministic-timing load/store rank on an unmodified LPDDR6 interface through an under-array DRAM-emulation bridge, staggered bank reads with zero-cycle weight swizzling, and posted SLC writes. Across this rank and DRAM, NORmal places agent state by mutability and lifetime rather than by hotness, serving 200B-class models and persistent planner contexts in place while dynamically partitioning subchannels across agent phases. In serving-level simulation on production agent traces, NORmal is 8.9$\times$--28.0$\times$ faster than UFS offloading, within 0.4% of an unlimited-DRAM ideal, and 2.8$\times$--6.3$\times$ faster than HBF on sessions beyond 256K tokens, with 8.1$\times$--17.8$\times$ less memory energy per token.

items.title: Machine-learning-based 3D sidewall reconstruction of line/space patterns from 2D SEM images
items.abstract: Critical-dimension scanning electron microscopy (CD-SEM) is a fast metrology tool for pattern features, but a top-down SEM image remains a two-dimensional view of a three-dimensional sidewall morphology. We present a virtual-metrology workflow that links Monte Carlo-based SEM image simulation with convolutional neural network (CNN) regression to recover 3D sidewall roughness descriptors directly from image data. Synthetic resist line/space patterns with controllable roughness are generated from Fourier-filtered stochastic fields parameterized by RMS and ξ, rendered into realistic Monte Carlo-based SEM images with Nebula, and sampled with Latin Hypercube Sampling over the experimental EUV line/space geometry. The sampled ranges are chosen to cover representative EUV line/space pattern metrics. A validation-optimized stacked ensemble of ResNet CNN regressors predicts RMS and ξ from the image inputs. On a held-out test set of 75 samples, the ensemble achieves R2 = 0.936 for RMS and R2 = 0.902 for ξ. Applied to the SEM image, it predicts (0.547nm, 9.060nm), showing that Monte Carlo-based CNN inference can estimate key 3D sidewall roughness descriptors directly from top-down SEM images.

items.title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
items.abstract: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. Layered bismuth oxychalcogenides, Bi2O2X (X = S, Se, Te), are mixed-anion crystals whose covalent slabs and ionic sheets are bound electrostatically rather than by van der Waals forces and whose Bi3+ 6s^2 lone pairs can become stereochemically active. Despite the rapid development of Bi2O2Se for fin and gate-all-around transistors, its fundamental thermal expansion and heat transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that lone-pair stereoactivity, not chalcogen mass, governs both properties. Path-integral molecular dynamics shows that the volumetric thermal expansion coefficient at 300 K decreases from 8.14 x 10^-5 K^-1 in Bi2O2S to 6.72 x 10^-5 and 6.61 x 10^-5 K^-1 in Bi2O2Se and Bi2O2Te, respectively, despite a 13% larger unit cell in the telluride, whereas substituting the S mass into Bi2O2Se changes its value by only 0.6%. Lone-pair-driven Bi off-centering in orthorhombic Bi2O2S makes b-axis expansion 1.63 times a-axis expansion yet leaves in-plane thermal conduction isotropic within 3%. Phonon transport calculations including four-phonon scattering and Wigner coherence predict a thermal conductivity maximum in Bi2O2Se (1.83 and 0.95 W m^-1 K^-1 in the in-plane and cross-plane directions, respectively, at 300 K) because Bi2O2S is limited by anharmonic scattering and Bi2O2Te by slow cross-plane phonons. Thermoreflectance measurements from 300 to 500 K and in situ X-ray diffraction on Bi2O2Se single crystals agree with these predictions within 6.4%. Phonon Boltzmann transport simulations of 12-nm-wide fins, which run hotter than Fourier diffusion predicts, show that Bi2O2Se minimizes the hotspot temperature and the thermal-mismatch strain at the gate dielectric.

items.title: Enhancing SiOx Protection during SiGe Selective Wet Etch in CFET Integration Using Oxide Surface Functionalization
items.abstract: This work describes the OSF concept (Oxide Surface Functionalization) as being a pre-treatment before a wet SiGe removal within the CFET integration. The SiGe is removed with an HF_H₂O₂ formulated chemistry that induces some oxide loss in the CFET structures (hard mask and STI). The OSF consists in a selective coating that occurs on the oxide surfaces and not on the SiGe surfaces that need to be removed. The selective coating prevents the oxide surface of being significantly etched during the wet SiGe removal.
items.venue: Diffusion and defect data, solid state data. Part B, Solid state phenomena/Solid state phenomena

items.title: Enhanced SiGe/Si Selective Etching by Acetic Acid in HNA Solutions
items.abstract: Selective SiGe etching process is crucial for the fabrication of Gate-all-around field-effect transistors (GAAFET) and three-dimensional dynamic random access memory (3D-DRAM). A mixture of HF, HNO 3 , and CH 3 COOH (HNA solution) is the etchant traditionally used to etch Si, but can also be used to etch SiGe. The effect of adding various concentrations of CH 3 COOH to HF/HNO 3 solutions on the selective etching of SiGe over Si was investigated in this study. It was found that addition of CH 3 COOH can enhance the selective etching of SiGe over Si, while an excessive amount causes etching of Si. In addition, concentration optimization of HNA solution was conducted to further increase the etching selectivity of SiGe over Si.
items.venue: Diffusion and defect data, solid state data. Part B, Solid state phenomena/Solid state phenomena

items.title: Comparative analysis of gate-dielectric effects on the analog and linearity performance of MoS2-, MoSe2-, and WS2-based FETs
items.abstract: Abstract This work investigates the influence of gate dielectric engineering on the analog, RF, and linearity performance of transition metal dichalcogenide field-effect transistors (TMD-FETs). A self-consistent non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF)-based simulation framework is employed to analyze MoS 2 -, MoSe 2 -, and WS₂-based FETs integrated with different high-k gate dielectrics. The impact of dielectric materials on electrostatic integrity, carrier transport, transistor efficiency ( g m / I D ), quality factor (Q-factor), and RF linearity metrics is systematically examined. Key device parameters including ON current ( I ON ), OFF current ( I OFF ), current ON/OFF ratio ( I ON / I OFF ), subthreshold swing (SS), transconductance ( g m ), second-order transconductance ( g m2 ), and third-order transconductance ( g m3 ) are evaluated. The results demonstrate that high-k dielectrics significantly enhance gate electrostatic control, resulting in improved ON-state current, reduced SS, enhanced g m / I D efficiency, and superior Q-factor characteristics. Furthermore, the use of high-k dielectrics shifts the peaks of g m2 and g m3 toward lower gate voltages, indicating improved low-voltage RF linearity behavior. Among the investigated materials, WS₂-based FETs exhibit superior transconductance and RF performance characteristics, while MoS 2 -based devices provide an excellent trade-off between power efficiency, nonlinear distortion behavior, and analog/RF characteristics. The findings offer essential insights for optimizing dielectric–channel combinations in next-generation low-power, high-linearity, and RF-oriented nanoelectronic devices.

items.title: CFET RMG Dual Work Function Metal Patterning with Sacrificial Layer for Nanosheets Pinch-Off
items.abstract: We reported the process flow and challenges of dual work function metal patterning between different work function metal thicknesses and gate lengths to monolithic Complementary FET. To resolve the dilemma of spin-on-carbon hard mask fill and nanosheet pinch-off, we propose integrating sacrificial gap-closure layers and isotropic etches to dual work function metal patterning. We prove that the sacrificial layers can be removed with high selectivity to work function metal in wet etch chemistry. We report the controllable wet etch rate of the sacrificial layers by concentrations and temperatures. Finally, we first demonstrate dual work function metal patterning with a sacrificial layer and isotropic etch step by step on a monolithic Complementary FET test vehicle.
items.venue: Diffusion and defect data, solid state data. Part B, Solid state phenomena/Solid state phenomena

items.title: Analysis of Si/SiGe Intermixing Layer Thickness by Inductively Coupled Plasma – Mass Spectrometry
items.abstract: A new method for characterizing the intermixing layer between epitaxially deposited Si and SiGe based on the atomic scale wet etch combined with Inductively Coupled Plasma – Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS). The thermally induced Ge and Si interdiffusion is considered as one of the root causes for the poor process control and undesired cavity profile after etch, which, in turn, may significantly impact the device performance. The developed ICP-MS method allows us to analyze the thickness of the Si/SiGe intermixing layer and the Ge concentration profile, which can help to improve the upstream processes.
items.venue: Diffusion and defect data, solid state data. Part B, Solid state phenomena/Solid state phenomena

items.title: Uniaxial strain tuning of functional properties in antiferroelectric PbZrO3 membrane capacitors
items.abstract: Lead zirconate (PbZrO3, PZO) is a prototypical antiferroelectric (AFE) system promising for applications such as energy storage and neuromorphic computing. However, in conventional thin-film architectures, its functional potential is often limited by substrate clamping. Although emerging freestanding membrane techniques offer an approach to release this clamping and enable dynamic strain engineering, a systematic understanding of how external strain modulates the switching between AFE and ferroelectric (FE) states is missing. In this study, we investigate the uniaxial strain effects on PZO membrane capacitors transferred onto flexible substrates via a gold-bonding method. We demonstrate that in-plane dynamic strain modulates the AFE-FE switching and functional properties. Corroborated by atomistic simulations, we reveal that the strain-dependent evolution arises from the superposition of the intrinsic strain dependence of specific domain orientation variants and extrinsic strain-induced redistribution of the relative population of different domain variants. These findings provide a predictive understanding of uniaxial strain tuning of AFE-FE switching in PZO, and pave the way for exploiting the functional potential of freestanding antiferroelectric membranes.

items.title: A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator
items.abstract: Frontier large language models write correct CUDA kernels for most single-operator benchmark tasks, yet their accuracy collapses on accelerators whose architecture and programming language they have rarely seen. We present a case study of an LLM agent loop built for such accelerators. Our example is the FuriosaAI RNGD NPU, programmed in a recent, sparsely documented Rust DSL, where the loop optimized three Gemma-4-12B decode kernels over 12 days on a shared, scarce device. The loop builds its own target knowledge: it writes and checks a summary of the DSL documentation, measures the chip with microbenchmarks, records compiler-derived legality rules, and revisits this knowledge when the toolchain changes, rechecking rules and measurements where it can. A role-based search over per-kernel Design Trees explores whole-kernel designs and accumulates small accepted changes in the best version of each kernel. Because device time is scarce and readings are noisy, cheap checks screen new designs before any device run, and late in the run a change was accepted only after repeated comparisons with the best kernel on the device. The final kernels reach a 9.293x geomean speedup over the official baseline, each within 1.25x of the cycles needed just to move its weights. Our prompts, profiler and acceptance test are available at https://github.com/bgchun-fs/multi-agent-kernel-gen-loop.

items.title: Rosemary: Efficient and Adaptable In-Storage Acceleration for Fully Homomorphic Encryption
items.abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables computation on encrypted data and is promising for privacy-preserving computing. However, FHE deployment remains constrained due to massive computational, memory, and data-movement overheads. Existing acceleration strategies often overlook the storage I/O bottleneck caused by the enormous size of FHE data in large-scale applications, as most prior works focus on small benchmarks that fit in main memory. Our studies show that state-of-the-art FHE systems spend 71\% to 85\% of their execution time moving data between storage and compute units rather than performing useful computation. To address the I/O bottleneck, we present Rosemary, a heterogeneous FHE acceleration system that incorporates a novel in-storage processing (ISP) architecture with compiler-level and algorithmic optimizations. Our key innovations include 1) an adaptable hardware-aware FHE engine inside a NAND flash-based solid-state drive (SSD) for efficient and cost-effective in-storage FHE processing, 2) a Throughput-Data-Aware Program Allocator (TDAP) that partitions FHE workloads into heterogeneous programs, and 3) a Compiler-Level Ciphertext-Aware Optimizer (CLCAO) that exploits ISP-friendly FHE kernels for low-cost ISP execution. Across a diverse set of FHE workloads, including encrypted deep learning inference and cloud database queries, Rosemary achieves geometric-mean speedups of $185.7\times$ over state-of-the-art CPU/GPU implementations and $3.7\times$ over prior FHE accelerators, while improving energy efficiency by up to $3.9\times$ and Energy-Delay-Area-Product (EDAP) by up to $16.5\times$.

items.title: Exceptionally Matched p-SiNW/n-IGZO Complementary Field-Effect Transistors for Monolithic 3D Logic
items.abstract: Abstract Monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) provide a route toward a higher logic density by vertically stacking complementary devices within the same footprint. Their realization through heterogeneous integration requires p- and n-channel transistors that are both individually high-performing and electrically matched. Here, we demonstrate high-performance heterogeneous Si/oxide M3D CFETs by vertically integrating p-type silicon nanowire (p-SiNW) FETs with n-type indium gallium zinc oxide (n-IGZO) transistors. The site-controlled p-SiNWs are formed through a scalable in-plane solid–liquid–solid (IPSLS) process without postgrowth hydrogen passivation, facilitating subsequent oxide–semiconductor integration. The vertically integrated p- and n-channel devices exhibit closely matched current-driving capabilities, near-zero threshold voltages, and subthreshold swings of 120 and 133 mV dec–1, respectively. This exceptional p/n matching enables sharp and well-balanced switching, yielding a peak voltage gain of 103 V/V at VDD = 5 V, a normalized gain of 20.6 V–1, and large, nearly symmetric noise margins (NML = 0.45 VDD and NMH = 0.44 VDD). The architecture is further extended to NOR, NAND, and OR gates with experimentally verified logic operations. These results establish a high-performance heterogeneous Si/oxide integration platform for dense and robust M3D complementary logic.

items.title: SLICE-CiM: Selective Layer-wise Inference Control Engine with Confidence-Based Early Exit for SRAM based Digital Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Digital SRAM compute-in-memory (CIM) macros enable energy-efficient CNN inference by eliminating off-chip weight transfers; however, peripheral control logic introduces three inefficiencies: bit- slice over-activation at reduced precision (L1), unnecessary accumula- tion depth (L2), and idle precision-transition stalls (L3). To address these, we present four synthesizable peripheral blocks: a Flush-Merge Enable (FME) controller, a Confidence-Based Early-Exit (EE) module, a Precision Register with Decoder (PR/PD), and a Bit-Serial Cycle Controller (CC), co-designed to minimize switching activity, wordline overhead, and leakage. Implemented in TSMC 65-nm CMOS at 335 MHz, the peripheral framework occupies 1769.760 μm2 post-synthesis and 1982.131 μm2 post-PnR. Gate-level VCD analysis reports 6.0706 μW leakage and 288.2902 μW (post-synthesis) / 322.8850 μW (post-PnR) dynamic power, totaling 328.9556 μW (0.2402% of system power). The EE module dominates dynamic power (58.2%), while WLG dominates area (58.1%). System evaluation on MobileNetV2 (CIFAR-100) shows efficiency scaling from 31.35 TOPS/W (8b/8b, 1.2 V) to 454.91 TOPS/W (2b/8b, 0.8 V), achieving 13.33x improvement without bitcell modification or retraining. The framework targets CNN workloads exploiting sparsity, with Transformer extension as future work.

items.title: Prospector: learning a compact graph traversal policy for scientific reasoning
items.abstract: Scientific reasoning in specialized engineering fields depends on knowledge scattered across the literature, often proprietary and absent from frontier LLM training data. In such domains, frontier models tend to give generic answers. Knowledge graphs (KGs) can ground LLM reasoning. Because a graph is too large to provide in full, typical LLM+KG systems preselect a portion, deciding relevance before reasoning begins. Here we train a compact model, Prospector, to reason over a domain knowledge graph by traversing it step by step, seeking evidence in light of what it has already found. Prospector calls a small set of tools one at a time to progressively build its context, and answers with a chain of evidence that can be checked edge by edge against what its tools retrieved from the graph. On a knowledge graph built from the semiconductor-manufacturing literature, Prospector approaches the strongest off-the-shelf models given the same graph and tools, and it far exceeds off-the-shelf models answering closed-book or from a pre-selected portion of the graph. Although trained only on the semiconductor graph, Prospector transfers to unseen knowledge graphs from three other distinct fields: bio-inspired materials, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and materials properties. Served on a single GPU, Prospector answers faster and at a fraction of the cost of a hosted service, while keeping proprietary data on the owner's hardware. We find that the policy's latent state is indicative of its next move on both seen and unseen graphs, and modulating the latent state can steer the policy from one behavior mode to another. These results suggest a practical LLM + KG paradigm for scientific and engineering reasoning over private data, in which a compact model trained on a graph from published literature transfers its traversal to unseen graphs that stay with their owners.

items.title: p-DCIM: A 28nm Probabilistic SRAM DCIM based Ising Machine for Near-Memory Context Selection in LLM-RAG Pipeline
items.abstract: We present a fabricated SRAM DCIM Ising machine that performs set-level context selection for large language model (LLM) with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). In RAG, the evidence-selection stage is increasingly delegated to repeated language-model reranking, which adds substantial energy to the inference pipeline. We reformulate evidence selection as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problem and solve it on a dual-mode digital compute-in-memory (DCIM) macro: the same multiply-and-accumulate datapath computes the embedding-similarity scores that populate the QUBO coefficients and evaluates the per-spin Hamiltonian differences that drive the anneal. The annealing temperature is set by a digital plane-count control along with the SRAM pseudo-read random bit flips, giving graded cooling entirely from on-chip digital configuration. The macro is taped-out in a 28 nm process [0.16 mm2, 0.41 mW] and is proposed to be integrated as part of the logic base-die in hybrid high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and high-bandwidth flash (HBF) stacks in a GPU package, where only the selected passage identifiers return to the host. Replacing the language-model selection pass with the near-memory Ising solver yields a macro normalized selection-energy estimate more than six orders of magnitude lower than the LLM-based baseline and reduces the evaluated total energy per query by 67%, while maintaining comparable token-level F1 on the evaluated examples.

items.title: Demonstration of high output power (3.75 W/mm) with 31.8% PAE in Ga-Polar AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on sapphire at 94 GHz
items.abstract: In this work, a recessed-gate Ga-polar AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) on sapphire incorporating an AlGaN back-barrier for W-band operation is demonstrated. The device achieves a subthreshold slope of ~130 mV/dec, a peak transconductance of 0.75 S/mm, and an fmax exceeding 240 GHz. Continuous-wave load-pull measurements at 94 GHz show an output power of 3.75 W/mm with a power-added efficiency of 31.8%. This performance significantly exceeds the best previously reported Ga-polar devices on sapphire and approaches that of state-of-the-art Ga-polar devices on SiC, which provides a promising pathway toward high-performance W-band devices.

items.title: Valley Hall viscosity in gapped graphene with and without a magnetic field
items.abstract: Hall viscosity is conventionally defined through the stress response to time-dependent strain, a perturbation that is difficult to implement in solid-state experiments. We formulate a related viscoelastic response to static, spatially inhomogeneous electric fields and compare it with the strain-based response. For gapped graphene in a perpendicular magnetic field, the two formulations give the same Landau-level response, whose Hall viscosity is asymmetric between the two valleys. At zero magnetic field, a valley-even quantum-metric coefficient combines with the valley-odd Hall conductivity to produce equal and opposite valley-resolved responses; global time-reversal symmetry therefore forces the net Hall viscosity to vanish. In an insulating state, exact particle--hole symmetry eliminates this zero-field response, whereas particle--hole-symmetry breaking generates a cutoff-dependent geometric contribution from the occupied Fermi sea. These results connect valley-dependent viscoelasticity with electromagnetic response in gapped Dirac materials and clarify the conditions under which a valley Hall viscosity can arise.

items.title: Processing-Tuned Laser-Induced Graphene Transducers for Polyaniline pH Sensors
items.abstract: Abstract Flexible pH sensors are important for wearable, biomedical, environmental, and process-monitoring applications, but achieving simple, scalable fabrication while maintaining high sensing performance remains challenging. Laser-induced graphene (LIG) has emerged as a promising transducer material because it enables direct laser patterning of porous, conductive graphitized carbon electrodes on flexible substrates. Although laser-processing conditions are known to affect LIG morphology, graphitization, and electrical properties, their influence on pH-sensitive layer formation and pH-sensing performance has not been systematically investigated. In this study, polyaniline (PANi)-modified LIG pH sensors were fabricated using four laser-processing combinations of laser power and scan speed. The resulting LIG and PANi/LIG electrodes were characterized using sheet-resistance measurements, optical microscopy, SEM, Raman spectroscopy, and XPS. PANi was electropolymerized on the LIG working electrodes under identical cyclic voltammetry conditions, and the assembled sensors were evaluated in pH 4–9 buffer solutions. The results showed that laser processing produced distinct LIG morphologies, porosities, sheet resistance, and PANi coverage, leading to different sensing performances. Among the samples, PANi/LIG-9.2–350, fabricated at 9.2 W and 350 mm/s, exhibited the best overall performance, with a near-Nernstian sensitivity of −60.04 mV/pH, a 12 h drift rate of 1.67 mV/h, hysteresis of 2.06 mV, and rapid response time of 13.2 s. These findings emphasize the significance of laser-processing-dependent LIG microstructure and electrical properties in governing PANi deposition behavior and resulting potentiometric pH-sensing performance.
